# Morph2Mol: A Foundation Model for Predicting Single-Cell Spatial Transcriptome from Histology Images

Predict spatial single-cell gene expression from H&E images using an image encoder, a spatial decoder, and a reference bank of cells with measured expression.

## Resources

- **Website:** [Morph2Mol portal](https://morph2mol.vercel.app/)
- **Online inference:** [Hugging Face Space](https://huggingface.co/spaces/zchx/Morph2Mol-demo)

- **Model:** [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/zchx/Morph2Mol)
- **Paper:** [arXiv:2608.08366](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.08366)

## Installation

Use Python 3.10 or later and install a PyTorch build suitable for your hardware.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/zchxhcz1/Morph2Mol.git
cd Morph2Mol
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

For SVS, NDPI, or MRXS images, install the OpenSlide system library and `openslide-python`. PNG, JPEG, and TIFF images are also supported. Large slide images should use an OpenSlide-readable format to avoid loading the entire image into memory.

## Download the model

Download the checkpoints, fusion weights, gene information, and reference bank from Hugging Face. UNI2-h requires separate access through [MahmoodLab/UNI2-h](https://huggingface.co/MahmoodLab/UNI2-h).

After receiving UNI2-h access, authenticate with your own Hugging Face account:

```bash
hf auth login
python - <<'PYTHON'
from huggingface_hub import snapshot_download, hf_hub_download

model_dir = "models/morph2mol"
snapshot_download("zchx/Morph2Mol", local_dir=model_dir)
hf_hub_download("MahmoodLab/UNI2-h", "pytorch_model.bin", local_dir=f"{model_dir}/uni2h")
PYTHON
```

See [model files](weights/README.md) for the directory structure.

## Prediction

Choose your own model, image and output locations in the commands below. Run prediction from a single H&E image:

```bash
python predict/predict.py \
  --image /path/to/slide.svs \
  --release models/morph2mol \
  --out results/prediction.h5ad
```

The command segments nuclei, extracts cell-centered image crops, predicts expression, retrieves reference expression, and combines both predictions. It also saves the segmentation beside the output. The model download includes the fusion weights and reference bank used by this command. The first segmentation run downloads the Cellpose model; use `--segment-model` to provide local segmentation weights.

Spatial prediction uses up to 128 target cells and 64 neighboring context cells per block, with context selected within 137 µm. All cells in the block participate in attention; only target predictions are saved. Every cell is output once. Partitioning is deterministic for a given sample ID and fixed seed.

If the image does not contain physical resolution metadata, supply its actual microns per pixel:

```bash
python predict/predict.py --image /path/to/image.png --mpp 0.25 \
  --release models/morph2mol --out results/prediction.h5ad
```

`0.25` is an example. Use the resolution of your image. Prediction requires no measured expression or precomputed image features for the target slide.

| Option | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `--cells cells.npz` | Use existing cell boundaries instead of automatic segmentation |
| `--prepared /path/to/slide` | Read prepared cell crops and boundaries instead of `--image` |
| `--tissue lung/wide` | Select organ and panel-width fusion weights; `--tissue lung` selects width automatically |
| `--genes all` | Predict all 18,580 model genes; this is the default |
| `--genes genes.txt` | Predict an ordered list of gene symbols, one per line |
| `--save-embeddings` | Save image and spatial features |
| `--workers 4` | Set CPU workers for loading cell crops |
| `--enc-chunk 32 --query-batch 64` | Reduce transient GPU memory use |
| `--sample-id SAMPLE --exclude RELATED_SAMPLE` | Exclude the target and related references when they occur in the bank |

CUDA is the default device. CPU inference is available with `--device cpu --amp fp32`. Prediction matrices are written to disk in batches; output size scales with the number of cells and requested genes. Automatic segmentation produces nuclei; use supplied cell boundaries when available.

## Fusion weights

Fusion weights cover all 15 reference organs: bone, brain, breast, cervix, colon, heart, kidney, liver, lung, lymph_node, ovary, pancreas, prostate, skin and tonsil. The [model repository](https://huggingface.co/zchx/Morph2Mol#fusion-weights) lists all 20 available organ/panel groups, including groups with one reference slide. Fitting retrieves from the other reference slides across tissues, excluding the query reference and its related donor/block samples.

Groups use organ names such as `lung/narrow` and `lung/wide`. `narrow` means fewer than 1,000 measured model genes in the fitting reference; `wide` means at least 1,000. With an organ alone, width is selected from the number of requested output genes. Supply an explicit group to keep that choice fixed when changing the requested gene subset. A missing width uses another available width of the same organ; an omitted or unknown organ uses global weights.

The model download includes the combined `beta.json` used automatically during prediction. Individual gene-weight tables are also available under `beta/ORGAN/WIDTH.json`. Global weights are fitted across the full reference set independently of organ grouping. No target expression is needed.

## Output

```python
import anndata as ad
prediction = ad.read_h5ad("results/prediction.h5ad")
```

| Field | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `X` | Combined gene-expression scores |
| `layers['A']` | Direct predictions in `log1p(mu)` scale |
| `layers['R']` | Reference expression scores; NaN where reference coverage is unavailable |
| `var['beta']` | Applied fusion weight for each gene |
| `var['covered']` | Reference coverage for each gene |
| `obsm['spatial']` | Cell centroids as x,y coordinates in source-image pixels |
| `obsm['X_morph2mol_stage2']` | Stage 2 image embeddings, with `--save-embeddings` |
| `obsm['X_morph2mol_se2']` | Spatial decoder embeddings, with `--save-embeddings` |
| `obsm['X_morph2mol_phase1']` | Stage 1 retrieval embeddings, with `--save-embeddings` |

The combined score is `beta * A + (1 - beta) * R`. Genes without reference coverage or fitted weights use the direct prediction. Combined scores describe variation across cells within each gene; they are not molecule counts.

## Training

[Training instructions](docs/training.md) cover RNA embedding preparation, image–RNA alignment, expression training, reference-bank construction, and fitting fusion weights. Training requires paired H&E images and measured spatial expression.

[Input formats](docs/formats.md) describe image geometry, prepared-slide files, reference-bank inputs, and output coordinates.

## 是什么

Comparative SAE Atlas 是一个跨模型比较分析框架，用于在相同的 6,000 个 Tabula Sapiens 细胞上运行十个单细胞基础模型，并通过每层一个稀疏自编码器（SAE）打开模型内部表示，以统一校准的注释方法进行比较。它旨在回答：每个模型编码了什么、它们共享什么、针对特定任务该用哪个模型，以及模型特征是否能预测模型从未见过的生物学。该仓库包含一个交互式在线图谱（`index.html`）、完整的分析流水线（GPU 提取和本地分析）以及所有结果文件，并附有严格的审计机制。

## 亮点

- **统一比较框架**：在相同细胞和相同 SAE 配置下运行十个模型，消除了数据或方法差异，使比较公平且可复现。
- **严格的统计控制**：每个结论都配有对应的零模型（如随机基因、度匹配随机基因、细胞置换），并报告失败的对照，确保结论的可靠性。
- **可审计性**：所有数字都从结果文件读取，并有 `audit_all.py` 进行 312 项检查，覆盖论文、补充材料、图表和网站，确保可追溯。
- **跨模型可扩展性**：通过适配器（adapters）支持不同架构（如 MLM、自回归、基于文本的模型），并处理了不同输入编码（如 binning、rank order、ESM2 token）。
- **资源管理**：GPU 阶段和本地分析分离，支持在 H100 上运行大型模型，同时本地分析仅需 CPU 和 NumPy，降低了复现门槛。

## 为何对本课题有用

本仓库直接针对【虚拟细胞/虚拟器官 × 单细胞/空间组学 × 生物基座模型、生物大语言模型、Bio Agent】方向，提供了以下关键价值：

- **模型评估与选择**：对于构建虚拟细胞或生物基座模型，该框架提供了一种系统方法，评估不同模型（如 scGPT、Geneformer、UCE 等）在编码生物学概念上的能力，帮助选择最适合特定任务的模型。
- **可解释性方法**：通过 SAE 和校准注释，揭示了模型内部特征与生物学通路（如蛋白质合成、抗原呈递）的对应关系，这对于理解生物大语言模型的“黑箱”至关重要，可迁移到虚拟器官建模中。
- **零模型方法论**：其严格的统计控制（如随机基因、度匹配零模型）为验证生物基座模型预测的显著性提供了模板，避免虚假发现，这在 Bio Agent 的决策中尤为重要。
- **跨模型比较**：对于多模型集成或模型融合的虚拟细胞系统，该框架提供了比较不同模型表示空间的工具（如 CKA、SAE 方差解释），可指导模型集成策略。
- **数据与代码复用**：提供了完整的流水线（如 `coexpression_baseline`、`trrust_robustness`），可直接用于评估新模型或新数据集，加速课题研究。

## 怎么用

- **安装与依赖**：本地分析环境使用 `requirements.txt`（Python 3.13, NumPy 2.3.4, SciPy, h5py, anndata, matplotlib）；GPU 提取环境使用 `pipeline/atlas_h100/environment.yml`（Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.13, CUDA 13, 需 H100）。
- **主入口**：
  - 本地分析：`pipeline/scripts/` 下的脚本，如 `audit_all.py`（运行 312 项审计）、`inject_atlas.py`（重建网站）、`agreement_curve.py`（模型间一致性分析）。
  - GPU 提取：`pipeline/atlas_h100/` 下的脚本，如 `build_ts_corpus.py`（构建 Tabula Sapiens 语料库）、`run_model.py`（运行模型）、`sae.py`（SAE 训练）。
- **运行示例**：
  ```bash
  pip install -r requirements.txt
  export ATLAS_BASE=$(pwd)
  cp /path/to/MANUSCRIPT.md /path/to/SUPPLEMENTARY.md outputs/atlas/comparative/
  python pipeline/scripts/audit_all.py
  python pipeline/scripts/inject_atlas.py
  ```
- **数据格式**：输入为单细胞表达数据（如 Tabula Sapiens 的 h5ad 格式），输出为特征目录、结果文件（JSON）和图表。模型输入格式各异（如 binning、rank order、文本），由适配器处理。
- **调试入口**：`pipeline/scripts/` 下的脚本可直接运行，如 `coexpr_degmatched.py`（共表达基线）、`trrust_robustness/s01_build_cache.py`（TRRUST 缓存构建），适合断点调试。

## 核心 idea

核心方法学洞察是：**通过统一的数据、SAE 和校准注释，将模型比较转化为可统计检验的假设，并用严格的零模型区分真实生物学信号与数据库伪影**。该框架强调“每个结论都必须有对应的零模型”，从而避免了常见的过度解读，并揭示了模型共享的“核心”主要是共表达结构，而非模型特有的知识。

## 可搬移点

- **SAE 训练与特征提取模块**（`pipeline/atlas_h100/common/sae.py`）：可解耦并用于任何单细胞基础模型的内部表示分析，以提取可解释特征。
- **校准注释器**（`pipeline/atlas_h100/common/annotate.py`）：可独立使用，将特征基因列表映射到生物学通路，并支持自定义数据库。
- **零模型生成器**（如 `degree_null.py`、`coexpr_degmatched.py`）：可迁移到其他生物基座模型评估中，用于生成随机基因或度匹配零模型，验证预测显著性。
- **CKA 和 SAE 方差解释分析**（`cell_cka.py`、`svd_vs_sae.py`）：可复用为模型表示空间的比较工具，适用于虚拟细胞模型集成。
- **审计框架**（`audit_all.py`）：可泛化为任何科学计算项目的可追溯性检查，确保结果可复现。
- **License**：README 未明确说明，需确认。

**可迁移性评估**：该仓库的模块化设计（适配器、SAE、注释、分析脚本分离）支持逐步替换，例如可将新的单细胞模型通过适配器接入，或替换注释数据库，以适配特定课题需求。
readme:
# Comparative SAE Atlas

Ten single-cell foundation models, run on the same 6,000 Tabula Sapiens cells, opened with one
sparse autoencoder per layer (172 in all), annotated with one calibrated method, and compared:
what each model encodes, what they share, which to use for a given task, and whether their
features predict biology the models were never shown.

Live atlas: https://avantipova.github.io/comparative-sae-atlas/ (also served from this
repository's `index.html`; open it locally with any static server).

## What is here

```
index.html, data/            the site: a 12 MB page plus the feature maps it fetches on demand
outputs/atlas/comparative/   the 59 result files and 7 figures every number is read from
pipeline/atlas_h100/         the GPU stage: adapters, SAE, extraction, per-model analyses
pipeline/scripts/            the local stage: matrices, controls, prediction tests, assembly, audit
pipeline/atlas_template.html the site's markup; index.html is built from it
pipeline/legacy/             earlier builders, kept for provenance, used by nothing
docs/DECISIONS.md            what was decided, why, what it cost, where it lives
docs/METHODS.md              methods in brief, with pointers into the code
docs/REPRODUCE.md            how to check the numbers, rebuild the site, re-run the analysis, re-extract
docs/RESULTS.md              every result file: written by, read by, what it holds
requirements.txt             the local analysis environment (Python 3.13, NumPy 2.3.4)
```

Not here: the manuscript and supplement (shared separately; the audit needs them dropped into
`outputs/atlas/comparative/`), the per-run feature catalogues and external inputs (1.2 GB,
published as release assets and fetched by `pipeline/scripts/fetch_runs.sh`), and the SAE
weights and activations, which stay on the GPU host (`pipeline/atlas_h100/README.md`).

The catalogues were re-extracted in October 2026 after three faults in the first release were
found: a position cap that let some models see 32 cells and others 6,000, filler genes in the
top-gene lists, and an unseeded SAE. Every number below is from the corrected run; what changed
and why is in `docs/DECISIONS.md` (decision 16).

## Check it

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
export ATLAS_BASE=$(pwd)
cp /path/to/MANUSCRIPT.md /path/to/SUPPLEMENTARY.md outputs/atlas/comparative/
python pipeline/scripts/audit_all.py      # 312 checks: paper, supplement, figures, site
python pipeline/scripts/inject_atlas.py   # rebuilds index.html from the result files
```

## The models

| model | params | layers | reads a cell as | objective | prior | species |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| AIDO.Cell | 10M | 8 | expression, all genes | MLM | none | human |
| scGPT | ~50M | 12 | binned expression | MLM | none | human |
| tGPT | ~120M | 8 | rank order | autoregressive | none | human |
| scFoundation | 100M | 12 | expression, read-depth aware | MAE | none | human |
| GeneCompass | 104M | 12 | rank order plus value | MLM | knowledge graph | human, mouse |
| MaxToki | 217M | 11 | rank order | autoregressive (Llama) | none | human |
| Geneformer-V2 | 316M | 18 | rank order | MLM | none | human |
| UCE | 650M | 33 | ESM2 protein tokens, sampled by expression | masked | ESM | multi-species |
| C2S-Scale | 2B | 26 | rank-ordered gene names as text | autoregressive | text (Gemma-2) | human, mouse |
| Tahoe-x1 | 3B | 32 | binned expression | MLM | none | human |

Checkpoints and sizes are in `pipeline/atlas_h100/configs/models.yaml` and Table S1.

## What we found

Every number below is audited against the result file that produced it. The controls that
failed are reported alongside the ones that passed.

- **The naive "universal core" is a database artefact.** The permissive annotator (top-5 genes
  against five large databases) reports 1,977 concepts shared by all ten models. Random genes
  share 3,570 under the same construction (z = −24.2); at the mid layer 365 real against 582
  random (z = −4.9). It does not hold.
- **A calibrated backbone is real and modest.** Requiring three of a feature's top-10 genes in
  one curated pathway of at most 200 genes, 96 concepts are shared by at least 8 of the 10
  models: 27.5× the uniform random-gene null and 51.2× a degree-matched one (p < 0.004, 250
  permutations); 55 to 133 concepts at every depth; reproduced on an independent draw of cells
  that shares none with the corpus (Jaccard 0.52 against 0.035, p = 0.02, ten models). By the
  genes behind each match, 42 concepts are one protein-synthesis block, 12 other housekeeping
  and 42 specific programmes (antigen presentation, cytokine signalling, defence, muscle); the
  96 form 37 distinct programmes (`backbone_composition.json`). No concept is in all ten models.
- **Co-expression alone recovers most of it.** A dictionary built from gene-gene correlation in
  the same cells, with no model (a seed gene plus its nine most correlated genes), recovers 73
  to 95 of the 96 backbone concepts per dictionary with random seeds; the models' own middle
  layers recover 23 to 96. The backbone is mostly the co-expression structure of the data, not
  something the models add to it.
- **Geometry agrees without the annotator.** Linear CKA between every pair of models is above
  its cell-shuffle floor (worst pair 43×). The SAE explains more variance than the best rank-32
  PCA subspace in all ten models, by +0.02 (tGPT) to +0.55 (Geneformer-V2). Tissue identity is
  linearly decodable at every depth, with no gain from a non-linear probe. PCA of the raw
  expression decodes tissue as well (0.94 balanced accuracy against 0.85 to 0.96 for the models'
  middle layers).
- **Gene pairs recover known regulation in four of the ten models, but co-expression does about
  as well.** Gene pairs that co-fire in the same features recover TRRUST edges above a null that
  preserves every gene's degree: UCE 10.2×, Tahoe-x1 9.4×, C2S-Scale 5.5×, Geneformer-V2 2.5×
  (p ≤ 0.005); the other six do not. The loose annotation rule uses TRRUST, and the threshold of
  five shared features was chosen after scoring against it. Co-expression from the same cells
  passes the same test; matched for genes and partners per gene, only Tahoe-x1 stays ahead once
  same-family and look-alike pairs are set aside, also within cell types. SAEs that were never
  trained give weaker pair signal, and a Geneformer-V2 with random weights gives none. All four
  hold on an equal budget of 50,707 pairs.
  Pairs predicted by two models independently are 15.3× over the null against 5.0× for one
  (2,000 rewirings, `agreement_curve.py`), a precision of 0.23 %; agreement beyond two models adds
  nothing (none of the 918 pairs shared by five or more models is a known edge).
- **Literature and perturbation give small support.** Co-mention in NCBI gene2pubmed
  2.3× a publication-count-preserving null; in CRISPRi Perturb-seq (genome-wide K562 screen, RPE1 essential-gene screen), knocking down
  one gene moves the other into the top 5 % of responders 1.24× more often than a
  responsiveness-matched null in K562 and 1.33× in RPE1.
- **No new biology, and the reason is the evidence.** Only 98 of 4,272 pairs were never
  co-mentioned, and six of those join two well-studied genes. The models feature 5,953 genes
  with fewer than five papers; the recurrence filter is 7.0× harsher on them, and 732 of the 774
  protein-coding ones are absent from the Perturb-seq screen. Predictive power does not decline
  with how studied a gene is. The atlas ranks testable links; it cannot confirm a link about an
  unstudied gene with these resources.

Also not supported: annotation rate as an interpretability score, "about 100 % of features invisible
to SVD" (true of random directions at this dimensionality), and a "new biology" shortlist that
two nulls showed to be a deficit. Architecture-to-feature associations rest on n = 10 models,
have bootstrap CIs of about ±1, and are reported as descriptive only.

## Credit

Built on the method and single-model atlases of Biodyn-AI
([bio-sae](https://github.com/Biodyn-AI/bio-sae)). This repository is the cross-model extension:
one corpus, one calibrated annotator, a null behind every claim.

one_liner: EXERKINEMAP 是一个结合基因组/蛋白质语言模型与单细胞/空间组学、面向运动响应信号传导的虚拟细胞世界模型框架，核心聚焦细胞状态转换与跨组织映射，与课题高度匹配。
card:
## 是什么

EXERKINEMAP 是一个计算框架，用于建模运动响应性分子信号如何在细胞、组织和器官之间传递。它整合了基因组和蛋白质语言模型、单细胞与空间组学数据以及可穿戴设备数据，构建了一个“虚拟细胞世界模型”，该模型由编码器、转移算子和解码器组成，并采用因果集结构将每个预测限制在其因果过去。它提供前向映射来预测对干预的信号响应，以及逆向映射来提出能将细胞状态移向健康参考的 exerkine、配体和受体序列。

## 亮点

*   **多模态整合**：将基因组语言模型（gLM）、蛋白质语言模型（pLM）、单细胞基础模型（scFM）和空间组学数据融合到一个统一的潜在状态中，并通过分子网络（配体-受体-通路）进行消息传递。
*   **因果结构**：采用因果集结构，确保预测仅依赖于因果过去，增强了模型的可解释性和可靠性。
*   **动作条件转移**：将运动、重力、营养等动作作为外生因果输入，直接进入转移动力学，而非仅影响输出头，使模型能够模拟干预效果。
*   **双向映射**：同时提供前向映射（预测信号响应）和逆向映射（设计序列以达成目标状态），支持从观察到干预的闭环。
*   **可穿戴设备集成**：通过 DBDP 和 WPP 整合可穿戴数据，将生理状态纳入模型，支持个性化健康监测。
*   **序列生成与评估**：提供“Exerkine Sequence Generation Gym”，使用 ESM-2 进行掩码 Gibbs 采样，并评估结构、新颖性、受体结合和跨物种转移，为序列设计提供系统化流程。
*   **模块化设计**：代码结构清晰，将基础模型、任务、评估、可穿戴集成等分离，便于扩展和替换。

## 为何对本课题有用

*   **直接对齐**：该仓库正是“虚拟细胞/虚拟器官 × 单细胞/空间组学 × 生物基座模型”方向的典型实现，展示了如何将多组学数据与语言模型结合，构建细胞状态转移模型。
*   **虚拟细胞世界模型**：其编码器-转移-解码器架构和因果集结构，为构建虚拟细胞或虚拟器官的动态模型提供了可借鉴的框架，特别是如何将外部干预（如运动）作为动作条件融入状态演化。
*   **生物基座模型应用**：展示了如何利用 gLM 和 pLM（如 ESM-2）进行序列嵌入和生成，并如何与单细胞/空间数据对齐，这对于构建生物大语言模型驱动的细胞状态预测器具有直接参考价值。
*   **Bio Agent 潜力**：其逆向映射和序列生成功能，可视为一个“设计代理”，能够提出新的分子序列以实现特定生理目标，这与 Bio Agent 的概念高度契合。
*   **可迁移的方法**：其 tokenization 消融实验、序列生成评估流程、以及可穿戴数据集成方式，均可迁移到其他虚拟细胞或器官建模任务中。

## 怎么用

*   **主入口**：`python run_exerkinemap.py --input data/raw/sequences/ --output results/`
*   **安装**：
    ```bash
    conda create -n exerkinemap python=3.11
    conda activate exerkinemap
    pip install -r requirements.txt
    ```
*   **依赖**：见 `requirements.txt`，包括 numpy, pandas, scipy, h5py, scikit-learn, torch, torch-geometric, tensorflow, umap-learn, tokenizers, transformers, biopython, anndata, scanpy, squidpy, leidenalg, liana, decoupler, networkx, igraph, graphviz, matplotlib, seaborn, scikit-image, mlxtend 等。
*   **输入数据**：
    *   序列数据：FASTA 格式或 CSV（含 `sequence` 和 `label` 列）
    *   单细胞/空间数据：通过 anndata 支持的格式（如 h5ad）
    *   元数据：CSV（如 `gdm_exerkine_candidates.csv`）
*   **输出数据**：
    *   预测结果：CSV 或 JSON（如 tokenization 消融结果）
    *   生成的序列：FASTA 或 CSV
    *   模型权重：PyTorch 或 TensorFlow 格式
*   **GPU 需求**：需要 GPU 加速，特别是训练和 ESM-2 推理（README 建议在 Colab 中使用 GPU）。
*   **调试入口**：
    *   单元测试：`exerkinemap/tests/test_exerkines.py`
    *   示例脚本：`workflows/01_download_data.py`, `workflows/04_build_sequence_reference.py`
    *   教程：`tutorials/exerkine_tutorial.ipynb`, `tutorials/exerkine_sequence_generation_gym.ipynb`

## 核心 idea

核心方法学洞察在于：通过将多模态生物数据（序列、单细胞、空间、可穿戴）编码到一个统一的潜在空间，并利用动作条件转移算子模拟外部干预（如运动）对细胞状态的影响，同时通过因果集结构确保预测的因果一致性，从而实现了从观察到干预的闭环建模，并支持逆向设计分子序列以达成目标生理状态。

## 可搬移点

*   **因果集模块** (`exerkinemap/causal/causal_set.py`)：该模块实现了因果集结构，可独立提取并用于任何需要因果约束的序列或状态预测模型中，增强模型的可解释性。
*   **序列生成与评估流程** (`exerkinemap/generation/` 和 `tutorials/exerkine_sequence_generation_gym.ipynb`)：其基于 ESM-2 的掩码采样和评估指标（结构、新颖性、结合）可迁移到其他蛋白质或 RNA 设计任务中。
*   **tokenization 消融框架** (`exerkinemap/benchmarks/tokenization_ablation.py`)：该框架可复用于评估不同 tokenization 策略在生物序列分类任务中的效果，适用于任何序列基础模型开发。
*   **多模态融合编码器** (`exerkinemap/embeddings/`)：其将 gLM、pLM、scFM 和空间数据融合的机制，可借鉴用于构建其他虚拟细胞模型的输入表示。
*   **可穿戴数据集成** (`Exerkinetics/wearables/`)：其处理可穿戴数据（如 DBDP）的流程，可迁移到需要整合生理时序数据的虚拟器官模型中。
*   **License**：MIT，允许自由使用和修改，但需确认具体文件是否包含额外声明。

# EXERKINEMAP **EXERKINEMAP** (EXERcise KINEmatics Multiomics single-cell Analysis and spatial omics holistic modeling and maPping) is a computational framework for modeling how exercise-responsive molecular signals move between cells, tissues and organs. It combines genomic and protein language models, single-cell and spatial omics, and wearable data in a **virtual cell world model**: an encoder, a transition operator and a decoder, with a causal-set structure that restricts every prediction to its causal past. A forward map predicts the signaling response to an intervention, and an inverse map proposes exerkine, ligand and receptor sequences that move a cell state toward a healthy reference.

> **Status:** research software under active development. Generated sequences and model outputs are **hypotheses to test, not results**, and nothing here is clinical or medical advice. See [Limitations and responsible use](#limitations-and-responsible-use). ## Contents - [What it does](#what-it-does) - [Architecture](#architecture) - [Project status](#project-status) - [Quick start](#quick-start) - [Execution workflows](#execution-workflows) - [Omics foundation model pipeline](#omics-foundation-model-pipeline) - [Downstream tasks](#downstream-tasks) - [Wearables, DBDP and countermeasure design](#wearables-dbdp-and-countermeasure-design) - [Data sources](#data-sources) - [Tutorials and documentation](#tutorials-and-documentation) - [Exerkine Sequence Generation Gym](#exerkine-sequence-generation-gym) - [Tokenization ablation and one-hot control](#tokenization-ablation-and-one-hot-control) - [GDM candidate reference and RefSeq refresh](#gdm-candidate-reference-and-refseq-refresh) - [Limitations and responsible use](#limitations-and-responsible-use) - [License](#license) ## What it does By integrating genomic and protein language models with single-cell and spatial omics, EXERKINEMAP lets you input target molecular sequences to identify and map candidate exerkines, ligands and receptors. It is optimized for exercise-responsive physiological adaptation, for example evaluating exerkine signaling in Gestational Diabetes Mellitus (GDM), using multimodal datasets from [MoTrPAC (rat and human)](https://motrpac-data.org). The model grows along two axes: * **A virtual cell bank** across cell types, genotypes and conditions (healthy control, GDM, T2D, cancer, CVD, obesity). * **Composition** from cells to tissues, organs and the whole person, including the fetal–maternal interface. ## Architecture ### The pipeline * **ExerkineRNA (gLM):** tokenizes nucleotide sequences (codons, regulatory tags) into contextual genomic embeddings. * **ExerkineProtein (pLM):** generates and refines amino-acid representations with models such as ESM-2. * **ExerkineMap:** aligns these sequence embeddings with spatial and single-cell omics to construct predictive ligand–receptor communication networks. ### Virtual cell world model | Part | What it does | |---|---| | **Structured encoder and cellular manifold** | modality encoders (gLM, pLM, scFM, spatial) fused by message passing over a molecular network of ligands, receptors and pathways into a tissue-indexed latent state | | **Action-conditioned transition dynamics** | advances the state under an action (exercise, gravity, nutrition) and a wearable weight; the action enters the dynamics themselves, not only an output head | | **Structured decoder and cross-modal consistency** | decodes RNA and protein sequences, expression, space, phenotype and ligand–receptor compatibility, tied together by translation, alignment, cycle and ligand–receptor consistency losses |

The full definitions, equations and algorithms are in [`docs/exerkine_math_model.md`](docs/exerkine_math_model.md). ### Omics foundation model taxonomy EXERKINEMAP is a **sequence-centric, cell-centric and multi-omics** foundation model system. Each row follows the common omics-FM pipeline: feature representation, embedding strategy, network architecture, applications from molecular to clinical scale.

## Project status | Component | Status | |---|---| | Sequence reference building, RefSeq manifest refresh, GDM candidate catalog | available | | Tokenization ablation and benchmark manifest builder | available | | Pre-training, MoTrPAC fine-tuning and prompting modules (`exerkinemap/foundation_model/`) | available | | Exerkine Sequence Generation Gym (notebook) | available | | scFM and spatial encoder, molecular-network fusion | in development | | Action-conditioned transition operator and decoder with consistency losses | in development | | DBDP / WPP / SensorLM integration and countermeasure policy | design stage | | Tissue-indexed exerkine probabilities (MoTrPAC tissues, HuBMAP organs) | design stage | > The table reflects the current design documents. Update it as modules land. ## Quick start Map your target sequences and generate exerkine communication networks in a few steps. ### 1. Install dependencies ```bash conda create -n exerkinemap python=3.11 conda activate exerkinemap pip install --upgrade pip pip install -r requirements.txt ``` ### 2. Prepare your sequences Place your target RNA or protein sequences into `data/raw/sequences/`. Ensure your MoTrPAC reference metadata is situated in `data/raw/metadata/`. ### 3. Run the model Execute the preprocessing and mapping workflow to align your target sequences against the multi-omics data: ```bash # Prepare references and build sequence embeddings python workflows/01_download_data.py python workflows/04_build_sequence_reference.py # Execute the mapping pipeline python run_exerkinemap.py --input data/raw/sequences/ --output results/ ``` ## Execution workflows The repository workflows cleanly separate foundation model training stages from standard spatial-omics alignment: * `01_download_data.py`: ingests external datasets and prepares local environments. * `02_pretrain_omics_fm.py`: executes the self-supervised pre-training pipeline on generalized large-scale datasets. * `03_finetune_motrpac_fm.py`: executes supervised fine-tuning using validated MoTrPAC targets. * `04_build_sequence_reference.py`: constructs the sequence reference libraries for alignment. * `05_prompt_specialized_tasks.py`: runs human prompts and inference logic for downstream tasks such as variant prediction or biomarker identification. ## Omics foundation model pipeline The three-stage pipeline (`exerkinemap/foundation_model/`) parses complex, multimodal biological data into cohesive physiological representations: 1. **Pre-training (`pretraining.py`):** self-supervised learning on large, unlabeled biological data. Transformers convert nucleotide (`ExerkineRNA`) and amino-acid (`ExerkineProtein`) sequences into tokens with positional encoding, establishing a baseline understanding of sequence grammar. 2. **MoTrPAC-anchored fine-tuning (`finetuning.py`):** supervised fine-tuning anchors the learned embeddings to empirical, multi-tissue expression data from the Molecular Transducers of Physical Activity Consortium (MoTrPAC). With a small curated exerkine set, prefer frozen backbones with adapters or light heads over full fine-tuning. 3. **Prompting and execution (`prompting.py`):** human prompting and Reinforcement Learning with Human Feedback (RLHF) apply the contextualized biological grammar to downstream biomedical tasks. ## Downstream tasks The `exerkinemap/tasks/` module isolates the model's physiological outputs: * **Exercise-responsive biomarker discovery:** extracts digital biomarkers from the latent space and cross-references them with the Exerkine Atlas. * **DNA and protein variant prediction:** generates exerkine sequence variants and predicts ligand–receptor binding affinities for spatial communication networks. * **Personalized medicine and virtual cell mapping:** builds patient-specific physiological profiles by tracking causal-set propagation, and generates virtual cell state maps from a sedentary baseline to a healthy, exercise-adapted state. ## Wearables, DBDP and countermeasure design Wearable telemetry enters the world model as exogenous, causal inputs that rescale the transition dynamics. * **Digital Biomarkers Data Pipeline (DBDP):** device harmonization (`devicely`), posture and activity recognition (DeepPostures, Human Activity Recognition), causal sliding-window features (FLIRT), and the [SensorLM](https://github.com/Google-Health/consumer-health-research/tree/main/sensorlm) sensor–language foundation model. Candidate data sources include the Stanford Wearables set from the DBDP Digital Health Data Repository. * **Whole Person Physiome (WPP):** a multiorgan knowledge graph (skeletal muscle, bone, tendon, heart, liver, brain, immune tissue) used to model myokine, osteokine and other exerkine cross-talk and to reason about unloading in microgravity, on the Moon (0.16 g) and on Mars (0.38 g). * **Closed-loop countermeasures:** a bounded policy recalibrates exercise and nutrition recommendations for skeletal muscle and other exerkine organs, spaceflight, health and resilience, and disease. It is **decision support with clinician oversight**, particularly for pregnancy, GDM and cardiovascular conditions. Whether circadian-timed training improves adaptation is evaluated, not assumed. ## Data sources | Source | Use | |---|---| | [MoTrPAC](https://motrpac-data.org) rat endurance-training compendium | whole blood, plasma and 18 solid tissues of male and female rats across 1, 2, 4 and 8 weeks; multiple omes | | MoTrPAC human acute-exercise data | sedentary adults, endurance and resistance bouts; blood, adipose and muscle | | HuBMAP | human organ reference atlases and cell-type tables for receptor-side targets | | Exerkine Atlas | validation of candidate exerkines | | UniProt, RefSeq | protein and mRNA sequences for exerkines, ligands and receptors (human and rat) | | DBDP repositories | wearable and CGM data for physiological priors | MoTrPAC tissues are rat and HuBMAP organs are human, so cross-species results need an explicit ortholog and organ-matching step with an uncertainty estimate. Follow each dataset's data-use terms. ## Tutorials and documentation * [`docs/exerkine_math_model.md`](docs/exerkine_math_model.md): the mathematical model, with notation, algorithms, a worked numerical example and a list of open issues. Start here to understand the algorithm. * [`tutorials/exerkine_tutorial.ipynb`](tutorials/exerkine_tutorial.ipynb): step-by-step walkthrough that follows the math reference. * [`tutorials/exerkine_sequence_generation_gym.ipynb`](tutorials/exerkine_sequence_generation_gym.ipynb): sequence-generation evaluation environment (below). * Other notebooks in `tutorials/` cover custom single-cell and spatial preprocessing, custom GLM tokenization, and building specialized ligand–receptor databases. ## Exerkine Sequence Generation Gym A Colab-ready notebook for **constrained variant design** of exerkines, ligands and receptors. It samples variants with ESM-2 masked Gibbs sampling (fixing signal peptides, cysteines and chosen binding residues) and scores each one against a matched random-mutation null: | Check | Measures | |---|---| | Structure | ESMFold pLDDT and backbone RMSD to wild type | | Novelty | nearest other natural sequence, training-set identity, diversity of the generated set | | Receptor binding | change in ligand–receptor score vs. wild type, as a percentile of random mutations | | Rat vs. human | ortholog divergence, where mutations fall, and cross-species binding transfer | ```bash # open tutorials/exerkine_sequence_generation_gym.ipynb in Google Colab (GPU recommended for ESMFold) ``` These scores are **proxies**. A language model that generates and scores the same sequences is circular, the bundled pair scorer is a demonstration trained on a handful of literature pairs, and none of this replaces experiments. Replace the demo pairs with your Exerkine Atlas pairs and plug in your own protein-level compatibility model. ## Tokenization ablation and one-hot control Run a matched binary sequence-classification benchmark from an empirical CSV with `sequence` and `label` (`0` or `1`) columns. EXERKINEMAP does not ship this labeled table: it must be assembled from a prespecified sequence-to-phenotype or regulatory task (for example, MoTrPAC-linked differential exercise labels) before benchmarking. The runner uses a stratified train/validation/test split, trains learned vocabularies only on the training sequences, and gives each tokenization arm the same linear-model optimization budget. It reports a position-aware one-hot supervised control alongside character, non-overlapping codon 3-mer, overlapping 6-mer, BPE, unigram and WordPiece tokenization. ```bash python -m exerkinemap.benchmarks.tokenization_ablation \ --input /path/to/empirical_sequence_labels.csv \ --output results/benchmarking/tokenization_ablation.csv ``` The CSV contains per-method accuracy, AUROC, AUPRC, Brier score, feature count and fit time. A same-stem JSON file records the evaluation configuration. These results are empirical outputs; the command does not populate results with placeholder scores. The default benchmark caps every sequence at 512 nt using a 5-prime (`prefix`) window and caps learned-tokenizer vocabulary training at 25,000 characters. Both settings are recorded in the JSON metadata. Choose a window that matches the prespecified biological task; use `--long-sequence-policy error` to reject rather than truncate long sequences. ### Raw controls Keep raw negative controls in [sequence_controls.csv](./data/raw/benchmarking/sequence_controls.csv). Each `control_definition` must state whether a control is empirical, technical or reference-derived: ```csv control_id,species,sequence,refseq_accession,source_url,control_definition ``` Build a benchmark-only processed file by selecting positives explicitly from the RefSeq candidate catalog: ```bash python -m exerkinemap.benchmarks.sequence_manifest \ --positive-entity-id FGF19 \ --positive-entity-id RARRES2 \ --positive-entity-id LEP \ --controls data/raw/benchmarking/sequence_controls.csv \ --candidates data/processed/refseq_sequence_manifest.csv \ --output data/processed/benchmarks/gdm_sequence_benchmark.csv ``` The builder requires at least three positive records and three raw controls, preserves control provenance, and rejects controls whose sequence duplicates a selected positive. Run tokenization ablation against the resulting processed benchmark file, not the all-positive candidate reference catalog. A benchmark built with reference-derived controls is a technical sequence baseline and must not be presented as evidence of exercise responsiveness or causal biology. ## GDM candidate reference and RefSeq refresh [gdm_exerkine_candidates.csv](./data/reference/gdm_exerkine_candidates.csv) is a typed catalog of the GDM-network candidates. It includes gene products, receptors, metabolites, reactive species, protein complexes, pathways, extracellular-vesicle cargo and unresolved aliases. Only unambiguous protein-coding genes receive human and rat RefSeq mRNA records; other entities remain in the manifest with blank sequence fields and an explicit `resolution_status`. Refresh [refseq_sequence_manifest.csv](./data/processed/refseq_sequence_manifest.csv) from NCBI with a contact email: ```bash python -m exerkinemap.scripts.refresh_refseq_manifest \ --email d.gomez@me.com ``` The resulting manifest is a candidate reference, not an empirical binary benchmark. Its `label=1` means candidate-list membership; it does not establish exercise responsiveness or causal activity. Do not use it as the tokenization-ablation input until a prespecified empirical negative/control cohort has been added. ## Limitations and responsible use * **Research use only.** Outputs are not medical advice. Countermeasure and exercise recommendations are bounded decision support that requires clinician oversight. * **Generated sequences are hypotheses.** Plausibility, predicted structure and predicted binding are proxies; experimental validation is required. Screen generated sequences against toxin and pathogen databases before sharing them. * **Circular scoring.** Using the same language model to generate and to score sequences overstates quality; use independent predictors. * **Small labeled set.** A curated exerkine list of roughly 800 entries limits full fine-tuning; prefer adapters and frozen backbones. * **Species gap.** MoTrPAC tissues are rat and HuBMAP organs are human; transfer needs ortholog mapping and uncertainty estimates. * **Wearable models.** Sensor–language models trained on consumer-device data must be validated on spaceflight and clinical cohorts before use there. * **Candidate lists are not evidence.** Membership in the GDM candidate catalog does not establish exercise responsiveness or causal activity. ## License See the repository license for terms of use.

one_liner: CellBench 是一个对 13 个单细胞基座模型进行冻结骨干基准测试的代码库，提供模型适配器、下游评估头和数据集清单，直接服务于单细胞基座模型的系统评估与比较。
card:
## 是什么

CellBench 是一个**冻结骨干（frozen-backbone）单细胞基础模型基准测试框架**，用于系统评估 13 个公开的单细胞基础模型（scFM）检查点以及 3 个无泄漏训练集拟合基线（PCA、UMAP、scVI）在多种下游任务上的表现。它覆盖 12 个静态组织/疾病队列和 4 个 CRISPR Perturb-seq 筛选，通过统一的适配器、评估流水线和统计分析，回答“冻结的单细胞基础模型保留了什么、遗漏了什么、泄漏了什么”这一核心问题。

## 亮点

- **大规模、多模型、多任务基准**：统一评估 13 个 scFM 和 3 个基线，跨越 16 个公共数据集，执行 2304 次表示运行和 192 次扰动运行，提供全面的性能画像。
- **标准化适配器架构**：`bio/models/adapters/` 为每个模型提供统一接口，支持冻结骨干提取嵌入，便于公平比较。
- **严格的泄漏控制**：基线模型仅在训练集上拟合，并执行 208 对预训练重叠审计，确保评估的公正性。
- **丰富的诊断工具**：包括直接线性探针（罕见亚型、连续细胞程序）、检查点参数审计、零变化扰动技能分析等，深入剖析模型行为。
- **可复现性**：提供完整的清单（`manifests/`）、数据/权重下载脚本、SHA-256 校验和隔离环境配置，确保结果可复现。

## 为何对本课题有用

CellBench 直接服务于**虚拟细胞/虚拟器官 × 单细胞/空间组学 × 生物基座模型**课题，因为它提供了：

- **评估方法论**：为任何新的单细胞基础模型（包括虚拟细胞模型）提供一套标准化的冻结骨干评估协议，可迁移到虚拟器官构建中的细胞状态预测、扰动响应模拟等任务。
- **模型选择依据**：通过对比 13 个 scFM 在组织、疾病、跨物种和扰动场景下的表现，帮助研究者选择最适合虚拟细胞建模的骨干模型。
- **泄漏检测框架**：其预训练重叠审计方法可应用于生物大语言模型，防止训练数据泄漏导致的性能虚高。
- **扰动预测基准**：Perturb-seq 评估协议可直接用于验证虚拟细胞模型在基因敲除/过表达下的预测能力，是构建可交互虚拟细胞的关键。
- **可扩展的适配器模式**：`bio/models/adapters/` 的设计可被复用，快速集成新的基础模型到虚拟细胞流水线中。

## 怎么用

- **主入口**：`main.py` 和 `scripts/run_full_benchmark.py` 是主要入口，运行完整基准测试。
- **安装与依赖**：使用 `environment-cellbench.yml` 创建 conda 环境，并安装 `requirements-cellbench.txt`；可选运行 `scripts/setup_frontier_environments.sh` 为特定模型（如 CellFM、GeneCompass）创建隔离环境。
- **数据与权重下载**：运行 `scripts/download_datasets.py` 和 `scripts/download_weights.py`（或 `download_frontier_weights.py`）下载公共数据集和预训练检查点，并验证 SHA-256。
- **运行基准**：`python scripts/run_full_benchmark.py --output-dir output/cellbench_runs`，然后 `python scripts/export_metrics.py` 导出指标。
- **诊断与复现**：运行 `scripts/run_direct_embedding_program_probe.py` 进行线性探针，`analysis/perturbation_rq.py` 进行扰动分析，`analysis/overlap_sensitivity.py` 进行重叠敏感性分析。
- **输入/输出格式**：输入为 `.h5ad` 格式的单细胞数据（如 CITE-seq、10x Genomics），输出为嵌入、评估指标（如聚类 ARI、注释准确率、扰动技能分数）和表格（`results/supplementary_tables.xlsx`）。
- **GPU 需求**：需要 GPU 加速，尤其是运行大型 scFM（如 scFoundation、UCELL）的推理。
- **调试**：`tests/` 目录包含单元测试，`scripts/smoke_pipeline.py` 可快速验证适配器契约。

## 核心 idea

CellBench 的核心方法学洞察是：**通过统一的冻结骨干适配器和严格的泄漏控制，将单细胞基础模型的评估从“黑盒性能报告”转化为“可分解的能力剖析”**，从而揭示模型在保留生物信号、遗漏稀有信息、泄漏预训练数据三个维度上的真实行为。其创新在于将评估设计为模块化、可复现的流水线，并引入零变化扰动技能和预训练重叠审计等新颖指标，为模型选择和改进提供可操作的反馈。

## 可搬移点

- **适配器接口**（`bio/models/adapters/`）：最值得解耦的部分。每个适配器封装了模型加载、预处理、嵌入提取的细节，可被直接复制或 import 到自定义 Pipeline 中，用于快速集成新的 scFM 或基线模型。
- **评估流水线**（`cell_eval/`）：包括固定 MLP 探针、Leiden 聚类、scIB 批次评估、Perturb-seq 残差解码等模块，可独立使用，用于评估任何嵌入向量的下游性能。
- **泄漏审计脚本**（`analysis/overlap_sensitivity.py`）：可迁移到生物大语言模型训练中，检测训练数据与评估数据的重叠。
- **数据准备脚本**（`bio/assets/prepare_datasets.py`）：标准化 `.h5ad` 处理流程，可复用于其他单细胞数据集。
- **License**：代码和脚本采用 MIT 许可证，允许自由使用和修改；但第三方模型检查点和数据集需遵守各自的上游许可，使用时需确认。

# CellBench: Frozen-Backbone Benchmark of Single-Cell Foundation Models

Official benchmark codebase, model adapters, downstream evaluation heads, statistical analysis scripts, and dataset/checkpoint manifests for **CellBench**:

> **What Frozen Single-Cell Foundation Models Preserve, Miss, and Leak**

CellBench evaluates **13 publicly released single-cell foundation model (scFM) checkpoints** in frozen-backbone mode alongside **3 leak-free training-split-fitted baselines** (`PCA`, `UMAP`, and `scVI`) across:
- **12 static tissue and disease cohorts** spanning healthy human organs, human diseases, and matched mouse organs (**2,304 representation runs** across unsupervised clustering, native batch assessment, supervised cell-type annotation, and HVG expression reconstruction);
- **4 CRISPR Perturb-seq screens** (**192 perturbation runs** across unseen two-gene combinations and unseen single-gene knockouts, anchored to zero-change baseline skill $\hat{\Delta}_g = \mathbf{0}$);
- **Direct frozen-embedding linear probes** for rare (<1%) subtypes and continuous cellular programs, **instantiated checkpoint tensor accounting**, and a **208-pair pretraining provenance and overlap audit**.

---

## Repository Structure

- **`bio/`** — Standardized frozen-backbone model adapters for all 13 scFMs and 3 training-split-fitted baselines, ortholog mappers, and automated dataset/weight downloaders (`bio/assets/datasets.py`, `bio/assets/weights.py`, `bio/assets/frontier.py`, `bio/assets/prepare_datasets.py`).
- **`cell_eval/`** — Unified downstream evaluation engine: fixed MLP probes for annotation and HVG reconstruction, Leiden clustering, native `scIB` batch assessment, paired-control Perturb-seq residual lookup decoding, and evaluation metrics.
- **`configs/`** — Per-model YAML execution and preprocessing configurations (`cellfm.yaml`, `cellplm.yaml`, `genecompass.yaml`, `geneformer.yaml`, `langcell.yaml`, `nicheformer.yaml`, `pca.yaml`, `scfoundation.yaml`, `scgpt.yaml`, `sclong.yaml`, `scprint2.yaml`, `scvi.yaml`, `tabula.yaml`, `transcriptformer.yaml`, `uce.yaml`, `umap.yaml`).
- **`scripts/`** — Command-line entry points for environment setup, downloading datasets and model weights, running the full benchmark, and executing direct linear-probe diagnostics:
  - `scripts/download_datasets.py`: Download and verify raw public datasets into `datasets/source_files/`.
  - `scripts/download_weights.py` & `scripts/download_frontier_weights.py`: Download pretrained checkpoints with SHA-256 verification into `weights/`.
  - `scripts/run_full_benchmark.py` & `scripts/run_batch.py`: Run multi-seed frozen-backbone extraction and downstream evaluation across cohorts and tasks.
  - `scripts/run_direct_embedding_program_probe.py`: Reproduce 5-fold Ridge linear probes for rare (<1%) subtypes and continuous cellular programs.
  - `scripts/compute_biological_information_channels.py`: Reproduce 12-cohort biological-channel profiles and concordance statistics.
- **`analysis/`** — Non-parametric rank aggregation (`task_layout.py`), checkpoint tensor parameter accounting (`checkpoint_parameter_audit.py`), leave-study-out overlap sensitivity (`overlap_sensitivity.py`, `match_scfoundation_sources.py`), Perturb-seq zero-change skill analysis (`perturbation_rq.py`), supplementary table generation (`generate_supplementary_tables.py`), and figure generation scripts.
- **`manifests/`** — Curated CSV and Markdown link indices for all 16 evaluation cohorts (`datasets.csv`) and 16 evaluated methods (`models.csv`).
- **`data/` & `results/`** — Run-level score exports (`data/exports/`), donor split counts, checkpoint parameter manifests (`data/parameter_audit/`), the 208-pair pretraining-overlap audit (`data/pretraining_overlap_audit.csv`), direct linear-probe outputs (`data/direct_embedding_program_probe.csv`), and multi-sheet Excel workbooks (`results/supplementary_tables.xlsx`, `results/perturbation_seed_results.xlsx`).
- **`resources/` & `tests/`** — Ensembl 1-to-1 human–mouse orthology tables, isolated environment lockfiles for frontier checkpoints, and unit tests.

---

## Quick Start

### 1. Environment Setup

```bash
conda env create -f environment-cellbench.yml
conda activate cellbench
pip install -r requirements-cellbench.txt

# Optional isolated environments for framework-specific checkpoints (CellFM, GeneCompass, scPRINT2, TranscriptFormer)
bash scripts/setup_frontier_environments.sh
```

### 2. Download Public Datasets & Pretrained Checkpoints

```bash
# Download public evaluation datasets and prepare standardized .h5ad cohorts
python scripts/download_datasets.py
python -m bio.assets.prepare_datasets

# Download pretrained foundation model weights and verify SHA-256 digests
python scripts/download_weights.py
python scripts/download_frontier_weights.py
python scripts/download_public_code.py
```

### 3. Run Frozen-Backbone Benchmark Evaluations

```bash
# Smoke test adapter contracts
python scripts/smoke_pipeline.py

# Full multi-seed benchmark (seeds 41, 42, 43 across 16 methods x 16 cohorts)
python scripts/run_full_benchmark.py --output-dir output/cellbench_runs
python scripts/export_metrics.py --run-dir output/cellbench_runs
```

### 4. Reproduce Diagnostic Probes, Provenance Audits, & Figures

```bash
pip install -r requirements-analysis.txt

# Direct frozen-embedding cellular-program and rare-subtype linear probes
CELLBENCH_ROOT=. python scripts/run_direct_embedding_program_probe.py
python scripts/compute_biological_information_channels.py

# Perturbation zero-change skill, overlap sensitivity, and figure generation
python analysis/perturbation_rq.py
python analysis/overlap_sensitivity.py
python analysis/redraw_main_task_figures.py
python analysis/draw_rq678_figures.py
```

---

one_liner: ssl-lab 开发基于 JEPA 的生成式自监督模型，核心目标是单细胞扰动数据生成与虚拟细胞建模，方法上实现条件流先验与解码器，与课题高度匹配。
card:
## 是什么

ssl-lab 是一个自监督学习实验室，专注于开发**可生成可信生物数据**的新方法。其旗舰目标是**单细胞扰动预测**：给定一个细胞群体和一种（可能从未实验过的）遗传扰动，生成该扰动后的细胞群体——包括哪些基因表达变化、变化幅度以及细胞间的异质性。它从 JEPA（联合嵌入预测架构）出发，通过添加潜在先验和与数据似然匹配的解码器，将自监督表示学习扩展为生成模型。该仓库是 genai-lab 的姊妹项目，方法学保持模态无关，可迁移到生理信号、健康记录和分子结构等数据。

## 亮点

- **方法学前沿**：将 JEPA（自监督学习 SOTA）扩展为生成模型，填补了表示学习与生成建模之间的空白。
- **条件生成**：实现了带 classifier-free guidance 的条件流先验，支持在给定干预条件下生成数据。
- **严谨的实验设计**：预注册研究、多臂对照（从零训练的 CVAE 基线、无训练加性参考）、每项指标报告不确定性（联合 bootstrap 与 max-t 区间）。
- **模块化架构**：数据适配器将不同模态（图像、单细胞、ECG）统一为模态无关的 token 张量，便于跨模态迁移。
- **工程化支持**：提供远程 GPU 训练工具（SkyPilot + RunPod），支持大规模训练。

## 为何对本课题有用

- **直接对齐**：单细胞扰动预测是虚拟细胞模型的核心任务之一，本仓库提供了完整的 JEPA + 条件流 + 计数解码器 pipeline，可直接作为虚拟细胞生成模型的基线或组件。
- **方法迁移**：JEPA 的自监督预训练在标签稀缺时（如 5% 标签）显著提升下游性能，这对单细胞数据（标签昂贵）尤其有价值。
- **条件生成范式**：条件流先验 + classifier-free guidance 可推广到其他干预条件（如药物、基因编辑），为虚拟器官中的干预模拟提供生成框架。
- **评估体系**：其效果大小、校准度、交互分数等评估指标可复用于虚拟细胞模型的验证，确保生成数据“可信如实测”。
- **模态无关设计**：数据适配器模式可轻松接入空间组学、生理信号等新模态，支撑虚拟器官的多模态整合。

## 怎么用

- **安装**：`mamba env create -f environment.yml`，`conda activate ssllab`，`pip install -e .`。
- **主入口**：
  - 表示学习：`python examples/jepa_basics/01_train_jepa_mnist.py --epochs 5`
  - 线性探针：`python examples/jepa_basics/02_linear_probe.py`
  - 解码器：`python examples/generative_jepa/03_train_decoder.py --epochs 5`
  - 流先验：`python examples/generative_jepa/04_train_flow_prior.py --epochs 20`
  - 采样：`python examples/generative_jepa/05_sample_and_decode.py`
- **单细胞扰动 pipeline**：`examples/perturbation_response/` 下按阶段脚本（00 处理数据、01 预训练、02 探针、03 解码器、04 条件流、05 采样、06 评估等）。
- **数据格式**：单细胞数据为 AnnData（.h5ad），ECG 为 WFDB 格式（带校验和读取器）。
- **GPU 支持**：通过 `ops/` 包（SkyPilot + RunPod）远程训练，脚本见 `examples/ops/`。
- **测试**：`pytest` 运行测试（`tests/` 和 `ops/tests/`）。

## 核心 idea

**核心洞察**：JEPA 的表示学习能力可以通过添加一个条件流先验和一个与数据似然匹配的解码器，转化为生成模型，从而在保持表示质量的同时实现可控生成。其关键创新在于：
- 将 JEPA 的潜在空间视为一个可采样的分布，用条件流（conditional flow）建模给定干预下的潜在变化，实现条件生成。
- 使用 classifier-free guidance 增强条件控制，无需额外分类器。
- 解码器针对数据似然设计（如单细胞计数用 NB/ZINB），确保生成数据在统计上可信。
- 通过“动作算子”（action operator）将生成与规划统一，为主动世界模型铺路。

## 可搬移点

- **条件流先验模块**（`src/ssllab/generative/`）：可直接解耦，用于任何潜在空间的条件生成，替换为自定义条件（如药物、基因扰动）。
- **JEPA 编码器/预测器**（`src/ssllab/models/`）：可单独用于自监督预训练，提升下游任务标签效率。
- **NB/ZINB 计数解码器**：可直接用于单细胞计数数据的生成，适配其他计数型组学数据。
- **评估指标**（效果大小、校准度、交互分数）：可复用于虚拟细胞模型的验证。
- **数据适配器模式**：可借鉴其将不同模态统一为 token 张量的设计，快速接入空间组学等新数据。
- **License**：README 未明确说明，需确认。

# ssl-lab [![Documentation](https://img.shields.io/badge/docs-pleiadian53.github.io%2Fssl--lab-indigo)](https://pleiadian53.github.io/ssl-lab/) 📖 **Documentation site (full math rendering):** ssl-lab develops new methods for **generating biological data that can be trusted like measured data**. Generative models already produce convincing images and video. The goal here is the same capability for experiments: given a biological system and an intervention, generate the dataset the experiment would have produced, accurately enough to explore, prioritize and partly replace work that today needs new sequencing runs or extra assays. The flagship target is **single-cell perturbation data**. Given a population of cells and a genetic perturbation, possibly a combination nobody has run, the model generates the perturbed population: which genes move, by how much, and how much the response varies from cell to cell. The same aim carries to other modalities, including physiological signals, health records and molecular structure. **Reliable is measured, not assumed.** Generated data are scored on the direction and the size of the effects they predict and on whether the generated populations are calibrated, always against strong references: a model of the same task trained from scratch, and a training-free baseline that a useful generator must beat. **The method line: self-supervised representations made generative.** The current build starts from JEPA (joint-embedding predictive architectures), a state-of-the-art self-supervised learner that predicts the *embeddings* of masked regions from their context instead of reconstructing raw data. On its own JEPA learns representations and cannot generate. To sample data the lab adds a **prior** over the latent and a **decoder** back to data space, matched to the data's likelihood. JEPA is the starting point because it is the frontier most worth extending, not a fixed commitment: each component is kept only where it earns its place against those references, and the aim is methods at and beyond the state of the art in both self-supervised learning and generative modeling. A design-space survey of how to make JEPA generative recommends a **conditional flow prior**: generation *given a condition*, such as a perturbation or an intervention, paired with a decoder matched to the data. That conditional architecture is the one shown below. ```mermaid flowchart LR XB(["baseline state x_b"]) --> ENC["JEPA encoder
(frozen)"] P(["intervention p"]) --> EMB["embed e(p)"] ENC -- "z_b" --> COND["condition
c = (z_b, z_p)"] EMB -- "z_p" --> COND NOISE(["noise ε"]) --> FLOW["conditional flow prior
v_η(z, t, c)"] COND --> FLOW FLOW -- "sample z* ~ p(z given c)" --> DEC["decoder z → x
(count-aware / pixel)"] DEC --> GEN(["generated sample
given the condition"]) classDef accent fill:#eef2ff,stroke:#6366f1,color:#1e1b4b; classDef io fill:#f8fafc,stroke:#94a3b8,color:#0f172a; class ENC,EMB,FLOW,DEC accent; class XB,P,NOISE,GEN io; ``` > The unconditional generative slice is built and verified end to end, and the conditional flow prior, i.e. the `v(z, t, c)` path with classifier-free guidance, is implemented and method-de-risked. The method is modality-agnostic; its applications (single-cell perturbation, digital phenotyping, and more) and the full design space are the **[Generative JEPA series](docs/generative_jepa/index.md)** and [Research directions](#research-directions) below. This *generative* slice is one of **two complementary extensions of JEPA** the lab pursues. The second turns JEPA from a passive predictor into an *active* world-model, described under [Research directions](#research-directions) below. The two are beginning to **converge**: the condition a generative JEPA samples under can be an *action*, and an action read as a latent **operator** is exactly the world-model line. So "generate the outcome of an intervention" and "plan the intervention" become two faces of one model. ## Why ssl-lab exists ssl-lab is a spin-off of its sibling project [genai-lab](https://github.com/pleiadian53/genai-lab) (generative AI for computational biology). It is where new methods for self-supervised and generative modeling are developed and stress-tested, starting from JEPA and the ideas built around it. The core is kept deliberately **modality-agnostic**, so a method proven on one kind of biological data can move to the next through a data adapter. Methods mature here and return to genai-lab as **genomic generative models** that can stand in for, and help plan, real experiments. ## Research directions JEPA is a *representation learner*: it learns by predicting the embeddings of masked regions from context. ssl-lab pushes it past that in two complementary ways: **1. Generative JEPA: make the representation *sampleable*.** *(method built + de-risked; design space mapped; applications WIP)* Add a prior over the latent and a decoder back to data space. The unconditional slice is verified end to end, with a rich, non-collapsed latent (strong linear-probe accuracy with no pretraining labels) and *genuinely novel* samples. A full **[Generative JEPA design-space survey](docs/generative_jepa/index.md)** then maps four routes for making JEPA generative: decode the latent, a variational posterior, conditioned diffusion, and planning on top. It adds the **conditional flow prior** that unifies them: generation *given an intervention*, with a decoder matched to the data's likelihood. The method is modality-agnostic, and the conditional `v(z, t, c)` path is de-risked as a method; the applications are where it earns its keep: - **Single-cell perturbation response** *(flagship, WIP)*: a staged "cell JEPA": intra-cell pretraining (Stage A) → variational / conditional-flow perturbation predictor (Stage B) → NB/ZINB count decoder (Stage C), on Norman-2019 Perturb-seq, graded on *effect size* (predicting unseen gene combinations) against a from-scratch CVAE baseline. An action-operator transition, an oracle ceiling, a decoder calibration fix and an encoder co-adaptation program have since extended it. Training the encoder together with the decoder brought the full pipeline level with the from-scratch baseline on the size of the predicted change, though not yet on its correlation, and no learned model yet beats the training-free additive reference. The pretraining itself is not shown to contribute at full data, which leaves label- and data-scarce settings as the place where it has to earn its keep. The [results ledger](examples/perturbation_response/docs/results/index.md) tracks every round. - **Digital phenotyping**: e.g. diabetes monitoring and management, where the rollout becomes a *generative personal world model*: a fan of plausible future trajectories under an intervention (this is also where Direction 2's world model meets the generative line). - **Further modalities**: the core is a likelihood-matched conditional generator, so new domains drop in as data adapters; the [data-modalities primer](docs/generative_jepa/appendix-data-modalities.md) surveys single-cell counts, EHR codes, and wearable / CGM streams. **2. Action operators on JEPA: make prediction *active*.** *(research line: tutorial corpus written; theory still developing)* Go from passively in-filling hidden regions to *acting on* them. JEPA's predictor already *is* a latent operator, but its query is a **frozen, blind action**: it says only *where* or *when* to predict, never *what acted*. Promote that query to a **learned operator the model chooses and conditions on**, for both *sensing* ("where should I look?") and *perturbing* ("what happens under this intervention?"), and the passive predictor becomes a controllable **world model**: it can roll futures forward, run counterfactuals ("what if more sleep?"), and surface change that known interventions don't explain. This builds on the **action-operator** formalism from the sibling project [GRL](https://github.com/pleiadian53/GRL), and spans two application poles: continuous behavioral / mental-health monitoring (operator structure *learned*) and protein structure & dynamics (structure *given* by SE(3)). > 📄 **Tutorial series** (full math on the [documentation site](https://pleiadian53.github.io/ssl-lab/)): three parts, read in this order: > - **[Time-Series JEPA](docs/time_series_jepa/index.md)**: the substrate, covering JEPA pointed at time series, multimodal channels, and the one blind spot that motivates operators. Its first runnable instance is the [ECG rhythm study](examples/ecg_rhythm/README.md). > - **[Action Operators](docs/action_operator/00-from-actions-to-operators.md)**: the foundation, covering what an action operator is, why JEPA benefits from one, and a gallery of concrete operators. > - **[Operator World Models](docs/operator_world_models/index.md)**: the synthesis, which conditions the predictor on *what acted* for counterfactual rollout, composable interventions, and a sharpened change signal. > > *Status: an actively developing theoretical line whose operator formalism is still being worked out, not settled. It now reaches into Direction 1. The [Generative JEPA series](docs/generative_jepa/index.md) treats action-conditioning as the bridge: the conditional flow prior's condition can be an action, and Route D's planner is an action operator, so the generative and world-model lines are converging on one substrate.* A concrete motivation in genomics: given an RNA sequence, *sense* to localize candidate splice sites, then *perturb* (in-silico edits / mutations) to learn what they do to splicing. That is the kind of active, hypothesis-driven understanding passive prediction alone can't reach. ## Studies so far Two applied studies have run so far. Each is pre-registered, compares arms within one study, and reports uncertainty alongside every number. Besides their own questions, together they answer a narrower one: what JEPA pretraining buys over training the same model from scratch. - **[Single-cell perturbation response](examples/perturbation_response/README.md)** (Norman 2019 Perturb-seq, twenty held-out two-gene combinations). The task is to generate the perturbed cell population for gene combinations never measured. The generative stack, a JEPA cell encoder with a conditional flow and a count decoder, is graded against a from-scratch conditional NB-VAE and a training-free additive reference. At full data, the from-scratch baseline and additivity lead, and an encoder trained jointly with the decoder from random weights does at least as well as one started from the JEPA weights. The [results ledger](examples/perturbation_response/docs/results/index.md) holds every round. - **[ECG rhythm classification](examples/ecg_rhythm/README.md)** (PTB-XL, 21,799 twelve-lead ECGs). Span-masked JEPA pretraining is compared with the same encoder trained from scratch, at nested label budgets. With labels for 5% of training patients, pretraining adds 0.078 macro AUROC, and the advantage shrinks to a tie when every patient is labelled ([results](examples/ecg_rhythm/results/01-jepa-label-efficiency/README.md)). Read together, the two studies point the same way. Pretraining pays off when labels are scarce and fades when they are plentiful, so label and data efficiency is the axis on which the perturbation study's pretraining is still to be tested. ## Related projects ssl-lab sits in a small constellation of related work: - **[genai-lab](https://github.com/pleiadian53/genai-lab)**: the parent project, focused on generative AI for computational biology. ssl-lab matures methods here and feeds them back to genai-lab for genomic generative models. - **[NMDiff](https://github.com/pleiadian53/nmdiff)**: a **distinct branch of SSL** that sits outside the three classical families. Contrastive (SimCLR/CLIP), predictive (BERT/GPT/MAE), and self-distillation (BYOL/DINO) methods all share one structural property: the labeling function `T` is *fixed*, and only the encoder is learned. NMDiff promotes `T` itself to a domain-parameterized hypothesis `L(·; θ)` and jointly optimizes it with the downstream classifier via an outer-loop cross-view AUC criterion. The labeling function isn't a hyperparameter; it *is* the scientific hypothesis. Call it **hypothesis-driven SSL**: applied to transcript NMD efficiency (where ground-truth labels don't exist), but the pattern generalizes to any label-scarce setting where domain knowledge can parameterize a candidate labeling. Within the 2026 macro-trend of *learning the supervision signal itself*, which also includes self-improving SSL, learned-augmentation SSL, and programmatic weak supervision, NMDiff is the interpretable, low-dimensional, domain-knowledge instance. - **[GRL](https://github.com/pleiadian53/GRL)**: origin of the action-operator formalism that grounds the action-operator research direction above. - **[protein-ml-lab](https://github.com/pleiadian53/protein-ml-lab)** *(sibling, early work in progress)*: new methods for protein modeling and design across the protein-ML stack (ESM, the AlphaFold lineage, RFdiffusion / ProteinMPNN / Chroma). It is the natural home for the action operator's **"given" pole**: there the operators are the rotations and translations of a molecule in 3D space, honest **SE(3)** group elements known in advance, so equivariance is *demanded* rather than learned, and frame-based structure prediction and generation are *operators on SE(3)* made literal (AlphaFold's residue frames, FrameDiff/RFdiffusion flows). Where ssl-lab's operators are **learned** from data, protein-ml-lab's are **known in advance**. These are the two poles of the same expressiveness↔structure dial, in two sibling repos. - **[tabular-icl-lab](https://github.com/pleiadian53/tabular-icl-lab)** *(sibling, early work in progress)*: tabular foundation models and in-context learning (TabPFN) for computational biology, as strong small-data references, evaluation probes and carriers of domain priors. Its first route asks whether a tabular in-context learner can predict what additivity misses in the perturbation study. ## Layout This project follows a use-case-driven R&D convention: reusable primitives in `src/`, thin driver scripts in `examples/`, intuition in `notebooks/`. ``` src/ssllab/ data/ image-proxy, single-cell Perturb-seq and PTB-XL ECG adapters -> modality-agnostic token tensors (signal geometry in physical time; a checksummed WFDB reader) models/ TinyViT backbone, JEPA encoder/predictor, latent decoder jepa/ block masking, EMA target, the assembled JEPA module objectives/ prediction loss + VICReg collapse regularizer generative/ flow prior (unconditional + conditional w/ classifier-free guidance), NB/ZINB count decoder, condition encoder, CVAE baseline, perturbation action operator (+ operator algebra) action_operator/ context-conditioned latent operators — generator bases, exp(M) eval/ collapse diagnostics, linear probe, effect size, calibration and population metrics, interaction scores, joint paired bootstrap with max-t intervals, image-grid viz coadapt.py joint encoder + decoder training (decoder only, joint, joint with the JEPA anchor) anatomy/ step-by-step shape traces of every component, for the architecture viewer utils/ seeding, device selection examples/ jepa_basics/ 01 train JEPA · 02 linear probe generative_jepa/ 03 decoder · 04 flow prior · 05 sample · 06 eval · 07 conditional flow · 08 sample conditional (image proxy) perturbation_response/ cell-JEPA perturbation pipeline (WIP): process Norman -> Stage A pretrain -> count decoder -> conditional flow or action operator -> sample -> effect-size eval (+ CVAE and additive references, ceiling analysis, one scoring script per pre-registered round); co-adaptation/ trains the encoder with the stages that read it ecg_rhythm/ PTB-XL: process -> data card -> labelled-patient subsets -> span-masked JEPA pretraining -> scratch / fine-tune / probe arms -> paired patient-cluster bootstrap -> results page ``` ## Setup ```bash mamba env create -f environment.yml # or: conda env create -f environment.yml conda activate ssllab pip install -e . ``` ## Run the vertical slice ```bash # 1. learn the representation (prints collapse diagnostics each epoch) python examples/jepa_basics/01_train_jepa_mnist.py --epochs 5 # 2. confirm the frozen latent is semantically useful python examples/jepa_basics/02_linear_probe.py # 3. learn to decode the frozen latent back to pixels python examples/generative_jepa/03_train_decoder.py --epochs 5 # 4. learn a sampleable prior over the frozen latent python examples/generative_jepa/04_train_flow_prior.py --epochs 20 # 5. sample z ~ prior, decode -> output/jepa_mnist/samples/samples.png python examples/generative_jepa/05_sample_and_decode.py ``` Artifacts are organized per experiment under `output//`: ``` output/jepa_mnist/ checkpoints/ encoder.pt decoder.pt prior.pt samples/ samples.png recon.png reports/ jepa_train.json probe.json logs/ train.log ``` On a GPU pod this same tree is written under the network volume (`/runpod-volume/ssl-lab/output//`) and rsynced back to the local `output/`: same structure, env-dependent prefix swapped. All scripts share an `--experiment` name (default `jepa_mnist`); pass a new name to keep separate runs side by side. On a GPU pod, the whole chain runs via `examples/generative_jepa/run_pod_pipeline.sh`. ## Remote training Models that don't fit in your local environment train on remote GPU pods. That infra lives in a separate, decoupled package [`ops/`](ops/) (SkyPilot + RunPod) at the repository root: the SSL library never imports it, and it is used from the root without being installed. Quick path: ```bash pip install -e '.[ops]' # PyYAML for compute-check + dry-run python examples/ops/ops_compute_check.py # local vs pod? python examples/ops/ops_run_pipeline.py --gpu a40 -- \ python examples/jepa_basics/01_train_jepa_mnist.py --epochs 50 # dry-run ``` See [ops/README.md](ops/README.md) for the full provision → run → fetch workflow.
