# Biology Foundation Model 학습 로드맵

생물학 foundation model(FM)을 **중급에서 전문가 수준**까지 혼자 학습하기 위한 자료다.
대상은 ML·생물학 기초가 이미 있는 학습자이고, 형식은 Markdown 강의노트와 Jupyter 실습이다.

웹 책(목차·검색 지원): <https://wgsim.github.io/biology-foundation-model-learning/> · English: [README.en.md](README.en.md)

## 실행 등급
| 표시 | 환경 |
|---|---|
| 🟢 | Mac 로컬 (CPU/MPS) |
| 🟡 | Google Colab GPU (T4급, 캡스톤 시험 실행 한 건만 A100) |
| 🔴 | 기관 GPU 클러스터 |

환경 설정은 [SETUP.md](SETUP.md)를 참고한다. 목차·검색이 있는 웹 책으로 보려면 SETUP.md §6(`bash book/build.sh`)을 따른다.

## 18주 일정 (주 8~10시간 기준)
| 주차 | 모듈 | 핵심 목표 |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | [00_orientation](00_orientation/) | 자가진단, 논문 읽기·재현 방법 |
| 1–2 | [01_foundations](01_foundations/) | 서열 토크나이징, 목적함수, 평가 함정(데이터 누수) |
| 3–6 | [02_protein](02_protein/) | PLM, 구조 예측, 설계, 변이 효과 예측 |
| 7–9 | [03_dna_genome](03_dna_genome/) | DNA/RNA 언어모델, sequence-to-function |
| 10–12 | [04_single_cell](04_single_cell/) | 단일세포 FM과 baseline 대비 비판적 평가 |
| 13–14 | [05_multimodal_other](05_multimodal_other/) | 분자·이미지·멀티모달·생물학 LLM |
| 15–16 | [06_advanced_research](06_advanced_research/) | 파인튜닝, 해석, 효율화, 벤치마크 설계 |
| 17–18 | [07_capstone](07_capstone/) | 프로젝트 또는 논문 재현 |

## 수준 체크포인트
- **중급 완료 (2~9주 후)**: 임베딩+probe, zero-shot 변이 점수화를 직접 구현하고 split 누수를 설명할 수 있다.
- **고급 (10~16주 후)**: FM과 단순 baseline을 공정하게 비교하는 평가를 설계할 수 있다.
- **전문가 (캡스톤)**: 논문 1편을 재현하거나 새 평가/적용 실험을 수행하고 한계를 서술할 수 있다.

## 각 모듈 구성
`README.md`(강의노트) · `notebooks/`(실습) · `exercises.md`(과제)

모듈마다 산출물 1개(단순 baseline 재현 / split 변경 효과 확인 / 동결 표현 vs 미세조정 비교 중 하나)와 데이터 누출 점검 항목을 포함한다. 자세한 내용은 [resources/reading_list.md](resources/reading_list.md)의 운영 메모를 참고한다. 용어는 [glossary](resources/glossary.md), 벤치마크는 [benchmarks](resources/benchmarks.md), 반복 패턴은 [cheatsheets](resources/cheatsheets/)에 있다.

## 진행 상태
- [x] 스캐폴드
- [x] 1차 문헌 검증 및 `resources/reading_list.md` (v2: Codex·agy 교차 검토 반영)
- [x] 모듈 00 오리엔테이션
- [x] 모듈 01 Foundations (강의노트·과제·노트북 3종, 실행 확인)
- [x] 모듈 02 Protein (강의노트·과제·노트북 4종: 01–03은 Mac에서, 04는 Colab T4에서 실행 확인)
- [x] 모듈 03 DNA·Genome (강의노트·과제·노트북 3종 모두 Mac에서 실행 확인, 노트북 03은 격리 환경)
- [x] 모듈 04 Single-cell (강의노트·과제·노트북 3종 모두 Mac에서 실행 확인, Colab T4에서도 01–03 실행 확인)
- [x] 모듈 05 Multimodal·기타 (강의노트·과제·노트북 2종 모두 Mac에서 실행 확인, Colab T4에서도 2종 모두 실행 확인, 시간은 Mac의 3~6배)
- [x] 모듈 06 Advanced (강의노트·과제·노트북 3종 Mac에서 실행 확인, Colab T4에서도 01–03 실행 확인. DDP 템플릿은 CPU 2프로세스로만 검증했고 SLURM 파일은 문법 점검만 했다. 클러스터는 미검증이다)
- [x] 모듈 07 Capstone: 제안서·보고서·루브릭·점검표·검토 프롬프트 템플릿을 만들었다. 실행되는 템플릿 노트북 1종은 Mac과 Colab T4에서 실행을 확인했다. 트랙 B~D는 MVP 하나씩을 캐시로 시험 실행했다([기록](07_capstone/examples/dry_runs/README.md)). 질문의 나머지 절반도 대부분 시험 실행했고([기록](07_capstone/examples/dry_runs/second_halves.md)), Geneformer V2-104M 미세조정만 Colab A100에서 학습했다. 트랙 E는 TraitGym 한 편을 시험 실행했다([기록](07_capstone/examples/dry_runs/track_E_traitgym.md)). 시험 실행은 모두 학습자 파일럿이 아니다. 새 모델은 scGPT whole-human 체크포인트 하나(약 207 MB, 소스 26개는 설치 없이 사용)이고, 새 데이터는 MoleculeNet CSV 3개(약 3.9 MB), TraitGym 지표 CSV 22개(2 KB), CELLxGENE H5AD 1개(150 MB)뿐이다.
- [x] resources 보강: [용어집](resources/glossary.md) · [벤치마크 지도](resources/benchmarks.md) · [치트시트 4종](resources/cheatsheets/) (코드 블록은 `.venv`에서 실행 확인). 전체 DOI·arXiv ID 125개와 상대 링크 147개를 점검했다. 이후 문서가 늘어 2026-11-10에 상대 링크 208개와 앵커를 다시 점검했고 깨진 것은 없었다. DOI는 다시 대조하지 않았다. 외부 URL 10개 중 4개는 자리표시자·디렉터리 주소다.

> 최신 모델·논문 정보는 작성 시 문헌 DB로 확인하며, 확인되지 않은 항목은 `⚠️ 미검증`으로 표시한다.

## 작성 방식과 한계
- 문서와 코드는 AI 코딩 도구(Anthropic의 Claude Code)로 작성했다. 커밋마다 `Co-Authored-By` 표기가 남아 있다. 각 모듈의 계획과 외부 다운로드는 저자가 승인한 뒤 진행했다.
- 교차 검토는 다른 AI 모델(OpenAI Codex, Google Gemini)이 했다. 사람 전문가의 검토와 학습자 파일럿은 하지 않았다.
- 오류가 남아 있을 수 있다. 인용한 수치와 주장은 원문으로 다시 확인해야 한다.

## 라이선스
- 코드와 문서는 모두 MIT 라이선스(`LICENSE`)다.
- 이 저장소에는 외부 모델 가중치와 데이터가 들어 있지 않다. 노트북이 실행 중에 내려받는 모델과 데이터는 각 출처의 라이선스를 따른다. 논문의 표·그림에서 읽은 값은 저장소에 두지 않는다. 확인한 근거와 확인하지 못한 항목은 [06 강의노트](06_advanced_research/README.md)의 "데이터·모델 라이선스와 연구 책임성" 절에 있다.

one_liner: 该仓库是一个基于CellRank的scRNA-seq细胞命运动力学AI推理基准测试，用于评估大语言模型和Agent在细胞状态转换推理上的能力，与课题方向高度相关但本身不提供模型训练或Agent实现。

## 是什么

这是一个用于评估前沿 AI 智能体（Agent）和大型语言模型（LLM）在计算生物学领域推理能力的基准测试仓库。它基于 CellRank 2.0 和单细胞 RNA 测序（scRNA-seq）数据，设计了一个完全确定性的、包含陷阱的基准任务，要求 AI 模型自主推断并执行复杂的细胞命运连续转变动力学，而非简单的伪时间相关性或静态差异表达。

## 亮点

- **确定性基准设计**：通过严格的随机种子管理，实现了跨 ARM64 和 x86_64 架构的完全可复现结果，确保评估的公平性和可验证性。
- **陷阱机制**：精心设计了三种类型的陷阱（静态差异表达、一维伪时间、CellRank API 误用），能够有效区分真正的科学推理与简单的指令遵循。
- **自动化评估**：提供了 `evaluator.py` 和 `test_traps.py`，实现自动化的评分和陷阱验证，支持大小写不敏感、多路径搜索和结构化失败诊断。
- **完整依赖锁定**：通过 `requirements.txt` 和 `pyproject.toml` 锁定了 scverse 生态的依赖版本，确保环境可复现。
- **多架构验证**：在 Apple Silicon 和 Intel/AMD 平台上均验证了基准的确定性，展示了单细胞随机算法在适当种子管理下的跨平台一致性。

## 为何对本课题有用

本仓库直接面向「虚拟细胞/虚拟器官 × 单细胞/空间组学 × 生物基座模型、生物大语言模型、Bio Agent」课题，具有以下核心价值：

- **评估 Bio Agent 的科学推理能力**：提供了一个严格的基准，用于测试生物大语言模型或 AI 智能体是否能够自主进行复杂的细胞命运动力学推理，而非仅仅执行指令。这对于构建和验证虚拟细胞模型中的智能体至关重要。
- **方法论借鉴**：展示了如何设计一个“陷阱重重”的基准，以区分真正的科学推理与表面上的指令遵循。这一方法论可直接迁移到其他生物基座模型的评估中，例如评估模型在空间组学数据上的推理能力。
- **数据与任务设计**：使用了真实的单细胞数据（小鼠髓系祖细胞分化），并提出了一个明确的生物学问题（识别驱动命运决定的基因），这为虚拟细胞模型提供了可复用的任务模板。
- **确定性计算流程**：提供了完整的确定性解决方案（`solution.py`），可作为虚拟细胞模型中细胞命运预测模块的参考实现。

## 怎么用

- **主入口文件**：`solution.py`（参考实现）、`evaluator.py`（评分器）、`test_traps.py`（陷阱验证）。
- **安装依赖**：运行 `pip install -r requirements.txt`，依赖包括 `scanpy`、`cellrank`、`anndata`、`numpy`、`scipy`、`pandas`、`python-igraph`、`leidenalg` 等。
- **运行参考实现**：执行 `python solution.py`，约 25 秒生成 `output/answer.json`。
- **运行评分器**：执行 `python evaluator.py`，输出 JSON 格式的评分结果。
- **运行陷阱验证**：执行 `python test_traps.py`，验证黄金解通过、陷阱被捕获。
- **输入数据**：`data/myeloid_clean.h5ad`，包含 2,730 个细胞 × 3,451 个基因的原始计数矩阵，已去除预计算的图表示和注释。
- **是否需要 GPU**：README 未说明，但基于 CellRank 和单细胞数据规模，CPU 即可运行，GPU 非必需。
- **调试入口**：可参考 `test_traps.py` 中的测试用例，或直接运行 `solution.py` 并断点调试。

## 核心 idea

核心方法学洞察在于：**通过抽象化任务提示，迫使 AI 模型自主选择正确的计算路径（如构建连续转移核、使用 GPCCA 进行宏观态分解），从而将“指令遵循”与“科学推理”区分开来**。这一设计使得基准能够真正评估模型对细胞命运动力学深层原理的理解，而非表面上的 API 调用能力。

## 可搬移点

- **陷阱设计模式**：`test_traps.py` 中的陷阱实现（静态差异表达、一维伪时间、API 误用）可以直接复制到其他生物基座模型的评估 Pipeline 中，用于测试模型的鲁棒性和推理深度。
- **确定性计算流程**：`solution.py` 中的 CellRank 2.0 使用流程（构建核、计算 Schur 分解、计算命运概率、相关性分析）可作为虚拟细胞模型中细胞命运预测模块的参考实现，可逐步替换或集成。
- **评分器逻辑**：`evaluator.py` 中的评分规则（规则 1：schema 验证；规则 2：基因匹配；规则 3：相关性容差）可迁移到其他需要严格评估的生物学任务中。
- **许可证**：仓库采用 BSD-3-Clause 许可证，允许自由使用和修改，但需保留版权声明。具体可搬移模块的许可证需确认，但整体上 BSD-3-Clause 对学术和商业使用友好。

# CellRank Single-Cell Lineage Dynamics Benchmark
### *A Rigorous Frontier AI Reasoning Benchmark in Computational Biology*

[![scverse](https://img.shields.io/badge/ecosystem-scverse-blue.svg)](https://scverse.org/)
[![CellRank](https://img.shields.io/badge/toolkit-CellRank_2.0-brightgreen.svg)](https://cellrank.readthedocs.io/)
[![Reproducibility](https://img.shields.io/badge/reproducibility-deterministic-orange.svg)]()
[![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-BSD--3--Clause-lightgrey.svg)](LICENSE)

---

## 🔬 Overview

This benchmark evaluates autonomous AI agents and Frontier Large Language Models (LLMs) on high-level computational biology reasoning. Specifically, it tests whether an AI model can deduce and execute complex continuous transition dynamics on single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data rather than relying on trivial 1D pseudotime correlations or static differential expression.

Evaluating frontier AI models on scientific tasks presents a fundamental challenge: **detailed scientific prompts often turn evaluation tasks into simple instruction-following rather than genuine domain reasoning.** This repository demonstrates how to design a fully deterministic, trap-laden, and multi-architecture reproducible benchmark for evaluating AI agents on Markovian cell fate dynamics.

---

## 🧬 Biological Context & Dataset

* **Biological System:** Early murine myeloid progenitor differentiation (Paul et al., *Cell* 2015).
* **Data Dimensions:** 2,730 cells × 3,451 genes stored in `data/myeloid_clean.h5ad`.
* **Preprocessing Hygiene:** All pre-computed graph representations, PCA reductions, and AnnData annotations (`.uns`, `.obsm`, `.obsp`) were stripped. Models must construct their own deterministic graphs and state spaces from raw counts.
* **Core Biological Question:** In a bifurcating/trifurcating differentiation landscape, which gene acts as the primary lineage driver governing fate commitment toward mature terminal state `"0"`?

---

## 🎯 Ground Truth & Traps

The benchmark contains an exact, mathematically reproducible ground truth verified across both **ARM64** (Apple Silicon) and **x86_64** (Intel/AMD) platforms.

### Ground Truth Solution (`solution.py`)
* **Terminal State:** `"0"`
* **Primary Driver Gene:** `Id2`
* **Correlation with Fate Commitment:** `0.7579` (Pass tolerance: `[0.74, 0.78]`)
* **Deterministic Execution Time:** ~25 seconds

```json
{
  "terminal_state": "0",
  "top_driver_gene": "Id2",
  "correlation": 0.7579
}
```

### Engineered Biological & Architectural Traps

| Trap Type | Failure Mode / Model Mistake | Erroneous Output | Evaluation Result |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Trap 1: Static DE** | Model performs standard static differential expression (`sc.tl.rank_genes_groups`) between terminal clusters, completely ignoring continuous directional dynamics. | Gene: `Ccl5` | ❌ **FAIL** (Rule 2) |
| **Trap 2: 1D Pseudotime** | Model computes diffusion pseudotime (DPT) and correlates genes globally across the whole manifold, missing branch-specific fate absorption probabilities. | Gene: `Cd74`, corr: `~0.477` | ❌ **FAIL** (Rule 2 & 3) |
| **Trap 3: CellRank 2.x API** | Model assumes CellRank returns standard pandas DataFrames and attempts `.to_df()` on internal `Lineage` objects, triggering runtime errors. | Runtime Exception | ❌ **FAIL** (Rule 1) |

---

## 🔄 Evolution of this Benchmark: Lessons in Frontier AI Difficulty Calibration

> *"The request spells out every step, including correlating each gene with the fate probabilities toward state '0'... so there is nothing left for a model to work out. Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.1 Sol gave Id2 at 0.7579 in all 6 of our runs."*  
> — **Anubhav Malik**, CTO & Co-founder at Weekday (YC W21)

Designing evaluations for frontier AI models requires a delicate balance between **task specification** and **autonomous reasoning space**.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph v1["Version 1 (Initial Submission): Over-Specified"]
        A1["Raw Count Matrix"] --> B1["Explicitly compute Schur Decomposition"]
        B1 --> C1["Explicitly compute Fate Probabilities"]
        C1 --> D1["Explicitly correlate genes with state 0"]
        D1 --> E1["Frontier LLMs: 100% Pass@k (Instruction Following)"]
    end
```

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph v2["Version 2 (Hardened Benchmark): Goal-Driven Reasoning"]
        A2["Raw Count Matrix"] --> B2{"Autonomous Reasoning Choice"}
        B2 -- "Static DE?" --> C2["Trap: Ccl5 ❌"]
        B2 -- "1D Pseudotime?" --> D2["Trap: Cd74 ❌"]
        B2 -- "Dynamic Kernel & GPCCA" --> E2["Correct Fate Dynamics: Id2 (0.7579) ✅"]
    end
```

### Key Takeaways from v1 to v2:
1. **Instruction Following $\neq$ Scientific Reasoning:** When a prompt specifies exact library methods (`PseudotimeKernel`, `compute_schur`, `compute_fate_probabilities`), state-of-the-art models like Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.1 Sol act as deterministic syntax compilers rather than autonomous scientific agents, passing 6/6 runs effortlessly ($Pass@6 = 1.0$).
2. **Abstracting the Prompt (v2):** In v2 (`request.md`), the prompt only provides the overarching biological goal and minimal preprocessing hygiene. The model must independently decide to:
   * Construct a continuous transition kernel rather than a static graph.
   * Compute coarse-grained macrostates via generalized Perron Cluster Cluster Analysis (GPCCA).
   * Solve absorption probabilities to quantify lineage drivers.
3. **Flawless Multi-Architecture Determinism:** The ground truth reproducibility was confirmed across both ARM and Intel hardware architectures, proving that single-cell stochastic algorithms can achieve absolute cross-platform determinism with proper seed hygiene.

### 📊 Comprehensive Changelog: Version 1 (v1) vs Version 2 (v2)

| Component | Version 1 (v1 Initial Submission) | Evaluator Findings (Weekday Review) | Version 2 (v2 Hardened Benchmark) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Prompt (`request.md`)** | Explicitly spelled out intermediate API steps (computing Schur decomposition, calculating absorption probabilities, correlating specifically with state "0"). | Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.1 Sol passed 6/6 runs ($Pass@6 = 1.0$) because they followed instructions rather than reasoning. | **Fully Abstracted:** Removed all intermediate API clues and formulas. Models must autonomously deduce the need for continuous transition kernels and GPCCA. |
| **Biological Ground Truth** | Deterministic pipeline (`Id2` @ `0.7579`). | **Reproduced 100% identically** on both ARM64 (Apple Silicon) and x86_64 (Intel) hardware in ~25 seconds. | Kept identical. The core mathematical pipeline was verified by evaluators as flawless. |
| **Trap Mechanisms** | Engineered Trap 1 (`Ccl5` static DE) and Trap 2 (`Cd74` @ `0.477` global pseudotime). | **Both traps confirmed:** Evaluators reproduced `Ccl5` and `Cd74` exactly at 0.477. | Documented and formalized into an automated test harness. |
| **Automated Testing (`test_traps.py`)** | Missing live verification test scripts. | Evaluator noted no automated model run proof attached in the package. | **Added `test_traps.py`:** Standalone test suite executing the golden solution and both traps, asserting automatic grading. |
| **Environment & Dependencies** | No standalone `requirements.txt` included. | Evaluator had to infer runtime dependencies from their internal bioinformatics setup. | **Added `requirements.txt`:** Fully pinned scverse stack (`scanpy`, `cellrank`, `anndata`, `scipy`, `leidenalg`). |
| **Evaluation Grader (`evaluator.py`)** | Strict case-sensitive matching and fixed path (`output/answer.json`). | Risk of false negative if model outputs valid answer with minor formatting variation. | **Hardened Grader:** Case-insensitive (`Id2`/`id2`), multi-path search, and structured failure diagnosis. |

---

## 📁 Repository Structure

```
├── data/
│   └── myeloid_clean.h5ad      # Raw count scRNA-seq matrix (Paul et al. 2015)
├── repo/                       # Embedded scverse/cellrank codebase
├── request.md                  # Goal-driven benchmark prompt given to AI agents
├── solution.py                 # Golden reference implementation (deterministic)
├── evaluator.py                # Automated 3-stage validation and scoring harness
├── test_traps.py               # Automated verification suite testing solution & traps
├── grading_rules.md            # Detailed grading criteria and biological rationale
├── requirements.txt            # Reproducible environment dependencies
└── README.md                   # Benchmark documentation
```

---

## 🚀 Quickstart

### 1. Installation
```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

### 2. Running the Reference Solution
```bash
python solution.py
```
This generates `output/answer.json` with the golden solution in ~25s.

### 3. Running the Grader / Evaluator
```bash
python evaluator.py
```
Expected output:
```json
{
  "score": 1.0,
  "passed_all": true,
  "rule_1_schema": true,
  "rule_2_gene": true,
  "rule_3_correlation": true,
  "failure_reason": null
}
```

### 4. Running the Trap Verification Suite
```bash
python test_traps.py
```
Verifies that:
* The Golden Solution passes with `score: 1.0`.
* Trap 1 (`Ccl5`) is caught and fails with `score: 0.0`.
* Trap 2 (`Cd74`) is caught and fails with `score: 0.0`.

---

## 📜 Citation & Acknowledgements
- **Paul et al. (2015):** *Cell*, "Transcriptional Heterogeneity and Lineage Commitment in Early Myeloid Progenitors"
- **Lange et al. (2022):** *Nature Methods*, "CellRank for directed single-cell fate mapping"
- **Evaluation Feedback:** Special thanks to Anubhav Malik (CTO, Weekday / YC W21) for evaluation benchmarking insights.

## 是什么

Thalamus-Decision 是一个**带生物模态的、类型化决策模型**（typed decision model），用于生物学和医学领域。它读取 bulk 和单细胞表达谱以及文本/JSON 记录，回答带校准概率的封闭式问题（choice / yes-no / score），并给出自动化或转人工的建议。当前发布版本为 Thalamus-Decision-9B，基于 Thalamus-Reasoning-9B 微调而来。本仓库是推理引擎，包含 HTTP API、MCP 服务器、Python API、客户端和评估脚本，训练代码与数据未发布。

## 亮点

- **类型化输出**：模型输出固定类型的答案（choice / yes-no / score），并附带校准概率，而非自由文本，便于下游自动化决策。
- **双模态输入**：同时处理文本和表达谱（20,029 维向量），支持 DepMap 细胞系名称和自定义样本 ID 引用。
- **校准与自动化决策**：通过温度缩放校准概率，并基于验证集认证置信度阈值，实现 5% 或 1% 目标误差下的自动化/转人工判断。
- **高效推理**：支持 FlashAttention 2、flash-linear-attention 和 causal-conv1d 的 packed readout，显著提升吞吐量（27 decisions/s on H100）。
- **工程完备**：提供 HTTP API、MCP 服务器（支持 Claude Code 等 agent）、Python API 和标准库客户端，易于集成。
- **可复现评估**：提供评估脚本和基准测试，与 Thalamus-Reasoning 对比，验证了决策质量。

## 为何对本课题有用

本仓库直接面向**生物基座模型 × 单细胞/空间组学**方向，是构建**虚拟细胞/虚拟器官**决策层的关键组件：

- **决策层集成**：虚拟细胞模型（如基于单细胞数据的基座模型）可输出表达谱向量，Thalamus-Decision 提供类型化决策接口，将模型输出转化为可操作的生物学结论（如细胞类型、组织来源、疾病亚型），适合作为 Bio Agent 的决策模块。
- **多模态对齐**：其将表达谱（20,029 维）与文本指令结合的方式，为虚拟细胞模型与自然语言交互提供了范式，可迁移至空间组学数据的多模态推理。
- **校准与不确定性**：虚拟细胞模型在临床或科研应用中需要可靠的不确定性估计，本仓库的校准和自动化/转人工机制可直接借鉴，提升决策可信度。
- **Agent 集成**：MCP 服务器支持 Claude Code 等 agent，为 Bio Agent 提供标准接口，可快速接入虚拟细胞模型的推理结果。
- **评估基准**：其评估方法（AUROC、准确率）和基准集（Tabula Sapiens、GEO-OmicsQA）为虚拟细胞模型的决策能力评估提供参考。

## 怎么用

**安装与依赖**：
- 需要 Linux + NVIDIA GPU（≥24 GB）、Python 3.11–3.13。
- 使用 `uv sync --extra fast --extra mcp --extra eval` 或 `pip install -e ".[fast,mcp,eval]"`。
- 依赖 `thalamus-reasoning`（git 固定版本）、PyTorch 2.13、transformers 5.5.3 等。

**主入口与运行**：
- **Python API**：
  ```python
  from thalamus_decision import ThalamusDecision
  td = ThalamusDecision.load()  # 从 $THALAMUS_DECISION_HOME 或 HuggingFace 加载
  td.ask("Which line has the more mesenchymal expression program?", ["Line A", "Line B"],
         state="Line A: MCF7\nLine B: MDA-MB-231")
  ```
- **HTTP 服务器**：`uv run td-serve --model ingenius/Thalamus-Decision-9B --profiles mine.npz --port 8000`，提供 `POST /v1/decide` 等接口。
- **MCP 服务器**：`td-mcp` 命令，支持 HTTP 和 stdio 传输，可集成到 Claude Code。

**数据准备**：
- 使用 `tr-embed` 将表达谱（GEO counts、TPM、.h5ad）转换为 20,029 维向量，输出 `.npz` 文件和报告。
- 支持 DepMap 细胞系名称（如 MCF7）和自定义样本 ID（`@GSM1001`）。

**测试与调试**：
- 运行 `TD_TEST_MODEL=/path/to/model uv run pytest -q`，测试覆盖 CPU 上的 profiles、请求、校准、HTTP、MCP。
- 评估脚本：`uv run python eval/benchmark.py --benchmark all`（需 GPU）。

## 核心 idea

**将表达谱编码为固定长度向量，并通过线性层映射为 prompt 中的一个 token，使 LLM 能够以类型化输出（choice/yes-no/score）进行决策，同时通过温度缩放和认证阈值实现校准的自动化/转人工判断。** 其核心创新在于：

- **表达谱的 token 化**：将 20,029 维向量（包含数据类型标志、19,260 个基因表达值、Geneformer 嵌入）通过线性层转换为单个 token，与文本指令无缝融合，实现多模态推理。
- **双序平均**：对选项顺序正反两次推理取平均，减少顺序偏差，提高决策稳定性。
- **校准与认证**：基于验证集对每个问题类型和类别进行温度缩放，并认证置信度阈值，确保自动化决策的误差可控。

## 可搬移点

- **表达谱编码模块**（`tr-embed` 和线性层映射）：可解耦用于将单细胞/空间组学数据转换为 LLM 可理解的 token，适用于虚拟细胞模型的输入编码。
- **类型化决策接口**（`ThalamusDecision.ask/decide`）：可移植到自定义 Pipeline，作为 Bio Agent 的决策层，支持 choice/yes-no/score 输出。
- **校准与阈值认证逻辑**（`calibration.py`）：可复用于任何需要不确定性估计的模型，提升虚拟细胞模型的可信度。
- **MCP 服务器**（`mcp_server.py`）：可扩展为 Bio Agent 的标准接口，连接虚拟细胞模型与外部工具。
- **评估框架**（`eval/benchmark.py`）：可借鉴其评估指标和基准集，用于虚拟细胞模型的决策能力评估。

**License**：代码为 Apache 2.0，模型权重为 Ingenix.ai License（需确认是否允许商用或修改），数据文件各有条款。搬移时需注意模型权重的许可限制。
readme:
# Thalamus-Decision

Thalamus-Decision is a typed decision model for biology and medicine. It reads bulk and single-cell expression
profiles alongside text and JSON records, and answers closed questions with calibrated probabilities:

- **choice**: one of 2–255 named options;
- **yes/no**;
- **score**: a level of an ordered scale.

With a target error of 5% or 1%, each answer also says whether it can be automated or should go to a person. The
current release is Thalamus-Decision-9B.

[Model on Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/ingenix/Thalamus-Decision-9B) · [Thalamus-Reasoning](https://github.com/IngenixAI/Thalamus-Reasoning) · Paper: *Thalamus-Decision: A Typed Decision Model with a Biological Modality* (preprint in preparation)

This repository holds the inference engine: an HTTP API and MCP server, a Python API, a small client and the
evaluation scripts. The training code and training data are not released.

## Thalamus-Decision and Thalamus-Reasoning

Thalamus-Decision is built on [Thalamus-Reasoning](https://github.com/IngenixAI/Thalamus-Reasoning): Thalamus-Decision-9B
is fine-tuned from [Thalamus-Reasoning-9B](https://huggingface.co/ingenix/Thalamus-Reasoning-9B) and reads expression
profiles in exactly the same way. The two models answer different kinds of requests:

| | Thalamus-Reasoning | Thalamus-Decision |
|---|---|---|
| Answers | free text: explanations, comparisons, conversations | one of the options you give, with a calibrated probability for each |
| Output per question | generated text | probabilities, the answer, its confidence, automate or defer at a target error |
| Cost | generation, token by token | one forward pass per option order, no generation |
| Typical use | exploring samples, asking open questions | pipelines and agents that need decisions they can act on or route to a person |
| Profiles | 20,029-value vectors from `tr-embed`; DepMap cell lines by name; `@sample_id` | the same vectors, files and references |

The engine installs the `thalamus-reasoning` package and uses its code for every step that touches a profile:
- `tr-embed` builds profile vectors from your own data;
- `thalamus_reasoning.load_profiles` reads `.npz` files;
- the DepMap resolver finds cell lines by name;
- `tr-chat`'s message preparation places profiles in text.

The model repository carries the same `preprocessing/`, `depmap/` and `eval/` files as Thalamus-Reasoning-9B. So a
profile you prepared for Thalamus-Reasoning means the same to Thalamus-Decision.

## Two ways to give the model a profile

**1. Name a cancer cell line.** The model repository includes expression profiles of 1,673 cell lines from DepMap.
Write a cell line in the question's state, and its profile is attached at its first mention:
- common spellings work: `MCF7`, `mcf-7`, `HCT 116`, `ACH-000019`, `CVCL_0031`;
- names that are also ordinary words or gene symbols (`RD`, `KELLY`) count only when written as `@RD` or "RD cells";
- lines that are not in DepMap (for example HEK293T) stay plain text.

These are the rules of Thalamus-Reasoning's chat.

**2. Use your own samples.** Convert your expression table (GEO counts, TPM, `.h5ad`) into profile vectors with
`tr-embed`, load them into the server or the Python API, and refer to the samples by ID (`@GSM1001`).

## Install

You need Linux with an NVIDIA GPU of at least 24 GB, and Python 3.11–3.13.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/IngenixAI/Thalamus-Decision.git && cd Thalamus-Decision
uv sync --extra fast --extra mcp --extra eval    # engine, packed readout kernels, MCP, evaluation
```

With pip: `pip install -e ".[fast,mcp,eval]"`.

The `fast` extra installs FlashAttention 2, flash-linear-attention and causal-conv1d. They give the packed readout
the model was calibrated with, and compile against your PyTorch. Without them every prompt runs on its own: the same
answers up to bf16 rounding, several times slower.

The lock pins PyTorch 2.13, the version FlashAttention 2.8 builds against. Where no prebuilt FlashAttention wheel
matches your CUDA and Python, it compiles from source: that needs the CUDA toolkit (`nvcc`) and a lot of memory, so limit
the parallel compile jobs, for example `MAX_JOBS=4 uv sync --extra fast --extra mcp --extra eval`.

Model files (about 19 GB) are downloaded from the Hub on first use. To fetch them ahead of time:

```bash
hf download ingenix/Thalamus-Decision-9B --local-dir Thalamus-Decision-9B
export THALAMUS_DECISION_HOME=$PWD/Thalamus-Decision-9B
```

## Prepare your own profiles

`tr-embed` comes with the `thalamus-reasoning` dependency and works exactly as in Thalamus-Reasoning:

```bash
uv run tr-embed GSE123_counts.tsv.gz --out mine.npz     # bulk: TPM, FPKM, read counts or CPM
uv run tr-embed cells.h5ad --out cells.npz               # single cells: raw counts
uv run tr-embed cells.h5ad --pseudobulk-by donor --out donors.npz
```

These files stand for your own data and are not in this repository.

What `tr-embed` does:
- matches your genes to the 19,260-gene panel;
- detects bulk vs single-cell data, and TPM vs read counts;
- normalizes as in training;
- writes the vectors (`mine.npz`) and a report (`mine.report.json`) with gene coverage and warnings.

Read the report before trusting answers. Also read Thalamus-Reasoning's
[data preparation guide](https://github.com/IngenixAI/Thalamus-Reasoning/blob/main/skills/thalamus-reasoning-prepare-profiles/SKILL.md);
preparing data correctly matters more than anything else.

## Use from Python

```python
from thalamus_decision import ThalamusDecision

td = ThalamusDecision.load()       # $THALAMUS_DECISION_HOME or ingenix/Thalamus-Decision-9B

# DepMap cell lines by name: their profiles are attached as in Thalamus-Reasoning's chat
td.ask("Which line has the more mesenchymal expression program?", ["Line A", "Line B"],
       state="Line A: MCF7\nLine B: MDA-MB-231")
# {"type": "choice", "choice": "Line B", "confidence": 0.999, "probabilities": {...}, ...}

# Your own samples, from tr-embed (mine.npz is your own file)
td.load_profiles("mine.npz")
td.ask("Which sample shows the stronger interferon response?", ["Sample A", "Sample B", "neither"],
       state="Sample A: @GSM1001\nSample B: @GSM1004", max_error=0.05)

# Several typed questions about one state
td.decide(state="Cell line: MCF7", questions={
    "tissue": {"type": "choice", "instructions": "Which tissue does this cell line come from?",
               "criteria": ["breast", "lung", "colon", "skin"], "max_error": 0.05},
    "er":     {"type": "noul", "instructions": "Is it oestrogen-receptor positive?"},
    "grade":  {"type": "score", "instructions": "How proliferative is it?",
               "criteria": ["low", "intermediate", "high"]}})
```

Explicit vectors work as in `ThalamusReasoning.ask`: put one `<omics>` per vector in the state and pass the vectors in
order (`state="Expression profile: <omics>", vectors=[v]`). `td.decide_batch([...])` answers many requests in shared
forwards.

## Serve: HTTP API and MCP

```bash
uv run td-serve --model ingenix/Thalamus-Decision-9B --profiles mine.npz --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000
# ... READY http://myhost:8000 (Thalamus-Decision-9B, calibration CALIBRATION.json, 12 samples)
```

- **Start-up.** Loading takes under a minute from a local copy. The warm-up then compiles the kernels for 12 packed
  shapes, about 3 minutes on an H100. `GET /health` answers `loading` (HTTP 503) until the `READY` line.
- **Security.** The server has no authentication: run it on a trusted network or behind an authenticating proxy.
- **Slurm.** `scripts/serve.sbatch` runs the server on one GPU and writes its URL to a file.

| option | default | what |
|---|---|---|
| `--model` | `$THALAMUS_DECISION_HOME`, else `ingenix/Thalamus-Decision-9B` | local folder or Hub repo id |
| `--profiles FILE.npz ...` | none | `tr-embed` outputs; their samples become `@sample_id` |
| `--profile-store DIR` | none | keeps uploaded samples across restarts |
| `--embed on\|off` | off | run `tr-embed` on uploaded tables on the server, as Thalamus-Reasoning's web app does |
| `--depmap on\|off` | on | resolve DepMap cell-line names |
| `--mcp on\|off` | on | MCP at `/mcp` |
| `--host`, `--port` | 127.0.0.1, 8000 | `--host 0.0.0.0` accepts other machines |
| `--log-decisions FILE` | none | one JSON line per request, without vectors |

### `POST /v1/decide`

A request is a `state` (text, or a JSON object) and named `questions`:

```bash
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/decide -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "state": "Sample A: @GSM1001\nSample B: @GSM1004",
  "questions": {"ifn": {"type": "choice", "instructions": "Which sample shows the stronger interferon response?",
                        "criteria": ["Sample A", "Sample B", "neither"], "max_error": 0.05}}}'
```

| question field | values |
|---|---|
| `type` | `choice`, `noul` (yes/no) or `score` (ordered levels, lowest first) |
| `instructions` | the question text |
| `criteria` | `choice`, `score`: a list of options, or `{key: description}`. `noul`: optional, `[what yes means, what no means]` |
| `max_error` | 0.05 or 0.01: adds a `decision` (automate or defer) |
| `category` | the threshold category for `max_error` (listed by `GET /v1/models`); default: by type |
| `rank` | k: also return the k most probable options |
| `raw` | true: also return the uncalibrated probabilities of both option orders |

Profiles go into a request in one of three ways:

| way | request | what the model sees |
|---|---|---|
| references (default) | `@sample_id` and cell-line names in `state` | the first mention of each gets its profile right after it (`MCF7<omics>`), as in Thalamus-Reasoning's chat |
| explicit vectors | `"vectors": [v1, v2]` (20,029 floats each, or base64 of little-endian float32) and one `<omics>` per vector in `state` | the state as written, as `ThalamusReasoning.ask(text, vectors)` |
| profile list | `"profiles": ["@GSM1001", "MCF7"]` | one line `Expression profile: <omics>` per profile before the state |

The response has, per question:
- `probabilities` (calibrated), the answer and its `confidence`;
- with `max_error`, a `decision`: `automated` true or false, the certified threshold, and the error measured on test
  data;
- `profiles.notes`: which samples and cell lines were attached.

`noul` is the probability of yes; `score` is the expected level, and `level` the most probable one.

**Other endpoints:**

| endpoint | what |
|---|---|
| `POST /v1/profiles` | add samples: `{"npz": base64 of a tr-embed .npz}`, `{"vectors": {id: [...]}}`, or (with `--embed on`) `{"table": base64, "filename": ...}` |
| `GET /v1/profiles`, `GET /v1/profiles/{id}` | the loaded samples |
| `GET /v1/lines?q=breast` | DepMap cell lines with a profile |
| `POST /v1/resolve` | which samples and cell lines a text names, without a decision |
| `GET /v1/models`, `GET /health` | model, calibration and categories; status |

`src/thalamus_decision/client.py` is a client that needs only the Python standard library. `td-client --url URL demo`
runs example requests.

### MCP (Claude Code and other agents)

```bash
# HTTP. Tools: decide, decide_many, resolve, list_profiles, find_cell_lines
claude mcp add --transport http thalamus-decision http://myhost:8000/mcp

# stdio bridge: also upload_profiles, which sends a tr-embed .npz from your machine
claude mcp add thalamus-decision-local -- uv run --directory /path/to/thamalus-decision td-mcp --url http://myhost:8000
```

## How a profile becomes a vector

Each profile is a 20,029-value vector, built by `tr-embed` as in Thalamus-Reasoning. A linear layer turns it into
one token of the prompt.

| Block | Size | Computation |
|---|---|---|
| Data-type flag | 1 | bulk = 0, single-cell (cells or pseudobulk) = 1; z-scored |
| Expression | 19,260 | panel genes → scale to 10⁶ total → log1p → minus per-gene training mean → ÷ 1.535 |
| Geneformer-V2-104M | 768 | `<cls>` embedding (second-to-last layer) of the rank-value-encoded profile; z-scored |

## Confidence and decisions

- **Two option orders.** Every question is read with the options in the given and in the reversed order, and the two
  are averaged.
- **Calibration.** The probabilities are temperature-scaled with the model's `CALIBRATION.json`: one temperature per
  question type, and for `choice` per number of options.
- **Thresholds.** For `max_error` 0.05 or 0.01, the confidence threshold is certified on held-out calibration data,
  per category (`omics choice`, `omics yes/no`, `biology text (pathways, ontologies)`, ...) or per type.
- **Defer.** `automated: false` means: send the case to a person.
- **The targets are not guarantees.** On shifted test data the realised error was 6.4% at the 5% target and 1.9% at
  the 1% target. Each answer's `decision` reports its category's test error and whether it held (`holds_on_test`).
- **Without profiles,** set `category` to the closest one (`GET /v1/models` lists them).

## Evaluation

**The evaluation subsets of the model repository.** These are the same files as in Thalamus-Reasoning-9B, asked as
typed decisions with the released vectors (`uv run python eval/benchmark.py --benchmark all`, about 6 minutes on one
H100):

| Task | Metric | Thalamus-Decision-9B | Thalamus-Reasoning-9B |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tabula Sapiens, cell type (top 20) | macro AUROC | 0.975 | 0.920 |
| Tabula Sapiens, tissue | macro AUROC | 0.915 | 0.874 |
| Human Diseases, disease subtype (229 labels) | macro AUROC | 0.965 | 0.943 |
| Human Diseases, tissue | macro AUROC | 0.994 | 0.987 |
| GEO-OmicsQA, yes/no (2 × 500 questions) | accuracy | 0.777 | 0.765 |

- **How each model answers.** Thalamus-Decision answers one `choice` question over all candidate labels, or one
  `noul` question. Thalamus-Reasoning's scores come from its card: it scores each label by log-likelihood and generates
  its yes/no answers.
- **No overlap with training.** None of these profiles or questions is in Thalamus-Decision's training data.

**Held-out decision sets** (the paper's test sets; macro accuracy, %):

| Benchmark | Thalamus-Decision-9B | MedDecider-9B |
|---|---|---|
| Biology questions about a measured sample (43 sets) | 83.0 | 40.0 (text only) |
| Ontology and pathway tasks (8 sets) | 94.1 | 77.0 |
| Public text-only biology benchmarks (10 sets) | 69.3 | 70.3 |
| Medicine (24 sets) | 72.2 | 70.8 |
| Follows a planted wrong answer (%, lower is better) | 16.1 | 56.8 |

**General decisions** (public suites written for typed decision APIs, sent in their own request shape; all items,
an unanswered item scores 0):

| Suite | Metric | Thalamus-Decision-9B | MedDecider-9B |
|---|---|---|---|
| OpenDecisions | capability | 69.3 | 65.1 |
| JevBench public v1.2 | capability | 65.4 | 63.4 |
| JevBench (Benchmark Heaven) | accuracy | 82.2 | 78.8 |
| JevBench mini (metamorphic) | coherence | 81.7 | 76.2 |
| Jev Skills | JevExtra | 77.0 | 60.0 |
| Jev Skills | Rules7 | 81.1 | 68.0 |
| DecideBench | mean of 3 modes | 93.6 | 93.9 |
| Decision Index 0.2.1 | index (chance-corrected, 0 = random) | 49.9 | 36.7 |
| jev-rerank-bench | 8 sets, nDCG@10 | 66.4 | 64.1 |
| rag-hallu-bench | macro AUROC ×100 | 89.7 | 90.2 |
| unsafe-eval | mean balanced accuracy | 83.6 | 82.1 |

MedDecider-9B can show at most 10 options; the 17% of Decision Index questions with more score 0 for it. The training data include the training splits of three Decision Index benchmarks (WinoGrande, ESCI, ContractNLI).

## Checks

```bash
TD_TEST_MODEL=/path/to/Thalamus-Decision-9B uv run pytest -q    # CPU: profiles, requests, calibration, HTTP, MCP
```

- **No weights needed.** The tests use only the model folder:
  `hf download ingenix/Thalamus-Decision-9B --exclude "*.safetensors"`.
- **Same profile handling.** They check, among other things, that cell-line names and `@samples` resolve exactly as
  in Thalamus-Reasoning's chat.
- **Same answers as the evaluation pipeline.** On 919 test items (82 profile sets and 10 text-only sets), the engine
  matched the probabilities the model's calibration was fitted on: 100% of top answers, largest difference 2.3e-6.
  It then ran at 27 decisions/s on one H100.
- **`tr-embed` vectors.** With every profile in the form `tr-embed` writes, the 82 held-out profile sets scored as in
  the evaluation pipeline (+0.06 points, 95% CI −0.10 to +0.23).

## Limitations

- For research only, not for clinical decisions.
- Human RNA-seq only. Microarrays, other assays and other species are out of distribution. `tr-embed` checks the
  input and reports what it detected and any problems; read its report before trusting answers.
- The model chooses among the options you give; it does not explain or generate text. Offer "cannot be determined"
  when the state may not contain the answer.
- Its general knowledge is that of a 9B model. Put the facts and rules it needs into the state, and compute dates
  and numbers in code.
- DepMap profiles describe cancer cell lines in culture, not tumours.

## Support

Questions and bug reports: issues in this repository. Contact: [info@ingenix.ai](mailto:info@ingenix.ai).

## License

Code is released under the [Apache License 2.0](LICENSE) (see [NOTICE](NOTICE)). The model weights are released
under the [Ingenix.ai License](https://huggingface.co/ingenix/Thalamus-Decision-9B/blob/main/LICENSE) and derive from
[Thalamus-Reasoning-9B](https://huggingface.co/ingenix/Thalamus-Reasoning-9B) and [Qwen3.5-9B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B)
(Apache 2.0). Data files in the model repository keep their own terms; see its README.

## Citation

  author = {Kinas, Remigiusz and Pikusa, Michał and Powalski, Rafał and Możwiłło, Aleksandra and

             Powalski, Rafał},

one_liner: HeurekaBench 是一个面向单细胞生物学、用于评估 AI 共科学家（科学 Agent）的基准测试框架，与生物 Agent 方向相关，但本身不提供模型训练或推理实现。
card:
## 是什么

Heureka Bench 是一个用于创建和评估 AI 共科学家（AI co-scientist）基准测试的框架，它基于专有的多组学生物学模型 Archimedes，并针对单细胞生物学实例化为 sc-HeurekaBench。该框架通过半自动化的流水线，利用多个 LLM 从真实科学研究和对应代码仓库中提取见解并生成候选工作流，再与已报道的发现进行验证，从而构建出探索性、开放式的研究问题，用于端到端评估科学智能体。

## 亮点

- **专有生物学模型 Archimedes**：该模型基于数十万真实生物样本（而非文本）训练，能够对数据进行定位、质量控制和情境化，这是通用 LLM 无法做到的。
- **半自动化基准构建流水线**：利用多个 LLM 自动提取见解、生成候选工作流，并验证其与已报道发现的一致性，大幅降低了人工构建基准的成本。
- **端到端评估框架**：覆盖数据分析、解释和新见解生成的全过程，提供真实、探索性的研究场景，而非简单的问答任务。
- **定量分析智能体设计选择**：通过基准测试，能够量化分析智能体系统设计选择（如添加 critic 模块）对性能的影响，为智能体设计提供实证依据。

## 为何对本课题有用

本课题聚焦于虚拟细胞/虚拟器官、单细胞/空间组学以及生物基座模型、生物大语言模型和 Bio Agent。Heureka Bench 直接针对生物基座模型和 Bio Agent 的评估问题，提供了：

- **评估方法论**：为生物基座模型（如 Archimedes）和 Bio Agent 提供严格的端到端评估框架，填补了该领域缺乏真实、探索性基准的空白。
- **单细胞实例化**：sc-HeurekaBench 专门针对单细胞生物学，可直接用于评估单细胞数据分析智能体，与课题中的单细胞组学方向高度契合。
- **智能体设计洞察**：通过定量分析，发现 critic 模块能显著提升开源 LLM 智能体的表现，为构建更强大的 Bio Agent 提供设计指导。
- **可迁移的基准构建流程**：其半自动化流水线可迁移到其他组学数据（如空间组学）或虚拟细胞模型，用于构建新的评估基准。

## 怎么用

- **主入口**：仓库根目录的 `README.md` 提供了项目概览和链接；`Projects/` 目录下包含具体项目，如 `LearnAboutHeureka` 和 `Skill4AttieData`，其中 `Skill4AttieData` 包含 `SKILL.md` 和 `data_map.md`，可能用于定义智能体技能。
- **安装与依赖**：README 未说明具体的安装步骤或依赖文件（如 `requirements.txt` 或 `pyproject.toml`）。
- **输入/输出数据格式**：README 未明确说明，但提及基准问题基于科学研究和代码仓库，可能涉及单细胞数据（如 h5ad、CSV 等），具体格式需参考论文或仓库内文档。
- **是否需要 GPU**：README 未说明，但考虑到涉及 LLM 和生物模型，通常需要 GPU 加速，具体需确认。
- **Demo/示例/单元测试**：`Analysis/` 目录包含一个分析日志文件，`Projects/` 下有项目文档，但未提供可直接运行的示例或单元测试。

## 核心 idea

核心方法学在于：通过半自动化的流水线，将真实科学研究和代码仓库转化为探索性、开放式的基准问题，并利用多个 LLM 进行交叉验证，从而构建出能够端到端评估科学智能体的基准，同时通过定量分析揭示智能体设计选择（如 critic 模块）的影响。

## 可搬移点

- **基准构建流水线**：其半自动化的“提取见解-生成工作流-验证”流程可被解耦，用于构建针对虚拟细胞或空间组学数据的评估基准。
- **评估指标与设计分析**：用于量化智能体性能的评估方法和设计选择分析（如 critic 模块）可迁移到自定义 Bio Agent 的评估中。
- **Archimedes 模型**：虽然专有，但其“基于真实样本而非文本”的训练思路可启发生物基座模型的构建。
- **License**：README 未明确说明，需确认。

## Overview

Heureka Bench uses
`Archimedes`,
which is a proprietary multi-omics biology model
trained on measured biological samples rather than published text.

LLM-based reasoning models have enabled the development of agentic systems that act as co-scientists, assisting in multi-step scientific analysis. However, evaluating these systems is challenging, as it requires realistic, end-to-end research scenarios that integrate data analysis, interpretation, and the generation of new insights from the experimental data. To address this limitation, we introduce HeurekaBench, a framework to create benchmarks with exploratory, open-ended research questions for experimental datasets. Each such question is grounded in a scientific study and its corresponding code repository, and is created using a semi-automated pipeline that leverages multiple LLMs to extract insights and generate candidate workflows, which are then verified against reported findings. We instantiate the framework in single-cell biology to obtain sc-HeurekaBench benchmark and use it to compare state-of-the-art single-cell agents. We further showcase the benefits of our benchmark for quantitatively analyzing current design choices in agentic systems. We find that the addition of a critic module can improve ill-formed responses for open-source LLM-based agents by up to 22% and close the gap with their closed-source counterparts. Overall, HeurekaBench sets a path toward rigorous, end-to-end evaluation of scientific agents, grounding benchmark construction in real scientific workflows.

### Core Components in Heureka Bench

- **Archimedes**: “A proprietary model trained on hundreds of thousands of real biological samples — not text — so Heureka can place, QC, and contextualize your data in ways a general LLM can't.”, as noted by Heureka Labs.
- **ARC (AI Research Companion)**: The embedded scientific agent that queries the underlying biological model to perform data analysis, statistics, and handle local research files. [1]

Open question: **How does `Archimedes` compare to general language models like GPT-4 or Claude for biological data analysis?**

## References

- [[2601.01678] HeurekaBench: A Benchmarking Framework for AI Co-scientist](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.01678>)
- [How to discover: A Heureka Labs experiment by Matthew Hirschey](https://handbook.heurekalabs.co/)
  - [About this Handbook](https://handbook.heurekalabs.co/about.html)
- [mlbio-epfl/HeurekaBench: [ICLR 2026] A framework to "create benchmarks" and "evaluate AI co-scientists" in experimental data-driven real-world scientific research. · GitHub](https://github.com/mlbio-epfl/HeurekaBench)
- [Heureka Labs YouTube Channel](https://www.youtube.com/@Heureka-Labs)
  - [Heureka! Stories of Discovery with Matthew Hirschey](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=y82wZem60Ks)`

## 是什么
这是一个**文献与模型资源索引仓库**，由 Theis Lab 维护，配套发表于 Nature Methods 的综述论文《Transformers in Single-Cell Omics: A Review and New Perspectives》。它本身不提供可运行的模型或算法，而是以网页仪表盘（Jekyll + React）的形式，系统性地收集、分类和展示单细胞组学领域所有基于 Transformer 架构的论文与实现，并区分了模型实现、评估基准和 LLM 应用等不同类别。

## 亮点
- **结构化知识库**：将散落的单细胞 Transformer 文献按“模型实现”、“评估”、“LLM”等维度分类，并支持通过 YAML 数据文件动态更新，便于社区协作维护。
- **交互式前端**：基于 React 和 Radix UI 构建了可筛选、可排序的表格界面，用户可按模型、任务、数据模态等条件快速检索，极大提升文献调研效率。
- **可复现的构建流程**：使用 Webpack 打包前端资源，YAML 数据经脚本转换为 JS 模块，整个流程清晰，便于本地部署或二次开发。
- **社区驱动**：明确欢迎 PR 和 Issue，数据格式简单（YAML），降低了贡献门槛，有利于保持资源的新鲜度。

## 为何对本课题有用
本仓库直接服务于“**生物基座模型、生物大语言模型**”这一核心课题，是**领域地图和文献导航**的黄金标准。对于研究虚拟细胞/虚拟器官的团队，它提供了：
- **快速定位基线模型**：可以迅速找到当前所有基于 Transformer 的单细胞模型（如 scBERT、scGPT、Geneformer 等），了解其架构、任务和评估方式，避免重复造轮子。
- **发现评估基准**：仓库中的“transformer-evaluation”页面专门收集了模型评估相关的论文，这对于建立虚拟细胞模型的标准化评测体系至关重要。
- **追踪 LLM 应用**：“transformer-llms”页面聚焦于大语言模型在单细胞领域的应用，直接对应“生物大语言模型、Bio Agent”方向，可帮助研究者把握前沿趋势。
- **构建领域知识图谱**：其分类和标签体系可作为我们构建虚拟细胞知识图谱或训练 Bio Agent 时的结构化知识来源。

## 怎么用
- **主入口**：仓库根目录的 `index.md` 和 `_pages/` 下的三个 Markdown 文件（`single-cell-transformers.md`、`transformer-evaluation.md`、`transformer-llms.md`）是内容源。
- **安装与依赖**：前端依赖见 `package.json`，需要 Node.js 环境。运行 `npm install` 安装依赖，`npm run build` 或 `npm run dev` 构建/开发前端。
- **数据格式**：核心数据存储在 `_data` 目录（README 提及，但目录树未列出具体文件），格式为 YAML，每条记录包含论文标题、链接、模型类型、任务等字段。
- **运行方式**：这是一个静态网站项目，构建后可直接部署。本地调试可运行 `npm run dev` 启动 Webpack 开发服务器。
- **无需 GPU**：本仓库不涉及模型训练或推理，纯前端展示，无需 GPU 算力。
- **调试入口**：可直接查看 `assets/js/pages/` 下的 React 组件（如 `single-cell-transformers.jsx`）和 `assets/js/data/yaml-data.js`（构建后生成）来理解数据流。

## 核心 idea
其核心方法学在于**将领域知识进行结构化、分类化和可检索化**，通过一个轻量级的 YAML 数据层和交互式前端，将海量文献转化为一个动态的、社区可维护的知识图谱。它不提供新算法，但提供了一种高效组织、导航和更新领域知识的方式，这对于快速发展的交叉学科（如虚拟细胞）至关重要。

## 可搬移点
- **数据组织模式**：`_data` 目录下的 YAML 文件结构（具体字段需查看仓库）是高度可移植的，我们可以借鉴其模式来构建自己的“虚拟细胞模型/工具”清单，作为团队内部知识库或 Bio Agent 的训练语料。
- **前端筛选组件**：`assets/js/components/` 下的 `FilterableTable.jsx`、`FilterPanel.jsx` 等 React 组件实现了强大的多条件筛选功能，可直接解耦并复用到我们自己的模型比较或结果展示平台中。
- **构建脚本**：`scripts/generate-yaml.js` 展示了如何将 YAML 数据转换为前端可用的 JS 模块，这种数据管道设计可迁移到其他需要动态更新数据的场景。
- **License**：README 未明确说明 License，需确认。但作为学术综述的配套资源，通常允许非商业使用和引用，具体需查看仓库中的 LICENSE 文件（目录树未列出）。

# Transformers in Single-Cell Omics
This repository accompanies [Transformers in Single-Cell Omics: A Review and New Perspectives](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41592-024-02353-z). Please refer to the manuscript for the details.

An up-to-date list of single-cell transformer papers is available on the [website](https://theislab.github.io/single-cell-transformer-papers/).

We welcome contributions to this repository. Please open a pull request or an issue if you want to add or edit an entry. Model data is stored in `_data` directory, following the format of the existing entries. New entries are added at the top of the corresponding table.

### Citation
If you find the the data in this repository useful for your work, please cite:
```
@Article{szalata_transformers_2024,
	title = {Transformers in single-cell omics: a review and new perspectives},
	volume = {21},
	issn = {1548-7105},
	url = {https://doi.org/10.1038/s41592-024-02353-z},
	doi = {10.1038/s41592-024-02353-z},
	abstract = {Recent efforts to construct reference maps of cellular phenotypes have expanded the volume and diversity of single-cell omics data, providing an unprecedented resource for studying cell properties. Despite the availability of rich datasets and their continued growth, current single-cell models are unable to fully capitalize on the information they contain. Transformers have become the architecture of choice for foundation models in other domains owing to their ability to generalize to heterogeneous, large-scale datasets. Thus, the question arises of whether transformers could set off a similar shift in the field of single-cell modeling. Here we first describe the transformer architecture and its single-cell adaptations and then present a comprehensive review of the existing applications of transformers in single-cell analysis and critically discuss their future potential for single-cell biology. By studying limitations and technical challenges, we aim to provide a structured outlook for future research directions at the intersection of machine learning and single-cell biology.},
	pages = {1430--1443},
	number = {8},
	journaltitle = {Nature Methods},
	shortjournal = {Nature Methods},
	author = {Szałata, Artur and Hrovatin, Karin and Becker, Sören and Tejada-Lapuerta, Alejandro and Cui, Haotian and Wang, Bo and Theis, Fabian J.},
	date = {2024-08-01},}
```

## 是什么

DeepSpot 是一个基于深度学习的开源工具，用于从 H&E 染色的组织病理学图像预测空间转录组（spatial transcriptomics）数据。它通过将每个空间 spot 视为多个子 spot 的集合（bag），并整合局部形态与全局空间上下文，从而在 spot 或单细胞分辨率下预测基因表达。该仓库提供了完整的训练、推理和预处理流程，并附带预训练模型和大型预测数据集。

## 亮点

- **双分辨率支持**：同时支持 spot 级别（DeepSpot）和单细胞级别（DeepCell）的预测，适应不同空间组学平台（如 Visium 和 Xenium）。
- **空间上下文建模**：通过将 spot 分解为子 spot 并聚合邻域信息，显式建模空间上下文，显著提升预测精度。
- **即用型生态**：提供预训练权重（Zenodo）、大规模预测数据（HuggingFace，8TB，覆盖 4 种癌症类型）以及完整的 Jupyter notebook 教程，降低使用门槛。
- **模块化设计**：代码结构清晰，分为 spot/cell 两个子模块，便于扩展和替换。
- **与病理学基础模型集成**：支持 UNI、Hoptimus0、Phikon 等预训练病理学模型作为特征提取器，利用强大的视觉表征。

## 为何对本课题有用

DeepSpot 直接属于“虚拟细胞/虚拟器官 × 单细胞/空间组学 × 生物基座模型”这一课题方向，是构建虚拟空间转录组学的核心工具。其价值在于：

- **虚拟空间转录组生成**：能够从常规 H&E 图像预测空间基因表达，无需昂贵的空间组学实验，为虚拟器官建模提供数据增强手段。
- **基础模型集成范式**：展示了如何将病理学基础模型（如 UNI）与下游预测头结合，为生物基座模型在空间组学任务上的应用提供了可复用的架构参考。
- **单细胞分辨率扩展**：DeepCell 模块将预测推进到单细胞级别，与虚拟细胞模型的目标高度契合，可作为单细胞空间转录组预测的基线或组件。
- **大规模数据资源**：提供的 TCGA 预测数据集（56M spots）可作为虚拟细胞/器官研究的训练或验证资源，尤其适用于缺乏空间组学数据的场景。

## 怎么用

- **安装**：
  ```bash
  git clone https://github.com/ratschlab/DeepSpot
  cd DeepSpot
  conda env create --file=environment.yaml
  conda activate deepspot
  pip install .
  ```
  需要额外安装 pyvips（`conda install conda-forge::pyvips`）。
- **主入口**：仓库提供 Jupyter notebook 教程（`example_notebook/`），分为 Visium spot 级别和 Xenium 单细胞级别，包含预处理、训练和推理步骤。
- **依赖**：核心依赖包括 PyTorch 2.4.1、Lightning、scanpy、squidpy、pyvips 等，详见 `environment.yaml` 和 `pyproject.toml`。
- **输入/输出**：输入为 H&E 组织图像（tile 或 patch）及对应的空间坐标；输出为预测的基因表达矩阵（通常为 AnnData 格式，可保存为 h5ad）。预处理会过滤背景区域（如平均 RGB > 200 的 tile）。
- **GPU 需求**：需要 GPU 加速（CUDA 12.4），因为涉及深度学习模型训练和推理。
- **调试入口**：可直接运行 notebook 中的示例，或使用 `deepspot.spot.DeepSpot` 和 `deepspot.cell.DeepCell` 类进行断点调试。

## 核心 idea

核心方法学在于将空间转录组预测问题建模为“bag-of-sub-spots”的深度集合学习：每个 spot 被划分为多个子 tile，通过预训练病理学模型提取局部特征，同时聚合邻域 spot 的特征以捕获空间上下文，最终通过基因预测头输出表达值。这种设计使得模型能够同时利用局部形态和全局空间关系，从而在有限标注下实现高精度预测。

## 可搬移点

- **特征提取与聚合模块**：`deepspot/utils/utils_image.py` 中的图像 tile 处理和特征提取逻辑，可解耦后用于自定义的病理图像分析 pipeline。
- **模型架构**：`deepspot/spot/model.py` 和 `deepspot/cell/model.py` 中的 bag-of-sub-spots 网络结构，可作为空间组学预测的通用组件，替换或集成到其他模型中。
- **数据预处理流程**：`deepspot/spot/dataloader.py` 和 `deepspot/cell/dataloader.py` 中的数据处理逻辑（如 tile 划分、邻域构建）可复用，用于处理 Visium 或 Xenium 数据。
- **损失函数**：`deepspot/spot/loss.py` 和 `deepspot/cell/loss.py` 中的损失函数设计，可借鉴用于其他空间组学预测任务。
- **License**：MIT 许可证，允许自由使用、修改和分发，但需保留版权声明。

注意：具体模块的接口和依赖需参考源码，建议在移植时进行适配。

Try the interactive [Aurora demo](https://www.auroraomics.org/demo).

  - [9.2025] DeepSpot was featured in the Eric and Wendy Schmidt Center article ["Machine Learning Teams Push the Boundaries of Virtual Spatial Biology in Global Autoimmune Disease Challenge."](https://www.ericandwendyschmidtcenter.org/updates/machine-learning-teams-push-the-boundaries-of-virtual-spatial-biology-in-global-autoimmune-disease-challenge)

## Changelog

### NEW version (May 2025)
  - DeepCell for spatial transcriptomics at **single-cell** resolution
  - [new tutorials](example_notebook/)
  - change in the module structure
      - `from deepspot.spot import DeepSpot`
      - `from deepspot.cell import DeepCell`
  - [8 TB of predicted TCGA spatial transcriptomics data - LUSC, LUAD, SKCM, KIRC](https://huggingface.co/datasets/nonchev/TCGA_digital_spatial_transcriptomics)
    - 3780 samples
    - 56 317 393 spots
    - 4 cancer types
  - [more DeepSpot pretrained models on Visium and Xenium data](https://zenodo.org/records/15322099)



## Do you want to generate spatial transcriptomics data using your H&E images?

We introduce DeepSpot, a novel deep-learning model that predicts spatial transcriptomics from H&E images. DeepSpot employs a deep-set neural network to model spots as bags of sub-spots and integrates multi-level tissue details and spatial context. This integration, supported by the robust pre-trained H&E models, significantly enhances the accuracy and granularity of gene predictions from H&E images.

![deepspot](/figures/figure_2.png)

**Fig.: DeepSpot leverages pathology foundation models and spatial tissue context.**
**Workflow of DeepSpot**: H&E slides are first divided into tiles, each corresponding to a spot. For each spot, we create a bag of sub-spots by dividing it into sub-tiles that capture the local morphology, and a bag of neighboring spots to represent the global context. A pretrained pathology model extracts tile features, which are input to the model. The concatenated representations are then fed into the gene head predictor, ρgene, to predict spatial gene expression.

## Setup

```
git clone https://github.com/ratschlab/DeepSpot
cd DeepSpot
conda env create --file=environment.yaml
conda activate deepspot
pip install .
```

##### NB: Please ensure you have installed [pyvips](https://github.com/libvips/pyvips) depending on your machine's requirements. We suggest installing pyvips through conda:
```
conda install conda-forge::pyvips
```

Install jupyter kernel 
```
python -m ipykernel install --user --name deepspot --display-name "deepspot"
```

## Getting Started

Please take a look at our notebook collection to get started with DeepSpot for Visium or the adapted version of DeepSpot - DeepCell, for Xenium. We provide a small toy examples.

**DeepSpot** for spatial transcriptomics at **spot** resolution:
  - [Spatial transcriptomics data preprocessing spot level resolution](example_notebook/Visium_spot_example/GettingStartedWithDeepSpot_1_preprocessing.ipynb)
  - [DeepSpot training](example_notebook/Visium_spot_example/GettingStartedWithDeepSpot_2_training.ipynb)
  - [DeepSpot inference](example_notebook/Visium_spot_example/GettingStartedWithDeepSpot_3_inference.ipynb)
  - [DeepSpot inference with pretrained model](example_notebook/Visium_spot_example/GettingStartedWithDeepSpot_3.1_inference_pretrained_models.ipynb)

**DeepCell** for spatial transcriptomics at **single-cell** resolution:

Moreover, we provide pretrained weights for DeepSpot, which were generated during the training of the model in our publication and were used, for example, to generate spatial transcriptomics data for TCGA skin melanoma and kidney cancer slides.

card:
## 是什么

Lobster AI 是一个由 LangGraph 驱动的多智能体生物信息学分析系统，旨在通过自然语言交互，让用户能够对多种组学数据（如单细胞转录组、基因组、蛋白质组、代谢组等）进行端到端的分析。它通过一个监督者（supervisor）协调多个领域专家智能体（agent），每个智能体负责特定的分析任务，并能够调用底层的科学计算库（如 Scanpy、PyDESeq2 等）来执行具体的计算。

## 亮点

*   **多智能体架构**：采用 LangGraph 监督者模式，将复杂的生物信息学分析流程分解为多个领域专家智能体，每个智能体专注于特定任务（如转录组、基因组、蛋白质组等），实现了高度的模块化和可扩展性。
*   **本地执行与数据隐私**：分析在用户本地机器上运行，数据文件不会离开用户环境，仅将消息和工具结果发送给所配置的 LLM 提供商，这为敏感的生物医学数据提供了隐私保护。
*   **可复现性与可追溯性**：系统能够记录整个分析过程中的所有步骤，并可以导出为 Jupyter Notebook，支持通过 Papermill 进行无头重跑，确保了分析的可复现性和可审计性。
*   **灵活的 LLM 提供商支持**：支持多种 LLM 提供商，包括 Anthropic、OpenAI、Google Gemini、AWS Bedrock、Azure AI 以及本地模型（如 Ollama），用户可以根据需求、成本和隐私要求灵活选择。
*   **可扩展的智能体生态**：通过 Python entry points 机制，用户可以轻松创建和集成新的领域专家智能体，无需修改核心代码，这为扩展新的组学数据类型或分析功能提供了便利。
*   **丰富的领域覆盖**：内置了转录组学、基因组学、蛋白质组学、代谢组学、药物发现、机器学习等多个领域的专家智能体，覆盖了从数据获取、质量控制、统计分析到可视化、解释的完整分析流程。

## 为何对本课题有用

Lobster AI 与「虚拟细胞/虚拟器官 × 单细胞/空间组学 × 生物基座模型、生物大语言模型、Bio Agent」课题高度相关，其价值体现在：

*   **作为 Bio Agent 的参考实现**：Lobster AI 是一个典型的 Bio Agent 系统，其多智能体架构、工具调用机制、状态管理（LangGraph）以及可扩展的插件系统，为构建面向虚拟细胞/虚拟器官研究的智能体提供了直接的设计蓝图和可复用的代码模式。
*   **加速单细胞/空间组学分析流程**：其转录组学智能体直接支持单细胞 RNA-seq 分析，包括质量控制、批次整合（Harmony）、聚类、细胞类型注释和轨迹推断等。这些功能是构建虚拟细胞模型的基础数据预处理和分析步骤，可以显著加速相关研究。
*   **提供数据获取与整合能力**：其研究智能体能够搜索 PubMed、GEO 等数据库并下载数据集，这对于构建虚拟细胞/虚拟器官所需的训练数据（如单细胞图谱、空间转录组数据）至关重要。
*   **促进多组学整合**：虚拟细胞/虚拟器官的构建需要整合多种组学数据（基因组、转录组、蛋白质组、代谢组等）。Lobster AI 的多智能体架构天然支持多组学数据的协同分析，为构建多模态生物基座模型提供了数据整合和分析框架。
*   **可复现的研究范式**：其将分析步骤导出为 Notebook 并支持重跑的特性，符合虚拟细胞/虚拟器官研究中对于可复现性和可验证性的要求，有助于建立标准化的分析流程。

## 怎么用

*   **安装**：
    *   macOS/Linux: 通过 curl 下载安装脚本并运行。
    *   Windows: 通过 PowerShell 执行安装脚本。
    *   或者使用 pip/uv 安装 `lobster-ai[full]` 并选择 LLM 提供商。
*   **配置**：运行 `lobster init` 选择 LLM 提供商（如 Anthropic、OpenAI、Ollama 等）并配置 API 密钥。
*   **启动交互式会话**：运行 `lobster chat` 进入交互式命令行界面，用自然语言描述分析任务，例如：
    ```
    > Search PubMed for single-cell CRISPR screens in T cells from 2023–2024, download the most cited dataset, run QC, integrate batches with Harmony, cluster the cells, annotate cell types, and export a notebook of the recorded steps.
    ```
*   **非交互式查询**：使用 `lobster query "your request"` 进行单轮查询。
*   **会话管理**：使用 `--session-id` 参数管理多个会话，支持会话恢复。
*   **导出与重跑**：在会话中使用 `/pipeline export` 导出分析步骤为 Jupyter Notebook，使用 `/pipeline run` 重跑。
*   **开发新智能体**：使用 `lobster scaffold agent` 生成新智能体包，实现工具函数并声明 AQUADIF 元数据，然后通过 entry points 注册。
*   **验证**：使用 `lobster validate-plugin` 和 `pytest -m contract` 验证智能体包的结构和契约。

## 核心 idea

Lobster AI 的核心 idea 是**将复杂的生物信息学分析流程抽象为可编排的多智能体系统，通过自然语言接口和标准化的工具契约（AQUADIF），实现分析流程的自动化、模块化和可复现性**。它利用 LangGraph 的状态图来管理分析流程的状态和转换，每个智能体封装特定的领域知识，并通过工具调用与底层科学计算库交互，从而将 LLM 的推理能力与专业的生物信息学工具结合起来。

## 可搬移点

*   **多智能体编排框架**：`lobster/agents/graph.py` 和 `lobster/agents/supervisor.py` 中的 LangGraph 监督者模式，可以直接借鉴或迁移到自定义的虚拟细胞/虚拟器官分析流水线中，用于协调多个分析模块（如数据预处理、模型训练、结果解释）。
*   **工具契约（AQUADIF）**：`lobster/config/aquadif.py` 中定义的 AQUADIF 元数据规范，可以用于标准化自定义分析工具的描述，使其能够被 LLM 智能体自动发现和调用。
*   **智能体注册机制**：`lobster/config/agent_registry.py` 中的 entry points 注册机制，可以用于构建可插拔的分析模块，方便扩展新的分析功能。
*   **数据适配器**：`lobster/core/adapters/` 下的各种数据适配器（如转录组、基因组、蛋白质组等），其设计模式可以迁移到处理空间组学数据或虚拟细胞模型输出数据。
*   **Pipeline 导出与重跑**：`lobster/core/` 中关于分析步骤记录和 Notebook 导出的逻辑，可以用于构建可复现的分析流程，确保虚拟细胞/虚拟器官研究结果的可验证性。
*   **License**：根目录 `pyproject.toml` 显示项目采用 AGPL-3.0-or-later 许可证，这意味着在迁移代码时需要遵守相应的开源协议条款，特别是如果用于商业或闭源项目，需确认合规性。

# CLI Reference **Core commands:** ```bash lobster chat # Interactive session (default) lobster query "your request" # Single-turn, non-interactive lobster init # Configure LLM provider and API keys lobster --help # Full command reference ``` **Session continuity:** ```bash lobster query --session-id my_project "Search PubMed for CRISPR" lobster query --session-id latest "Download the first result" # resume last session ``` **In-session slash commands** (inside `lobster chat`): ```text > /pipeline export # Export the recorded analysis steps as a Jupyter notebook > /pipeline run analysis.ipynb # Re-run an exported notebook > /data # List loaded datasets and modalities > /files # Browse workspace files > /status # Session info, token usage, active agents > /help # All slash commands ``` **Developer commands:** ```bash lobster scaffold agent --name my_expert --display-name "My Expert" \ --description "Description" --tier free # Generate a new agent package lobster validate-plugin ./lobster-my/ # Validate package structure and AQUADIF contract ```
# 🤖 For AI Coding Agents Install skills that give Claude Code, Cursor, or Gemini CLI deep knowledge of the Lobster architecture: ```bash curl -fsSL https://skills.lobsterbio.com | bash ``` This installs `lobster-use` (analysis workflows) and `lobster-dev` (agent development). With these loaded, your coding agent understands the full 10-package structure, tool patterns, entry point registration, and AQUADIF contract — without needing to read source code manually. **Scaffold a new agent package from the command line:** ```bash lobster scaffold agent \ --name epigenomics_expert \ --display-name "Epigenomics Expert" \ --description "ATAC-seq, ChIP-seq, and DNA methylation analysis" \ --tier free ``` Generates a complete, contract-compliant package: `pyproject.toml`, entry point wiring, tool stubs with AQUADIF metadata, and contract tests. Then point your coding agent at the generated scaffolding and ask it to implement the domain logic.
# Use Cases End-to-end walkthroughs across omics domains:
Domain Case Study
Single-Cell TranscriptomicsCell clustering, annotation & trajectory inference
CML Drug ResistanceResistance mechanism discovery from scRNA-seq
Drug DiscoveryTarget identification & compound prioritization
Clinical GenomicsVariant annotation & GWAS analysis
Mass Spec ProteomicsBiomarker panel selection from DIA-NN data
Literature MiningAutomated dataset discovery from PubMed
Multi-Omics MLFeature selection & survival analysis

# 🧠 Architecture Lobster AI is a multi-agent system: specialist agents for each omics domain, orchestrated by a LangGraph supervisor. * **Local execution:** Analysis runs on your machine. Your data files stay on your machine; messages and tool results are sent to the LLM provider you configure (with a local model such as Ollama, they stay on your machine too). * **Scientific libraries:** Agents call Scanpy, PyDESeq2, Harmony and others through tool functions. Some agents also have a code tool for custom analysis, which you can switch off per agent. * **Provenance:** Analysis steps are recorded and can be exported as a Jupyter notebook.



# 🛠️ Build Your Own Agent New agents are standalone packages that plug into Lobster via Python entry points. The `lobster-dev` skill loads the full architecture reference into your coding agent (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Cursor) — package layout, tool patterns, AQUADIF contract, and test fixtures. Use `lobster scaffold` to generate the package skeleton, then let your coding agent implement the domain logic.

# FAQ
What omics domains are supported? | Domain | Input Formats | Key Capabilities | |--------|--------------|-----------------| | **Single-Cell RNA-seq** | AnnData, 10x, h5ad | QC, doublet detection (Scrublet), batch integration (Harmony/scVI), clustering, cell type annotation, trajectory inference (DPT/PAGA) | | **Bulk RNA-seq** | Salmon, kallisto, featureCounts | Sample QC, normalization (DESeq2/VST/CPM), differential expression (PyDESeq2), GSEA, publication-ready export | | **Genomics** | VCF, PLINK | GWAS, LD pruning, kinship estimation, association testing, result clumping | | **Clinical Genomics** | VCF, ClinVar, gnomAD | Variant annotation (VEP), pathogenicity scoring, clinical variant prioritization | | **Mass Spec Proteomics** | MaxQuant, DIA-NN, Spectronaut | PTM analysis (phospho/acetyl/ubiquitin), peptide-to-protein rollup, batch correction | | **Affinity Proteomics** | Olink NPX, SomaScan ADAT, Luminex MFI | LOD quality filtering, bridge normalization, cross-platform concordance | | **Proteomics Downstream** | Any loaded proteomics modality | GO/Reactome/KEGG enrichment, kinase enrichment (KSEA), STRING PPI, biomarker panel selection (LASSO/Boruta) | | **Metabolomics** | LC-MS, GC-MS, NMR | QC (RSD/TIC), imputation, normalization (PQN/TIC/IS), PCA, PLS-DA, OPLS-DA, m/z annotation (HMDB/KEGG), lipid class analysis | | **Machine Learning** | Any modality | Feature selection (stability/LASSO/variance), survival analysis (Cox/KM), cross-validation, SHAP, multi-omics integration (MOFA) | | **Research & Data Access** | — | PubMed/GEO/PRIDE/MetaboLights search, dataset download orchestration, metadata harmonization |
Which LLMs can I use? Configure via `lobster init` or environment variables. All providers use the same agent interface. | Provider | Type | Setup | Notes | |----------|------|-------|-------| | **Anthropic** | Cloud | API key | Claude models — recommended default | | **Ollama** | Local | `ollama pull ` | Local model: no messages go to an LLM provider (online database searches still use the internet) | | **OpenAI** | Cloud | API key | GPT and o-series models | | **OpenRouter** | Cloud | API key | Access 200+ models via a single endpoint | | **Nebius AI Studio** | Cloud | API key | Open-weight models (Qwen, DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi) | | **Google Gemini** | Cloud | Google API key | Long context window | | **AWS Bedrock** | Cloud | AWS credentials | Enterprise compliance, IAM-based auth | | **Azure AI** | Cloud | Endpoint + credential | Azure-hosted deployments |
Pipeline export and slash commands ```text lobster chat > /pipeline export # Export a Jupyter notebook of the recorded steps > /pipeline list # List exported pipelines > /pipeline run analysis.ipynb geo_gse109564 > /data # Show loaded datasets > /status # Session info > /help # All commands ``` Headless re-runs: execute the exported notebook with Papermill — only names in the notebook's parameters cell can be overridden: ```bash papermill analysis.ipynb output.ipynb -p input_data "new_dataset.h5ad" ```
Advanced installation (Windows, pip) **Windows** (PowerShell): ```powershell irm https://install.lobsterbio.com/windows | iex ``` **uv** (recommended manual install): ```bash uv tool install 'lobster-ai[full]' # All bundled domains (transcriptomics, genomics, # proteomics) + metadata assistant; provider at init lobster init ``` Optional domains ship as separate packages — add them to the same tool environment: ```bash uv tool install 'lobster-ai[full]' --with lobster-metabolomics --with lobster-ml \ --with lobster-drug-discovery --with lobster-structural-viz ``` Re-running `uv tool install` rebuilds the tool environment: extras and `--with` packages reset to whatever the new command includes — list them again when upgrading. **pip**: ```bash pip install 'lobster-ai[full]' lobster init ``` **Upgrade**: ```bash uv tool upgrade lobster-ai # uv pip install -U lobster-ai # pip ```
How do I build my own agent? Agents are standalone Python packages that register via PEP 517 entry points. No changes to core required — Lobster discovers them automatically at startup. **1. Scaffold the package:** ```bash lobster scaffold agent \ --name my_domain_expert \ --display-name "My Domain Expert" \ --description "Analysis for [your domain]" \ --tier free ``` **2. Implement your tools** in the generated `tools/` directory. Each tool must declare AQUADIF metadata: ```python @tool def run_analysis(modality_name: str) -> str: """Run domain-specific analysis on a loaded modality.""" ... run_analysis.metadata = {"categories": ["ANALYZE"], "provenance": True} run_analysis.tags = ["ANALYZE"] ``` **3. Validate the package structure** before wiring: ```bash lobster validate-plugin ./lobster-my_domain/ ``` **4. Install and test:** ```bash cd lobster-my_domain && uv venv --python 3.12 .venv && source .venv/bin/activate uv pip install -e . pytest pytest -m contract # runs all AQUADIF contract checks ``` Install the `lobster-dev` skill to give your coding agent the complete reference — package layout, `AGENT_CONFIG` pattern, factory function signature, tool design rules, and the full validation checklist: ```bash curl -fsSL https://skills.lobsterbio.com | bash ```

Foundation for the lobster-use and lobster-dev skills — domain knowledge structure and skill distribution patterns.
UI component architecture and streaming patterns used in the Omics-OS Cloud frontend.
BubbleTea, Lipgloss, Glamour, and huh — the entire terminal UI stack powering lobster chat.

## 是什么

SpatialFusion 是一个用于空间组学数据深度学习分析的 Python 包，它提供了一个轻量级框架，将空间转录组学（ST）与 H&E 组织病理学图像相结合，学习细胞邻域的联合多模态嵌入，并将其分组为空间生态位（spatial niches）。该工具在单细胞分辨率下运行，可应用于配对的 ST+H&E 数据集、仅 H&E 全切片图像或仅空间转录组学数据。

## 亮点

- **轻量级框架**：设计简洁，依赖较少，易于集成到现有分析流程中。
- **多模态融合**：整合分子（基因表达）和形态学（组织图像）特征，捕捉组织结构和基因表达的协调模式。
- **生物信息学定义的生态位**：生态位不是简单的空间邻域，而是具有通路水平激活特征和跨组织功能一致性的可重复微环境，这通过训练潜在空间编码通路激活来实现。
- **预训练权重**：为所有支持的基座模型组合（UNI/scGPT、UNI/Nicheformer、Virchow/scGPT、Virchow/Nicheformer）提供预训练检查点，方便直接使用。
- **支持多种模式**：支持仅 H&E 和仅 RNA 模式，增加了灵活性。
- **可复现性**：提供完整的教程、示例数据和用于复现论文分析的独立仓库。

## 为何对本课题有用

SpatialFusion 直接针对虚拟细胞/虚拟器官研究中的关键问题：如何从空间组学数据中识别和表征功能性组织微环境。它通过将单细胞空间转录组学与组织病理学图像结合，学习联合嵌入，从而能够构建空间生态位图谱，这对于理解组织结构和功能至关重要。

- **对虚拟细胞/虚拟器官**：该方法提供了从真实组织数据中提取空间生态位的方法，可作为虚拟器官建模的参考或验证数据。
- **对单细胞/空间组学**：它展示了如何整合多模态数据（RNA+图像）来增强单细胞分析，并提供了可复用的嵌入和聚类流程。
- **对生物基座模型**：SpatialFusion 利用预训练的基座模型（如 UNI、Virchow、scGPT、Nicheformer）生成单模态嵌入，然后进行融合，这为构建多模态生物基座模型提供了思路。
- **对 Bio Agent**：虽然本身不是 Agent，但其模块化设计（嵌入、融合、聚类）可被封装为 Agent 的工具，用于自动化空间组学分析。

## 怎么用

**安装**：

```bash
mamba create -n spatialfusion python=3.10 -y
mamba activate spatialfusion
# CPU 或 GPU 安装，选择对应命令
pip install spatialfusion
```

**依赖**：需要 PyTorch 和 DGL，以及 pandas、scanpy、anndata 等。GPU 加速可选，但推荐使用。

**主入口**：`src/spatialfusion/embed/embed.py` 中的 `run_full_embedding` 函数。

**输入**：
- 一个 AnnData 对象，包含单细胞分辨率的原始计数（`adata.X`）、空间坐标（`adata.obsm['spatial_px']`）和可选的细胞类型注释（`adata.obs['celltypes']`）。
- 预计算的单模态嵌入：H&E 嵌入（来自 UNI 或 Virchow）和 RNA 嵌入（来自 scGPT 或 Nicheformer），以 pandas DataFrame 形式提供。

**输出**：一个包含所有细胞/核最终整合嵌入的 DataFrame。

**示例**：

```python
from spatialfusion.embed.embed import AEInputs, run_full_embedding
from spatialfusion.utils.pkg_ckpt import resolve_pkg_ckpt
import pandas as pd
import scanpy as sc

he_df = pd.read_parquet('UNI.parquet')
rna_df = pd.read_parquet('scGPT.parquet')
adata = sc.read_h5ad("object.h5ad")

ae_inputs_by_sample = {
    'sample1': AEInputs(adata=adata, z_he=he_df, z_rna=rna_df),
}
ae_ckpt = resolve_pkg_ckpt("checkpoint_dir_ae/spatialfusion-ae-uni-scgpt.pt")
gcn_ckpt = resolve_pkg_ckpt("checkpoint_dir_gcn/spatialfusion-gcn-uni-scgpt.pt")

emb_df = run_full_embedding(
    ae_inputs_by_sample=ae_inputs_by_sample,
    ae_model_path=ae_ckpt,
    gcn_model_path=gcn_ckpt,
    device="cuda:0",
    combine_mode="average",
    spatial_key='spatial_px',
    celltype_key='celltypes',
)
```

**测试**：运行 `pytest` 在 `tests/` 目录下。

## 核心 idea

SpatialFusion 的核心思想是：通过将单细胞空间转录组学与组织病理学图像结合，并训练一个潜在空间来编码通路水平的激活信号，从而定义和识别可重复的、功能相关的空间生态位，而不是仅仅基于空间邻域的聚类。

## 可搬移点

- **多模态融合模块**：`src/spatialfusion/models/multi_ae.py` 中的自编码器架构，可用于将不同模态的嵌入融合到统一空间，可被解耦并集成到自定义的多模态分析流程中。
- **图卷积网络（GCN）模块**：`src/spatialfusion/models/gcn.py` 中的 GCN 用于处理空间图结构，可被提取用于其他需要图结构数据的任务。
- **嵌入工具**：`src/spatialfusion/utils/embed_ae_utils.py` 和 `embed_gcn_utils.py` 中的函数，可用于处理嵌入和构建图，可被复用。
- **预训练权重**：提供的检查点可直接用于新数据，无需重新训练。

**License**：MIT，允许自由使用、修改和分发，可放心移植。

# SpatialFusion
[![Docs](https://img.shields.io/badge/docs-online-blue.svg)]( https://uhlerlab.github.io/spatialfusion/ ) **SpatialFusion** is a Python package for deep learning–based analysis of spatial omics data. It provides a lightweight framework that integrates **spatial transcriptomics (ST)** with **H&E histopathology** to learn **joint multimodal embeddings** of cellular neighborhoods and group them into **spatial niches**. The method operates at **single-cell resolution**, and can be applied to: * paired ST + H&E datasets * H&E whole-slide images alone * spatial transcriptomics data alone By combining molecular and morphological features, SpatialFusion captures coordinated patterns of tissue architecture and gene expression. A key design principle is a biologically informed definition of niches: not simply spatial neighborhoods, but **reproducible microenvironments** characterized by pathway-level activation signatures and functional coherence across tissues. To reflect this prior, the latent space of the model is trained to encode biologically meaningful pathway activations, enabling robust discovery of integrated niches. The method is described in the paper: [SpatialFusion: A lightweight multimodal framework for pathway-informed spatial niche mapping](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.03.16.712056). You can find detailed documentation at https://uhlerlab.github.io/spatialfusion/ --- ## Prepare SpatialFusion inputs Before running SpatialFusion, you need to generate unimodal embeddings from two modalities. You can choose which foundation model to use for each: | Modality | Supported models | | -------- | --------------- | | H&E / whole-slide image | [UNI](https://huggingface.co/MahmoodLab/UNI2-h) · [Virchow](https://huggingface.co/paige-ai/Virchow2) | | Spatial transcriptomics | [scGPT](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scGPT) · [Nicheformer](https://github.com/theislab/nicheformer) | We provide Dockstore workflows for generating these embeddings, detailed on our [documentation website](https://uhlerlab.github.io/spatialfusion/unimodal-embeddings/). ## Installation ### 1. Create virtual environment ```bash mamba create -n spatialfusion python=3.10 -y mamba activate spatialfusion ``` ### 2. Install platform-specific libraries SpatialFusion depends on PyTorch and DGL, which have different builds for CPU and GPU systems. #### CPU ```bash pip install "torch==2.4.1" "torchvision==0.19.1" \ --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu pip install dgl -f https://data.dgl.ai/wheels/torch-2.4/repo.html ``` #### GPU (CUDA 12.4) ```bash pip install "torch==2.4.1" "torchvision==0.19.1" \ --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu124 pip install dgl -f https://data.dgl.ai/wheels/torch-2.4/cu124/repo.html ``` --- ### 3. Install SpatialFusion package #### Basic installation — *Recommended for users* ```bash pip install spatialfusion ``` --- #### Install from source - *Recommended for contributors* Includes: `pytest`, `black`, `ruff`, `sphinx`, `matplotlib`, `seaborn`. ```bash git clone https://github.com/uhlerlab/spatialfusion.git cd spatialfusion/ pip install -e ".[dev,docs]" ``` --- ### 4. Verify Installation ```bash python - <<'PY' import torch, dgl, spatialfusion print("Torch:", torch.__version__, "CUDA available:", torch.cuda.is_available()) print("DGL:", dgl.__version__) print("SpatialFusion OK") PY ``` --- ### 5. Notes * Default output directory is: ``` $HOME/spatialfusion_runs ``` Override with: ``` export SPATIALFUSION_ROOT=/your/path ``` * CPU installations work everywhere but are significantly slower. Estimated install time: 15-30 min on a 'normal' desktop. **Tested system configuration** OS: Rocky Linux 8.10 (Green Obsidian), x86_64 CPU: AMD EPYC 7763 64-Core Processor GPU used: 1 × NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU memory: 48 GiB VRAM NVIDIA driver: 570.124.04 --- ## Tutorials A complete tutorial notebook to embed / finetune SpatialFusion on a sample is available at: ``` tutorials/embed-and-finetune-sample.ipynb ``` To get unimodal embeddings, we provide instructions or a tutorial at: ``` tutorials/get-unimodal-embeddings-sample.ipynb ``` To run SpatialFusion on H&E only, we provide a tutorial at: ``` tutorials/embed-he-only.ipynb ``` To run SpatialFusion on RNA only, we provide a tutorial at: ``` tutorials/embed-rna-only.ipynb ``` Additional packages for the foundation models you choose must be installed manually: - **scGPT**: [https://github.com/bowang-lab/scGPT](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scGPT) - **Nicheformer**: [https://github.com/theislab/nicheformer](https://github.com/theislab/nicheformer) - **UNI**: [https://huggingface.co/MahmoodLab/UNI2-h](https://huggingface.co/MahmoodLab/UNI2-h) - **Virchow**: [https://huggingface.co/paige-ai/Virchow2](https://huggingface.co/paige-ai/Virchow2) We also provide a ready-to-use environment file: ``` spatialfusion_env.yml ``` Tutorial data is available on Zenodo: [https://zenodo.org/records/17594071](https://zenodo.org/records/17594071) The estimated tutorial time running on a single GPU on the tutorial data, given FM embeddings are already computed, is 5-10 min. --- ## Pretrained Weights SpatialFusion ships pretrained checkpoints for every combination of supported foundation models. Select the pair that matches the embeddings you generated: | H&E model | RNA model | AE checkpoint | GCN checkpoint | | --------- | --------- | ------------- | -------------- | | UNI | scGPT | `spatialfusion-ae-uni-scgpt.pt` | `spatialfusion-gcn-uni-scgpt.pt` | | UNI | Nicheformer | `spatialfusion-ae-uni-nicheformer.pt` | `spatialfusion-gcn-uni-nicheformer.pt` | | Virchow | scGPT | `spatialfusion-ae-virchow-scgpt.pt` | `spatialfusion-gcn-virchow-scgpt.pt` | | Virchow | Nicheformer | `spatialfusion-ae-virchow-nicheformer.pt` | `spatialfusion-gcn-virchow-nicheformer.pt` | | UNI | *(H&E only)* | — | `spatialfusion-he-gcn-uni-scgpt.pt` | | *(RNA only)* | scGPT | — | `spatialfusion-rna-gcn-uni-scgpt.pt` | All checkpoints are bundled with the package under `src/spatialfusion/data/` and are resolved automatically via `spatialfusion.utils.pkg_ckpt.resolve_pkg_ckpt`. --- ## Usage Example A minimal example showing how to embed a dataset using the pretrained AE and GCN. Swap in the checkpoint filenames that match your chosen foundation models (see the table above): ```python from spatialfusion.embed.embed import AEInputs, run_full_embedding from spatialfusion.utils.pkg_ckpt import resolve_pkg_ckpt import pandas as pd import scanpy as sc # Load H&E embeddings (UNI or Virchow — use whichever you generated) he_df = pd.read_parquet('UNI.parquet') # or 'Virchow2.parquet' # Load RNA embeddings (scGPT or Nicheformer — use whichever you generated) rna_df = pd.read_parquet('scGPT.parquet') # or 'nicheformer.parquet' # Load AnnData object adata = sc.read_h5ad("object.h5ad") # Mapping sample_name -> AEInputs # z_he holds H&E embeddings (UNI or Virchow); z_rna holds RNA embeddings (scGPT or Nicheformer) sample_name = 'sample1' ae_inputs_by_sample = { sample_name: AEInputs( adata=adata, z_he=he_df, z_rna=rna_df, ), } # Select the checkpoints matching your FM combination (e.g. UNI + scGPT shown here) ae_ckpt = resolve_pkg_ckpt("checkpoint_dir_ae/spatialfusion-ae-uni-scgpt.pt") gcn_ckpt = resolve_pkg_ckpt("checkpoint_dir_gcn/spatialfusion-gcn-uni-scgpt.pt") # Run the multimodal embedding pipeline # spatial_key: key in adata.obsm holding X/Y coordinates — set to match your AnnData # (e.g. check with list(adata.obsm.keys())) # celltype_key: key in adata.obs holding cell type labels — set to match your AnnData # (e.g. check with adata.obs.columns.tolist()) emb_df = run_full_embedding( ae_inputs_by_sample=ae_inputs_by_sample, ae_model_path=ae_ckpt, gcn_model_path=gcn_ckpt, device="cuda:0", # or "cpu" combine_mode="average", spatial_key='spatial_px', celltype_key='celltypes', save_ae_dir=None, # optional ) ``` This produces a DataFrame containing the final integrated embedding for all cells/nuclei. --- ## Required Inputs SpatialFusion operates on a **single-cell AnnData object** paired with an **H&E whole-slide image**. It also accepts only a WSI with cell coordinates in the H&E only mode, or only an AnnData object with RNA embeddings (no WSI) in the RNA only mode. ### **AnnData fields** | Key | Description | | ---------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | | `adata.obsm['spatial_px']` | X/Y centroid coordinates of each cell/nucleus in WSI pixel space. This is the default key expected by SpatialFusion; pass `spatial_key=` to `run_full_embedding` if your AnnData uses a different key (check with `list(adata.obsm.keys())`). | | `adata.X` | Raw counts (cell × gene). Must be single-cell resolution. | | `adata.obs['celltypes']` (optional) | Annotated cell types. This is the default key; pass `celltype_key=` to `run_full_embedding` if your AnnData uses a different column name (check with `adata.obs.columns.tolist()`). | ### **Whole-Slide Image (WSI)** A high-resolution H&E image corresponding to the same tissue section used for ST. Used to compute morphology embeddings with your chosen H&E foundation model (**UNI** or **Virchow**). --- ## Typical Workflow 1. **Prepare ST AnnData and the matched H&E WSI** 2. **Run your RNA foundation model** (scGPT or Nicheformer) to compute molecular embeddings 3. **Run your H&E foundation model** (UNI or Virchow) to compute morphology embeddings 4. **Select the matching pretrained checkpoint pair** (see [Pretrained Weights](#pretrained-weights) above) 5. **Run SpatialFusion** to integrate all modalities into joint embeddings 6. **Cluster & visualize** * Leiden clustering * UMAP * Spatial niche maps --- ## Repository Structure ``` . ├── LICENSE ├── pyproject.toml ├── README.md ├── src │ └── spatialfusion │ ├── data │ │ ├── checkpoint_dir_ae │ │ │ ├── spatialfusion-ae-uni-scgpt.pt │ │ │ ├── spatialfusion-ae-uni-nicheformer.pt │ │ │ ├── spatialfusion-ae-virchow-scgpt.pt │ │ │ └── spatialfusion-ae-virchow-nicheformer.pt │ │ └── checkpoint_dir_gcn │ │ ├── spatialfusion-gcn-uni-scgpt.pt │ │ ├── spatialfusion-gcn-uni-nicheformer.pt │ │ ├── spatialfusion-gcn-virchow-scgpt.pt │ │ ├── spatialfusion-gcn-virchow-nicheformer.pt │ │ ├── spatialfusion-he-gcn-uni-scgpt.pt │ │ └── spatialfusion-rna-gcn-uni-scgpt.pt │ ├── embed/ │ ├── finetune/ │ ├── models/ │ └── utils/ ├── tests │ ├── test_basic.py │ ├── test_finetune.py │ └── test_imports.py └── tutorials ├── data └── embed-and-finetune-sample.ipynb ``` **Highlights:** * **src/spatialfusion/data/** — packaged pretrained AE and GCN checkpoints * **src/spatialfusion/** — main library modules * **embed/** — embedding utilities & pipeline * **finetune/** — niche-level finetuning * **models/** — neural network architectures * **utils/** — loaders, graph utilities, checkpoint code * **tests/** — basic test suite * **tutorials/** — practical examples and sample data --- ## Reproducibility repository The repository containing the code to reproduce the analysis presented in the manuscript can be found [here](https://github.com/uhlerlab/spatialfusion-analysis/tree/main) --- ## Citing If you use SpatialFusion, please cite: > Yates J, Shavakhi M, Choueiri T, Camp SY, Van Allen EM, Uhler C. SpatialFusion: A lightweight multimodal framework for pathway-informed spatial niche mapping. _bioRxiv_. 2026. doi:10.64898/2026.03.16.712056 --- ## Version ### Version This release adds RNA-only SpatialFusion support (**v0.3.0**). --- ## License MIT License. See `LICENSE` for details.
