## 是什么

这是一个名为 **Universal Biomedical Skills & Agents** 的仓库，定位为“研究级生物医学操作系统”（Biomedical OS），旨在将生物医学 AI 从孤立的提示词转变为可复现、可检查的科研工作单元。它通过组织 **1207 个技能（Skills）**（覆盖 54 个类别）为生物医学 AI 智能体提供标准化的技能库，并配套一个名为 **BioKernel** 的运行时平台，用于路由、编排和评估这些技能。

## 亮点

- **大规模技能库**：仓库包含 1207 个技能，覆盖 54 个类别，从基因组学、单细胞分析到临床工作流，形成了一个庞大的、可复用的生物医学 AI 技能库。
- **标准化技能格式**：每个技能以 `SKILL.md` 文件为核心，包含元数据、参考、预期输出和工具边界，这种标准化设计使得技能可以被智能体可靠地调用和评估。
- **运行时平台 BioKernel**：提供 FastAPI 服务器、语义路由、工作流引擎、多模型适配器（OpenAI、Anthropic、Gemini、本地模型）以及 MCP 支持，是一个完整的智能体运行时。
- **可评估性**：内置评估模块（LLM-judge 和断言），强调对智能体输出的可评估性，这对于科研场景的可复现性至关重要。
- **生态集成**：集成了 LangChain、Semantic Kernel、MCP 等主流框架，并包含大量外部技能集合（如 Auto-GPT、awesome-chatgpt-prompts 等），展示了良好的生态兼容性。

## 为何对本课题有用

本仓库与课题（虚拟细胞/虚拟器官 × 单细胞/空间组学 × 生物基座模型、生物大语言模型、Bio Agent）高度相关，其价值体现在：

- **为 Bio Agent 提供现成的技能库**：课题中构建的 Bio Agent 可以直接复用本仓库中的技能，例如单细胞分析（Scanpy）、空间转录组学（Squidpy）、基因组变异解读等，避免重复开发。
- **提供智能体编排范式**：BioKernel 的语义路由、工作流引擎和评估机制，为构建复杂的生物医学多智能体系统（如虚拟细胞模拟中的多步骤分析）提供了可参考的架构。
- **标准化技能描述（SKILL.md）**：这种将领域知识封装为标准化技能单元的方式，非常适合用于构建可组合、可验证的生物医学 AI 工作流，是虚拟细胞模型构建中模块化设计的良好范例。
- **多模型适配**：支持多种 LLM 提供商，使得课题可以灵活选择基座模型（如 GPT、Claude、Gemini 或本地模型）来驱动生物医学智能体。

## 怎么用

- **安装与运行**：
  ```bash
  cd biokernel
  pip install -e ".[all-providers]"
  biokernel serve --port 8000
  ```
- **路由查询**：
  ```bash
  biokernel run "Analyze JAK2 V617F mutation in MPN patients" --provider anthropic
  ```
- **交互式会话**：
  ```bash
  biokernel interactive
  ```
- **MCP 暴露**：
  ```bash
  biokernel mcp
  ```
- **测试**：
  ```bash
  pytest -q biokernel/tests
  ```
- **技能结构**：每个技能位于 `Skills/<Category>/<Skill_Name>/SKILL.md`，包含元数据、参考、预期输出和工具边界。

## 核心 idea

**核心思想**：将生物医学 AI 能力从“提示词”提升为“可复用的技能单元”，并通过一个统一的运行时（BioKernel）来路由、编排和评估这些技能，从而实现可复现、可审计的智能体科研工作流。

## 可搬移点

- **技能库结构**：`Skills/` 目录下的 `SKILL.md` 格式（包含元数据、参考、预期输出、工具边界）可以直接复制并适配到自定义的 Bio Agent 系统中，作为技能定义的标准。
- **BioKernel 运行时**：`biokernel/` 中的 FastAPI 服务器、语义路由、工作流引擎和评估模块，可以作为构建自定义生物医学智能体平台的参考实现，或直接作为基础框架。
- **评估模块**：`biokernel/evaluator/` 中的 LLM-judge 和断言机制，可以迁移到任何需要评估 LLM 输出的生物医学场景中。
- **License 注意**：仓库声明为“Proprietary”（专有），且包含大量第三方开源组件（如 LangChain、Semantic Kernel 等），在复制或修改代码前需确认具体文件的许可证，尤其是涉及商业用途时。
- **可替换性**：该仓库的模块化设计（技能、适配器、评估器分离）支持逐步替换和自定义，例如可以替换默认的 LLM 适配器以接入新的基座模型，或添加自定义技能到技能库中。

# Universal Biomedical Skills & Agents _A research-grade Biomedical OS for reproducible, agentic life-science and clinical AI workflows._ ![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/Status-Active-green) ![Skills](https://img.shields.io/badge/Skills-1207-blue) ![Tests](https://img.shields.io/badge/BioKernel%20tests-74%20passing-brightgreen) ![Domains](https://img.shields.io/badge/Domains-Clinical%20%7C%20Genomics%20%7C%20Drug%20Discovery%20%7C%20Agentic%20AI-purple) ![Runtime](https://img.shields.io/badge/Runtime-BioKernel%20%7C%20MCP%20%7C%20Multi--LLM-orange) > **Attribution and copyright:** This repository, its curation strategy, Biomedical OS architecture, agent designs, and first-party workflows are maintained by **MD BABU MIA, PhD**. Open-source components retain their own licenses, while the original curation, architecture, and agentic workflow design require attribution, a link to the original repository, and preservation of this notice. --- ## 🧬 Research purpose This repository is designed for researchers who want to turn biomedical AI from isolated prompts into reproducible, inspectable units of scientific work. It organizes **1207 skills across 54 categories** into a structured library of `SKILL.md` files, reference notes, runtime adapters, and evaluation assets. The central idea is simple: a biomedical agent should know its domain, cite its evidence, use tools deliberately, preserve provenance, and stop at the right human review boundary. The repository supports translational research, clinical informatics, genomics, spatial and single-cell analysis, digital pathology, drug discovery, research automation, and modern agentic AI infrastructure. Its runtime layer, **BioKernel**, routes natural-language research questions to appropriate skills, composes multi-step workflows, and evaluates outputs with biomedical rubrics. ## 🔬 Scientific value for researchers | Research need | What this repository provides | |---|---| | Reproducible biomedical analysis | Standardized `SKILL.md` units with metadata, references, expected outputs, and tool boundaries | | Cross-platform agent deployment | BioKernel adapters for OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, local models, and MCP-compatible tool surfaces | | Agentic scientific discovery | Curated workflows for hypothesis generation, lab-in-the-loop planning, notebook analysis, and human-gated validation | | Translational evidence synthesis | Literature mining, knowledge graphs, clinical trial matching, biomarker analysis, and regulatory review patterns | | Research governance | Source reliability metadata, evaluation guidance, safety guardrails, rollback criteria, and reproducibility packages | ## 🧠 Research workflow ```mermaid flowchart LR accTitle: Biomedical Agent Workflow accDescr: Researcher questions are routed through curated skills, evidence tools, human review, and reproducible outputs. question([Research question]) --> route[BioKernel skill routing] route --> skill[Curated SKILL.md] skill --> tools[Data, literature, MCP, and analysis tools] tools --> review{Human checkpoint} review -->|Revise| skill review -->|Approve| artifact[Reproducible research artifact] artifact --> eval[Evaluation, provenance, and audit trail] classDef input fill:#ede9fe,stroke:#7c3aed,stroke-width:2px,color:#3b0764 classDef process fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#2563eb,stroke-width:2px,color:#1e3a5f classDef decision fill:#fef9c3,stroke:#ca8a04,stroke-width:2px,color:#713f12 classDef output fill:#dcfce7,stroke:#16a34a,stroke-width:2px,color:#14532d class question input class route,skill,tools,eval process class review decision class artifact output ``` ## 🧭 Major scientific domains | Domain | Representative capabilities | |---|---| | **Genomics and bioinformatics** | Variant interpretation, genome assembly, single-cell analysis, spatial transcriptomics, CRISPR screens, 3D genomics | | **Clinical and translational AI** | EHR/FHIR workflows, trial matching, prior authorization, clinical NLP, oncology decision support, safety review | | **Drug discovery and chemistry** | Target discovery, molecular property prediction, antibody design, protein structure, knowledge-graph repurposing | | **Pathology and imaging AI** | Whole-slide analysis, dMMR/MSI modeling guidance, radiology summaries, multimodal rad-path fusion | | **Agentic AI infrastructure** | Codex workflows, MCP operations, agent evaluations, computer-use agents, multi-agent scientific discovery | | **Research tools and databases** | Biomni-style orchestration, PubMed/ClinicalTrials access, cBioPortal, ChEMBL, AlphaFold, GTEx, gnomAD, GWAS, UniProt | ## 🧪 Current research highlights - **Scientific discovery agents:** [Scientific_Discovery_Agents_2026](Skills/Agentic_AI/Scientific_Discovery_Agents_2026/) captures the 2026 shift toward peer-reviewed biomedical discovery agents, including Co-Scientist, Robin, CellVoyager, SPARK, and Biomni-style orchestration.[^coscientist][^robin][^cellvoyager][^spark] - **Agent runtime modernization:** [OpenAI_Codex_Agents](Skills/Agentic_AI/OpenAI_Codex_Agents/) now reflects Codex app/cloud workflows, reusable skills, hosted tools, tool search, shell/apply_patch, MCP, and approval-aware execution.[^codex] - **MCP for research systems:** [MCP_Operations_2026](Skills/MCP_Servers/MCP_Operations_2026/) covers remote MCP authorization, protected-resource metadata, tool-poisoning review, identity propagation, timeout budgets, structured errors, and audit logging.[^mcp] - **Evaluation discipline:** [Agentic_Evals_Observability](Skills/Agentic_AI/Agentic_Evals_Observability/) now includes scope-control tests, out-of-scope action detection, scientific claim-boundary checks, and human-review checkpoints. ## 🧠 Biomedical model operations refresh Two gap-driven research batches add eleven first-party operational skills backed by authoritative model cards, repositories, releases, and primary literature: - **Genomics:** [Evo 2](Skills/Genomics/evo2-genome-model/), [AlphaGenome](Skills/Genomics/alphagenome-variant-effects/), and [OpenCRISPR](Skills/Genomics/opencrispr-gene-editors/). - **Single-cell foundation models:** [TranscriptFormer](Skills/Genomics/Single_Cell/transcriptformer-cell-embeddings/). - **Clinical and medical imaging:** [MedGemma 1.5](Skills/Clinical/medgemma-health-ai/), [MedSAM2](Skills/Clinical/Medical_Imaging/medsam2-3d-segmentation/), and [MONAI](Skills/Clinical/Medical_Imaging/monai-medical-imaging/). - **Structural biology and drug discovery:** [BioEmu](Skills/Structural_Biology/bioemu-protein-ensembles/), [Protenix-v2](Skills/Structural_Biology/protenix-structure-prediction/), [Boltz-2](Skills/Drug_Discovery/boltz2-biomolecular-interactions/), and [TxGemma](Skills/Drug_Discovery/txgemma-therapeutics/). The auditable source maps are in [batch 1](sources/research_20260618_new_biomedical_skills.md) and [batch 2](sources/research_20260618_new_biomedical_skills_batch2.md). ## 🧱 Repository architecture ```text Skills/ # Curated biomedical AI skills and agents ├── Agentic_AI/ # Agent runtimes, discovery agents, evals, memory, workflows ├── Clinical/ # EHR, oncology, radiology, trials, safety, regulatory workflows ├── Drug_Discovery/ # Antibody design, structure, chemistry, target discovery ├── Genomics/ # Single-cell, spatial, CRISPR, variant interpretation, assembly ├── MCP_Servers/ # BioMCP and protocol-aware biomedical tool servers ├── Pathology_AI/ # Whole-slide and computational pathology agents ├── Research_Tools/ # Biomni, literature mining, databases, reporting, knowledge graphs └── Software_Engineering/ # Scientific software and engineering best-practice skills biokernel/ # Runtime platform for routing, workflows, adapters, evals, and MCP ├── biokernel/ # FastAPI server, semantic router, workflow engine, MCP server ├── adapters/ # OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, and local model adapters ├── evaluator/ # Biomedical assertions and LLM-judge rubrics ├── optimizer/ # USDL transpiler and prompt optimization └── tests/ # 74 passing BioKernel tests docs/ # Architecture, operations, standards, strategy, and research notes sources/ # Auditable source maps for major curation passes ``` ## 🧾 Skill standard Curated skills are intentionally compact. Each high-quality skill should make it clear when to use it, what it can safely do, what tools it may invoke, what evidence it relies on, and where deeper references live. | Field | Purpose | |---|---| | `name` | Stable, hyphen-case identifier | | `description` | Trigger guidance for humans and agents | | `measurable_outcome` | Practical success criterion | | `source_reliability` | Evidence quality and provenance notes | | `allowed-tools` | Tool boundary for safe invocation | | `references/` | Deeper domain notes, papers, APIs, and operational guidance | | `agents/openai.yaml` | Optional UI metadata for agent surfaces | ## 🚀 Quick start ### Run BioKernel ```bash cd biokernel pip install -e ".[all-providers]" biokernel serve --port 8000 ``` ### Route a research question ```bash biokernel run "Analyze JAK2 V617F mutation in MPN patients" --provider anthropic ``` ### Start an interactive session ```bash biokernel interactive ``` ### Expose skills through MCP ```bash biokernel mcp ``` ### Run the BioKernel test suite ```bash pytest -q biokernel/tests ``` ## 👤 Principal investigator and maintainer **MD BABU MIA, PhD**

one_liner: AESTETIK 是一个面向空间转录组的多模态自编码器表征学习工具，整合转录组、形态和拓扑信息，但主要聚焦于表征学习与聚类，而非虚拟细胞/器官基座模型或生物大语言模型。
card:
## 是什么
AESTETIK 是一个基于卷积自编码器的多模态表示学习工具，用于从空间转录组数据中学习 spot 级别的低维表示。它整合了转录组、形态学和空间拓扑信息，以捕捉生物复杂性，并支持下游任务如聚类和形态学分析。

## 亮点
- **多模态融合**：在 spot 级别整合转录组和形态学信息，在邻域级别整合拓扑信息，实现更全面的表示。
- **模块化设计**：基于 Lightning 框架重写，提供 `fit()`/`predict()` API，遵循 scikit-learn 估计器接口，易于集成。
- **可扩展性**：支持多样本同时处理，并可选集成 Harmony、scVI 等跨样本对齐方法。
- **性能验证**：在 2024 年 Mammoth 国际组学竞赛中获欧洲区第一名，并有论文发表于 Bioinformatics。
- **易用性**：通过 pip 安装，提供示例 notebook 和模拟数据教程。

## 为何对本课题有用
本仓库直接面向空间转录组学，是虚拟细胞/虚拟器官研究中的关键数据模态。其核心价值在于：
- **表示学习**：为空间转录组数据提供高质量的 spot 表示，可作为生物基座模型（如虚拟细胞模型）的输入特征或预训练目标。
- **多模态整合**：展示了如何融合转录组、形态学和空间拓扑，为构建多模态生物大语言模型提供方法论参考。
- **跨样本对齐**：支持 Harmony、scVI 等对齐方法，有助于处理多批次数据，是构建大规模虚拟器官图谱的基础。
- **下游任务**：学习到的表示可直接用于聚类、域检测等，为 Bio Agent 提供可解释的细胞状态特征。

## 怎么用
- **安装**：`pip install aestetik` 或通过 `environment.yaml` 创建 conda 环境（依赖见 `environment.yaml`）。
- **主入口**：`from aestetik import AESTETIK`，使用 `fit()`、`transform()`、`predict()` 方法。
- **输入数据**：AnnData 对象，包含转录组表达矩阵（`.X`）和可选的形态学特征（需通过 pyvips 提取）。
- **输出**：`adata.obsm["AESTETIK"]` 为表示向量，`adata.obs["AESTETIK_cluster"]` 为聚类标签。
- **示例**：`example/gettingStartedWithAESTETIK.ipynb` 和模拟数据 notebook。
- **GPU**：需要 GPU 加速训练（PyTorch 依赖）。
- **测试**：`pytest` 运行测试套件，包含集成测试（标记为 `slow`）。

## 核心 idea
核心方法学在于通过多三元组损失（multi-triplet loss）联合优化转录组、形态学和拓扑信息，使自编码器学习到的表示能够同时保留分子、形态和空间邻域关系，从而更准确地反映细胞状态。

## 可搬移点
- **多模态融合模块**：`src/aestetik/modules/aestetik_module.py` 中的编码器-解码器结构和融合逻辑，可解耦后用于自定义多模态表示学习 Pipeline。
- **损失函数**：`src/aestetik/metrics/loss_function.py` 中的多三元组损失实现，可移植到其他对比学习任务。
- **数据预处理工具**：`src/aestetik/utils/` 下的转录组和形态学预处理函数，可独立使用。
- **跨样本对齐集成**：`src/aestetik/utils/utils_clustering.py` 中的 Harmony/scVI 集成逻辑，可借鉴用于批次校正。
- **License**：MIT，允许自由使用和修改，但需保留版权声明。

# AESTETIK: AutoEncoder for Spatial Transcriptomics Expression with Topology and Image Knowledge

This model is part of the paper "Representation learning for multi-modal spatially resolved transcriptomics data".

**Authors**: Kalin Nonchev, Sonali Andani, Joanna Ficek-Pascual, Marta Nowak, Bettina Sobottka, Tumor Profiler Consortium, Viktor Hendrik Koelzer, and Gunnar Rätsch

The preprint is available [here](https://www.medrxiv.org/content/10.1101/2024.06.04.24308256v1).

## News

  - [09.2026] Introducing [Aurora](https://www.auroraomics.org) - a no-code platform for virtual spatial transcriptomics from H&E images. Aurora makes virtual spatial transcriptomics accessible without requiring users to have their own GPUs, with a fully automated workflow designed to ensure that spatial transcriptomics predictions are performed correctly. Try the interactive [Aurora demo](https://www.auroraomics.org/demo).
  - [06.2026] New generation model [DeepSpot-M: a multimodal foundation model for transcriptome-wide virtual spatial transcriptomics from histology](https://www.medrxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.06.19.26356060v1). [Code.](https://github.com/ratschlab/DeepSpotM)
  - [05.2026] [Representation learning for multi-modal spatially resolved transcriptomics data](https://academic.oup.com/bioinformatics/advance-article/doi/10.1093/bioinformatics/btag316/8692433) has been published in Bioinformatics (Oxford)
  - [03.2026] [Towards Cross-Sample Alignment for Multi-Modal Representation Learning in Spatial Transcriptomics](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.03.02.709002v1) will be at ICLR 2026 Learning Meaningful Representations of Life 
  - [09.2025] AESTETIK now supports multi-modal (e.g., H&E images, spatial transcriptomics) and cross-sample integration using Harmony, scVI, etc.
  - [08.2024] AESTETIK secured the 1st place at the Mammoth International Contest On Omics Sciences in Europe 2024 organized by China National GeneBank, BGI Genomics, MGI and CODATA [link](https://micos.cngb.org/europe/index.html).

## Changelog
**NEW version (June 2025)**
  - **UPDATE:** Rewrote AESTETIK using the Lightning framework for improved modularity
  - **Added:** New `fit()/predict()` API
  - **Added:** Support for processing multiple samples at once
  - **Removed:** Multiple old methods and parameters in AESTETIK 

See [full changelog](CHANGELOG.md) for more details.
    
## Do you want to gain a multi-modal understanding of key biological processes through spatial transcriptomics?

We introduce AESTETIK, a convolutional autoencoder model. It jointly integrates transcriptomics and morphology information, on a spot level, and topology, on a neighborhood level, to learn accurate spot representations that capture biological complexity.

![aestetik](/figures/aestetik.png)

**Fig. 1 AESTETIK integrates spatial, transcriptomics, and morphology information to learn accurate spot representations.**
**A**: Spatial transcriptomics enables in-depth molecular characterization of samples on a morphology and RNA level while preserving spatial location. **B**: Workflow of AESTETIK. Initially, the transcriptomics and morphology spot representations are preprocessed. Next, a dimensionality reduction technique (e.g., PCA) is applied. Subsequently, the processed spot representations are clustered separately to acquire labels required for the multi-triplet loss. Afterwards, the modality-specific representations are fused through concatenation and the grid per spot is built. This is used as an input for the autoencoder. Lastly, the spatial-, transcriptomics-, and morphology-informed spot representations are obtained and used for downstream tasks such as clustering, morphology analysis, etc.

## Setup

We can install aestetik directly through pip.

```
pip install aestetik
```

We can also create a conda environment with the required packages.

```
conda env create --file=environment.yaml
```

We can also install aestetik offline.

```
git clone https://github.com/ratschlab/aestetik
cd aestetik
pip install .
```

Optional extras:

```
pip install ".[vips]"   # enables pyvips-based morphology helpers
pip install ".[viz]"    # enables plotnine-based cluster-search plot
pip install ".[test]"   # test dependencies (pytest)
```

##### NB: The morphology spot-extraction helpers require [pyvips](https://github.com/libvips/pyvips). We recommend installing pyvips through conda:
```
conda install conda-forge::pyvips
```

## Getting Started

After installing, confirm the version with `import aestetik;
aestetik.__version__`. AESTETIK follows the scikit-learn ``fit`` /
``transform`` / ``predict`` estimator surface:

```python
from aestetik import AESTETIK

model = AESTETIK(
    n_cluster=adata.obs.ground_truth.unique().size,
    morphology_weight=1.5,
    refine_cluster=True,
    window_size=3,
    clustering_method="kmeans",
)
model.fit(adata)
adata.obsm["AESTETIK"]        = model.transform(adata)
adata.obs["AESTETIK_cluster"] = model.predict(adata)

# Or in one shot:
adata.obs["AESTETIK_cluster"] = model.fit_predict(adata)
```

Please take a look at our [example](example/gettingStartedWithAESTETIK.ipynb) to get started with AESTETIK.

![aestetik](/figures/maynard_human_brain_analysis_151676_Transcriptomics_Morphology_AESTETIK.png)

[Here](example/gettingStartedWithAESTETIKwithSimulatedData.ipynb), another example notebook with [simulated spatial transcriptomics data](https://github.com/ratschlab/simulate_spatial_transcriptomics_tool).

![aestetik](/figures/AESTETIK_clustering.png)

## Related Projects

- [DeepSpot-M](https://github.com/ratschlab/DeepSpotM) — Multimodal foundation model for transcriptome-wide virtual spatial transcriptomics from H&E images. Represents genes as queryable embeddings, so it spans the protein-coding transcriptome including genes unseen during training.

Use it to embed genes, proteins, small molecules, morphology perturbations, and single cells; annotate the resulting objects; and compare embeddings with scverse-friendly plotting and analysis utilities.

## What embpy Does - Embeds biological entities through `BioEmbedder.embed(...)`. - Resolves biological identifiers into model-ready inputs, such as gene sequences, protein sequences, SMILES strings, and morphology images. - Returns AnnData, tables, or payloads with provenance and canonical IDs. - Stores generated embeddings outside `.X`, using `.obsm`, `.varm`, or `.uns` according to the entity type. - Adds real metadata annotations for genes, proteins, molecules, and cell lines. - Provides plotting and comparison helpers for embedding quality checks. ## 📖 Documentation Complete, interactive documentation and API references are available: - 🌐 **[Online Documentation](https://theislab.github.io/embpy/)** | **[ReadTheDocs](https://embpy.readthedocs.io/)** - 📂 **Documentation Guides in this Repository**: - [📘 **Overview & Architecture**](docs/index.md) - [🚀 **Getting Started & Installation**](docs/getting-started.md) - [🧪 **Hands-On Workflows & Practical Recipes**](docs/hands-on.md) - [💻 **Cross-Platform & Hardware Guide**](docs/cross-platform.md) - [🏛️ **Architecture & Technical Design**](docs/technical.md) - [📚 **API Reference**](docs/api-reference.md) - [🤝 **Contributing Guide**](docs/contributing.md) ### Running Documentation Locally ```bash pip install mkdocs-material "mkdocstrings[python]" mkdocs serve ``` Open **[http://127.0.0.1:8000](http://127.0.0.1:8000)** in your browser for live-reloaded documentation. ## Install > **Requires Python ≥ 3.11.** Check with `python --version` or `python3 --version` before starting. There are **two main install flavours** — pick one based on your hardware: | Flavour | When to use | | --- | --- | | `embpy[cpu]` | No NVIDIA GPU, or just getting started | | `embpy[gpu]` | NVIDIA GPU with CUDA available | A bare install gives the lightweight core (resolvers, IO, annotation, plotting) but **no embedding backends**. For real use, always pick `[cpu]` or `[gpu]`. > **GPU note (V100 / Volta):** the default `[gpu]` install gets PyTorch's CUDA 13 build, which supports GPUs from the Turing generation onwards (`sm_75` and newer, e.g. A100, H100) but not Volta (`sm_70`). On a V100 it reports CUDA as available, then every operation fails with `no kernel image is available`. Install the CUDA 12.6 build instead, which still supports Volta: > ```bash > # pip: install that torch first; embpy then keeps it > pip install torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu126 > pip install "embpy[gpu]" > > # uv: one line > uv pip install "embpy[gpu]" --torch-backend=cu126 > ``` --- ### 🐧 Linux / macOS **Option A — with `pip` (standard):** ```bash # CPU-only (Note: On Linux pip, you must install torch first to avoid the CUDA bundle) pip install torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu pip install "embpy[cpu]" # GPU (NVIDIA CUDA) pip install "embpy[gpu]" ``` **Option B — with `uv` (faster resolver, recommended):** ```bash # Create and activate an environment first (uv installs into it) uv venv --python 3.12 && source .venv/bin/activate # CPU-only uv pip install "embpy[cpu]" # GPU (NVIDIA CUDA) uv pip install "embpy[gpu]" ``` **Quick verification:** ```bash python -c "import embpy, torch; from embpy import BioEmbedder; print(embpy.__version__, torch.__version__, torch.cuda.is_available())" ``` --- ### 🪟 Windows On Windows, `pip` is tied to a specific Python version. Use `py -3.12` (or whichever Python ≥ 3.11 you have installed) to be explicit: **Step 1 — Check your Python version:** ```powershell py --list # shows all installed Python versions py -3.12 --version # confirm 3.12 is available ``` **Step 2 — Install embpy:** ```powershell # CPU-only (recommended for most Windows users) py -3.12 -m pip install "embpy[cpu]" # GPU (only if you have an NVIDIA GPU with CUDA) py -3.12 -m pip install "embpy[gpu]" ``` **Step 3 — Verify:** ```powershell py -3.12 -c "import embpy, torch; from embpy import BioEmbedder; print(embpy.__version__, torch.__version__, torch.cuda.is_available())" ``` > **Note:** `pysam` and `pyensembl` (genome access) are **not available on Windows** — these are Linux/macOS only. All other backends work natively on Windows. --- ### 🧪 Installing from Source (for development / contributors) If you are developing `embpy` or running the test suite, clone the repository and install in editable mode: **🐧 Linux / macOS:** ```bash # With test dependencies + run tests git clone https://github.com/theislab/embpy.git cd embpy pip install -e ".[test]" python -m pytest tests/ -v # Core only (no ML backends) pip install -e . ``` **🪟 Windows:** ```powershell # With test dependencies + run tests git clone https://github.com/theislab/embpy.git cd embpy py -3.12 -m pip install -e ".[test]" py -3.12 -m pytest tests/ -v # Core only (no ML backends) py -3.12 -m pip install -e . ``` **Verify the install:** ```bash # Linux / macOS -- core or [test] install (no PyTorch) python -c "import embpy; print(embpy.__version__)" # Linux / macOS -- [cpu] or [gpu] install python -c "import embpy, torch; print(embpy.__version__, torch.__version__)" # Windows -- core or [test] install (no PyTorch) py -3.12 -c "import embpy; print(embpy.__version__)" # Windows -- [cpu] or [gpu] install py -3.12 -c "import embpy, torch; print(embpy.__version__, torch.__version__)" ``` > Once this branch is merged into `main` and a new version is published to PyPI, > the same commands work without the `@ git+...` part, e.g. `pip install "embpy[gpu]"`. --- ### 🖥️ On an HPC cluster (Slurm) A cluster node is a Linux machine, so **the Linux / macOS commands above work unchanged**. This section only adds what is specific to a shared cluster: where to run them, where the caches go, and which GPUs the default build supports. Verified on the Helmholtz Munich HPC; adjust partition/QoS names for your site. **1. Work on a compute node, not the login node.** The tutorials are small enough for CPU: ```bash srun --partition=interactive_cpu_p --qos=interactive_cpu --cpus-per-task=8 --mem=16G --time=04:00:00 --pty bash ``` If you see `QOSMaxMemoryPerJob`, that is a **policy cap, not a shortage** — ask for less memory, not more. 16G is enough here. **2. Keep caches out of your home directory.** pip, uv and Hugging Face cache downloads under `~/.cache`, and home quotas are usually small: each install leaves 1–3 GB of wheels there, and model weights add more. Point the caches at project storage (replace the path): ```bash export PROJECT=/path/to/your/project/space export PIP_CACHE_DIR=$PROJECT/.cache/pip UV_CACHE_DIR=$PROJECT/.cache/uv HF_HOME=$PROJECT/.cache/huggingface export UV_LINK_MODE=copy # the uv cache and the environment are often on different filesystems ``` **3. Create an environment and install, exactly as on Linux:** ```bash uv venv .venv --python 3.12 && source .venv/bin/activate uv pip install "embpy[cpu]" # CPU node uv pip install "embpy[gpu]" # GPU node ``` The default `[gpu]` build runs on GPUs from the Turing generation onwards (`sm_75` and newer, e.g. A100, H100). Older **V100** (Volta) GPUs report CUDA as available, but every operation then fails with `no kernel image is available`. On those nodes, ask uv for the CUDA 12.6 build instead: ```bash uv pip install "embpy[gpu]" --torch-backend=cu126 ``` **4. Run the notebooks.** They live in the repository, so clone it first: ```bash git clone https://github.com/theislab/embpy.git && cd embpy uv pip install ipykernel jupyter jupyter nbconvert --to notebook --execute docs/notebooks/01_embed_any_model.ipynb --output /tmp/out.ipynb ``` To work on embpy itself, install the clone instead of the git URL: `uv pip install -e ".[cpu]"`. **Or run them interactively.** Start a server on the compute node: ```bash jupyter lab --no-browser --ip=0.0.0.0 --port=8899 ``` Jupyter prints a URL with a random token. Open it as `http://:8899/lab?token=` (`hostname` gives the node), through an SSH tunnel from your laptop if the node is not directly reachable: `ssh -N -L 8899::8899 `, then use `localhost:8899`. Do not set a fixed token such as `embpy`: anyone who can reach the node could then open your session, and with it a shell under your account. Do not background the server with `Ctrl+Z` — use `nohup ... &` if you need the prompt back. ---
Backends that must be installed separately A few backends cannot be installed by pip on an arbitrary machine, so they are in neither extra. embpy degrades gracefully without them, and asking for one of their models raises a typed `DependencyError` naming the command to run. Every line below was checked by resolving it with `uv pip compile`; the "Status" column says what actually happens today rather than what is intended. | Backend | Install | Status / why it is separate | | --- | --- | --- | | Caduceus | `uv pip install "embpy[caduceus]"` | resolves cleanly (`mamba-ssm`), but the wheel builds against your installed torch — install the matching torch first. Needs a CUDA toolchain if no wheel matches. | | Scooby | `uv pip install "embpy[scooby]" "scooby @ git+https://github.com/gagneurlab/scooby.git"` | the `scooby` model package is published on GitHub only, so it is installed by URL next to the extra. (The `scooby` on PyPI is an unrelated project.) | | Evo (v1/v1.5) | `uv pip install "embpy[evo]"` | **Linux only.** Depends on `triton`, which publishes no macOS wheels, so this is unsatisfiable on macOS. | | Evo 2 | `uv pip install "embpy[evo2]"` | **needs Python 3.11 or 3.12** — `evo2` declares `requires-python >=3.11,<3.13`, so it cannot install into a 3.13 environment at all. Needs its own venv (below). | | Flashzoi | `uv pip install "embpy[flashzoi]" --no-build-isolation` | the four `flashzoi_*` keys set `flashed=true` and need `flash_attn`, which is NVIDIA-only and builds against your installed torch. The eight plain `borzoi_*` keys need none of it. | | Boltz-2 | `uv pip install "embpy[boltz]"` | **downgrades numpy to 1.26** (boltz pins `numpy<2`). Everything compiled against numpy 2 in the same environment is at risk — prefer a dedicated environment. | | MiniMol | `uv pip install "embpy[minimol]"` | needs `--no-build-isolation`: `torch-sparse`/`torch-scatter` build against an already-installed torch. Install torch first, then this extra with that flag. | | ESM-C / ESM3 | `uv pip install "embpy[cpu]"` then `uv pip install esm --no-deps` | installing the extra normally **caps transformers at 4.48.1** (the `esm` SDK pins `<4.48.2`), which also silently moves borzoi-pytorch onto a 0.4.x release. `--no-deps` avoids both — `esm` works with newer transformers. ESM3 weights are additionally licence-gated. | | NT v3 | `uv pip install "embpy[ntv3]"` | needs no extra package; the barrier is **access**. The `InstaDeepAI/NTv3_*` repositories are gated, so accept the licence on the model page and `huggingface-cli login` (or set `HF_TOKEN`). | | AlphaGenome | `uv pip install "embpy[alphagenome]"` | API client, needs a key — no local weights | | single-cell FMs | `uv pip install "embpy[helical]"` | pins torch/transformers and needs the igraph C library. Cannot coexist with `arc-state` or `cell-eval` through a resolver — see the single-cell recipe below. | **Gated weights are not a packaging problem.** NT v3 and ESM3 install fine and then fail at download with a 401 until you have accepted the licence and authenticated. embpy reports this as an access error naming the model page, not as a missing package, so the two cases are distinguishable. **Some extras move shared pins.** `[esm3]` and `[boltz]` change `transformers` and `numpy` for the whole environment. uv will not warn you: both are *legal* resolutions rather than conflicts, so the downgrade is silent even if the extras are declared as conflicting. The remedies are per-case, below. #### Backends that want their own environment Four cases cannot share an environment with the standard install. Give each its own venv — embpy is identical in all of them, only the affected models differ. **Evo 2 — forced by the interpreter.** `evo2` requires Python `>=3.11,<3.13`, so no flag makes it install into a 3.13 environment: ```bash uv venv --python 3.12 .venv-evo2 uv pip install --python .venv-evo2/bin/python "embpy[evo2]" ``` **Flashzoi — forced by the build.** `flash-attn` ships no wheels and compiles against an already-installed torch, so it is two steps and NVIDIA-only: ```bash uv venv --python 3.12 .venv-flashzoi uv pip install --python .venv-flashzoi/bin/python "embpy[gpu]" uv pip install --python .venv-flashzoi/bin/python "embpy[flashzoi]" --no-build-isolation ``` **Boltz-2 — forced by numpy.** `boltz` pins `numpy<2`, putting every package compiled against numpy 2 in the same environment at risk: ```bash uv venv --python 3.12 .venv-boltz uv pip install --python .venv-boltz/bin/python "embpy[boltz]" ``` **Single-cell foundation models — forced by three mutually exclusive pins.** `helical` (scGPT, Geneformer, UCE) declares `numpy>=2.1.3,<2.3` and `transformers<=4.51.3`; `arc-state` (STATE) needs `transformers>=4.52.3`; and `cell-eval` pulls `pdex`, which needs `numpy>=2.4.2`. No Python version satisfies all three, so a resolver rejects the combination outright rather than picking badly. The helical ceilings turn out to be stale, though, so `--no-deps` plus its real runtime dependencies gets one environment with all of them (verified on linux-64: scGPT, Geneformer, scVI, STATE and PCA all embed): ```bash uv venv --python 3.13 .venv-sc uv pip install --python .venv-sc/bin/python \ arc-state arc-stack scvi-tools scib scib-metrics "cell-eval>=0.7.2" scanpy uv pip install --python .venv-sc/bin/python -e . # embpy *with* its deps uv pip install --python .venv-sc/bin/python --no-deps helical uv pip install --python .venv-sc/bin/python \ "datasets==3.6.0" einops sentencepiece biopython catalogue \ pybiomart requests-cache uv pip install --python .venv-sc/bin/python "transformers==4.57.6" ``` Five details are load-bearing, each of which fails in its own way: | Detail | What breaks without it | | --- | --- | | `--no-deps helical` | resolution fails, or numpy is dragged below 2.3 | | `datasets==3.6.0` exactly | Geneformer: `'Column' object has no attribute 'device'` | | `transformers==4.57.6`, not 5.x | embpy pins `huggingface-hub<1.0.0`, which lacks the `is_offline_mode` transformers 5 imports | | `-e .` *without* `--no-deps` | embpy's own light core (rdkit, sklearn) is missing, and the import errors look like model problems | | `scib` *and* `scib-metrics` | different packages; `tl.compute_scib_metrics` imports the first, so only installing the second raises `DependencyError` | `stack` installs and loads but then fails inside arc-stack's own h5ad reader (`Could not find gene names in the file`) even when `gene_name_col` is supplied — upstream, not embpy. `state` fetches ~12 GB of weights on first use unless you pass `model_kwargs={"state": {"checkpoint": ...}}`. **ESM-C / ESM3 does *not* need its own environment.** Install `[cpu]` or `[gpu]` normally and add `esm` with `--no-deps`, as in the table above. Asking for a model whose backend is absent raises a typed `DependencyError` naming the install line, so a missing backend stays distinguishable from a broken checkpoint or a gated repository.
## Quick Start ```python from embpy import BioEmbedder embedder = BioEmbedder(device="auto", organism="human") ``` Embed genes with multiple model families: ```python gene_adata = embedder.embed( ["TP53", "EGFR", "MYC"], entity_type="gene", id_type="symbol", model=["hyenadna_tiny_1k", "esm2_8M", "minilm_l6_v2"], output="anndata", ) gene_adata.varm.keys() gene_adata.uns["embeddings"].keys() ``` Embed gene perturbation labels as row-aligned action embeddings: ```python # pert_adata.obs["perturbation"] contains symbols such as TP53/MYC. pert_adata = embedder.embed( pert_adata, entity_type="gene", obs_column="perturbation", id_type="symbol", model="esm2_650M", output="anndata", is_perturbation=True, key="X_pert_esm2_650M", ) pert_adata.obsm["X_pert_esm2_650M"] ``` Embed proteins: ```python protein_adata = embedder.embed( ["TP53", "EGFR", "BRCA1"], entity_type="protein", id_type="symbol", model="esm2_8M", output="anndata", ) ``` Embed small molecules: ```python smiles = [ "CC(=O)OC1=CC=CC=C1C(=O)O", # aspirin "Cn1cnc2c1c(=O)n(C)c(=O)n2C", # caffeine ] molecule_adata = embedder.embed( smiles, entity_type="molecule", id_type="smiles", model="morgan_fp", output="anndata", key="X_morgan_fp", ) ``` Embed cells from AnnData with model-aware preprocessing: ```python cell_adata = embedder.embed( adata, entity_type="cell", model="pca", preprocessing="auto", output="anndata", key="X_pca", ) cell_adata.obsm["X_pca"] cell_adata.uns["embpy_cell_embeddings"] ``` Annotate and plot: ```python from embpy import tl, pl molecule_adata.obs["smiles"] = molecule_adata.obs_names molecule_adata = tl.annotate_molecules( molecule_adata, column="smiles", sources=["structural", "bioactivity", "ontology"], ) pl.plot_embedding_space( molecule_adata, obsm_key="X_morgan_fp", method="pca", color="mol_logp", ) ``` ## Tutorials **Start here** — a short, goal-oriented path: 1. [Embed with any model](docs/notebooks/01_embed_any_model.ipynb) — the full model catalog, then one embedding call per family (DNA, protein, molecule, text, …). 2. [Where embeddings live](docs/notebooks/02_output_contract.ipynb) — the `.obsm` / `.varm` / `.uns` storage contract and provenance. 3. [Comparing embeddings](docs/notebooks/03_compare_embeddings.ipynb) — every metric for asking whether two models encode the same structure, and which to use when. 4. [Which model captures *my* biology?](docs/notebooks/04_benchmark_models.ipynb) — rank models on your own labelled task. 5. [What else does embpy know about your entities?](docs/notebooks/05_annotate_entities.ipynb) — the annotation layer: physicochemical properties, the ChEMBL clinical record (phase, indications, safety, ATC, mechanism, targets), gene pathways and protein function. Network-bound, no weights, and the source of labels your analysis did not choose. 6. [Reading a model's attention](docs/notebooks/06_attention_weights.ipynb) — extract per-layer attention and reduce it to AnnData-ready summaries. **By modality** — deeper, domain-specific workflows: - [Genes](docs/notebooks/genes.ipynb) - [Proteins](docs/notebooks/proteins.ipynb) - [Small molecules](docs/notebooks/small_molecules.ipynb) - [Cells](docs/notebooks/cells.ipynb) - [Variant effects](docs/notebooks/variant_effects.ipynb) Each notebook uses real `BioEmbedder.embed(...)` calls, real annotation APIs, and embpy plotting/comparison utilities. ## Model Families embpy supports models across: - DNA and regulatory sequence models - protein language and structure models - small-molecule fingerprints and chemical language models - single-cell foundation models and classical baselines - morphology models for HPA and JUMP-style images - text models for biological descriptions Use: ```python embedder.list_available_models() ``` for the model keys available in your environment. ## Output Contract `BioEmbedder.embed(...)` follows a scverse-friendly output contract: - genes are feature-like and live in `.varm` by default - gene perturbation labels use `is_perturbation=True` and live in `.obsm` - proteins are feature-like and live in `.varm` - molecules, text, sequences, and cells are observation-like and live in `.obsm` - perturbation/action embeddings can be kept entity-aligned in `.uns` - `.X` remains expression/count-like data or a sparse placeholder See the [Architecture & Technical Guide](docs/technical.md#standardized-output-contracts) for the full contract. ## Citation If you use embpy in your work, please cite the repository for now. A formal citation will be added when the package is released. ## Contact For questions, issues, or feature requests, open a GitHub issue or contact the maintainers listed in the package metadata.

one_liner: 该仓库是NicheJEPA的可复现性代码，专注于单细胞/空间转录组数据的tokenization和数据集构建，为细胞基座模型提供数据预处理，但本身不包含模型训练或Agent实现。
card:
## 是什么

这是一个用于复现 **NicheJEPA** 的代码仓库。NicheJEPA 是一种基于 **联合嵌入预测架构（JEPA）** 的细胞邻域表示学习模型，旨在从单细胞/空间组学数据中学习细胞及其微环境（niche）的通用表征。该仓库提供了从数据预处理、tokenization（细胞邻域/细胞图）、模型训练到下游分析（如迁移学习、消融实验、基准测试）的完整流程，主要面向空间转录组学数据（如 MERFISH、STARmap、Slide-seq、Xenium 等）。

## 亮点

- **模块化流程**：将数据准备、tokenization、训练、分析清晰分离，每个步骤都有独立的脚本和配置文件，便于复现和扩展。
- **多种 tokenization 策略**：支持 **CellNeighborhoodTokenizer** 和 **CellGraphTokenizer**，分别将细胞邻域和细胞图结构转化为 token 序列，适配不同下游任务。
- **大规模数据处理**：支持多数据集、多物种、多组织、多基因 panel 的整合，并提供了数据模拟脚本（如生成多基因 panel 的半合成数据）来增强训练数据的多样性。
- **丰富的下游分析**：包含迁移学习（如 Visium 数据）、消融实验、与多种基线模型（如 Banksy、CellCharter、CellPLM、Nicheformer、scGPT、STformer 等）的基准测试，验证模型有效性。
- **工程化支持**：提供 LSF 集群作业包装脚本，便于在高性能计算环境（如 farm22）上运行大规模任务。

## 为何对本课题有用

本仓库直接面向 **虚拟细胞/虚拟器官 × 单细胞/空间组学 × 生物基座模型** 方向，是构建空间组学基础模型的重要参考实现。

- **表征学习**：NicheJEPA 通过 JEPA 架构学习细胞邻域的上下文表征，这种自监督方法可迁移到虚拟细胞模型中，用于捕捉细胞间相互作用和微环境状态。
- **Tokenization 方法**：细胞邻域和细胞图 tokenization 是将空间组学数据转化为适合大语言模型（LLM）输入的 token 序列的关键步骤，本仓库提供了可复用的实现，可直接用于构建生物大语言模型的输入管道。
- **多数据集整合**：仓库展示了如何整合来自不同平台、物种、组织的空间数据，这对于构建跨组织、跨物种的虚拟器官模型至关重要。
- **迁移学习**：提供了在 Visium 等新数据上微调预训练模型的示例，这种能力是生物基座模型落地应用的核心。
- **基准测试框架**：提供了与多种现有模型的对比流程，可用于评估新模型在虚拟细胞任务上的性能。

## 怎么用

- **主入口**：仓库没有单一主程序，而是通过多个脚本执行不同阶段。主要入口包括：
  - 数据模拟：`analysis/data_simulation/create_semi-synthetic-data_multiple-gene-panels.py` 和 `create_semi-synthetic-data_multiple-assays.py`，通过 `--config_file` 指定 YAML 配置。
  - Tokenization：`analysis/tokenization/create_cell_tokenized_dataset.py`，同样通过配置文件运行。
  - 训练：`analysis/model_training/train_model.sh`（具体训练脚本未在 README 中详述）。
  - 分析：多个 Jupyter notebook 和 Python 脚本，如 `analysis/Transfer_learning_visium/finetune_Visium_IJEPA.py`。
- **安装与依赖**：仓库未提供统一的安装文件，但 `envs/` 目录下包含多个环境配置文件（如 `banksy.sh`、`cellcharter.sh` 等），用于创建不同模型的环境。核心依赖包括 `anndata`、`huggingface` datasets、`torch` 等（具体版本未在 README 中说明）。
- **输入/输出数据格式**：
  - 输入：预处理后的 AnnData 文件（`.h5ad`），包含基因表达矩阵和空间坐标。
  - 输出：tokenized 的 Hugging Face dataset（用于训练），以及模型嵌入（如 `.npy` 或 `.csv` 文件）。
- **GPU 需求**：模型训练和推理需要 GPU 加速，但具体显存要求未在 README 中说明。
- **调试示例**：仓库提供了多个 Jupyter notebook（如 `analysis/Transfer_learning_visium/Prep_QC_data.ipynb`、`analysis/data_analysis/perturbation_notebook.ipynb`）和单元测试（如 `analysis/testing/` 下的 notebook），可用于断点调试和验证流程。

## 核心 idea

NicheJEPA 的核心思想是 **利用 JEPA（联合嵌入预测架构）在细胞邻域级别进行自监督学习**：通过掩码预测（masked prediction）学习细胞及其邻域的上下文表征，从而捕捉空间转录组数据中的局部微环境模式，而无需显式标签。这种架构避免了对比学习中的负样本问题，能够更高效地学习高维生物数据中的结构特征。

## 可搬移点

- **Tokenization 模块**：`analysis/tokenization/cell_neighborhood_tokenization.ipynb` 和 `cell_graph_tokenization` 相关代码，可解耦并移植到自定义 Pipeline 中，用于将空间组学数据转换为 token 序列，供生物大语言模型使用。
- **数据模拟脚本**：`analysis/data_simulation/create_semi-synthetic-data_multiple-gene-panels.py` 和 `create_semi-synthetic-data_multiple-assays.py`，可用于生成多基因 panel 或多 assay 的训练数据，增强模型泛化能力。
- **迁移学习流程**：`analysis/Transfer_learning_visium/` 下的脚本和 notebook，展示了如何将预训练模型微调到新数据，可借鉴到虚拟器官模型的跨组织迁移。
- **基准测试框架**：`analysis/benchmarking/` 下的 notebook 和脚本，提供了与多种基线模型的对比方法，可用于评估新模型。
- **License**：README 未说明 License，需确认。

# nichejepa-reproducibility

## Datasets

List of datasets: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1bfdBZ1MZEVKz2-4Ge89zwe5jVT4qnXAndStmXmJehTo/edit?gid=1836124407#gid=1836124407

`/lustre/scratch126/cellgen/team361/DATASETS/` houses all the data across experiments. An experiment is defined as a collection of anndata objects that may be from the same or different datasets, species, tissues, gene panels, and batches. 
- `silver` -- contains preprocessed AnnData files
- `gold` -- contains tokenized datasets
- `tokenizer` -- contains intermediate tokenizer files such as token dictionaries

### Preparing Semi-Real Experiment data comprising of Multiple Gene Panels:
For each batch of AnnData in the input directory, this script creates `n_gene_panels` new batches of AnnData, one per new gene panel. The new gene panels are created by randomly selecting genes from the original gene list according to the following procedure:
1. A fixed number of genes are shared between all gene panels.
2. The remaining genes are divided into `n_gene_panels` subsets according to the `subset_ratios` parameter.
3. The shared genes and the genes in each subset are concatenated to form the gene panels.

Usage:
```
python analysis/data_simulation/create_semi-synthetic-data_multiple-gene-panels.py --config_file [CONFIG-FILE]
```
To create `mmb0-300k-2b_2p` from `mmb0-300k-2b_1p`, use `config/multiple-gene-panels/multiple-gene-panels_mmb0-300k-2b_1p_to_mmb0-300k-2b_2p.yaml`
- `mmb0-300k-2b_1p` -- Merfish Mouse Brain | Batches 217, 218 | 1 gene panel
- `mmb0-300k-2b_2p` -- Merfish Mouse Brain | Batches 217, 218 | 2 gene panel (semi-real)


### Preparing Semi-Real Experiment data comprising of Multiple Assays with Shared Genes:
"""
For each batch of AnnData in the input directory, this script creates a list of shared gene symbols across all batches. It then creates a new batch of AnnData for each batch in the input directory with only the shared genes. The new batches are saved in the output directory.

Usage:
```
python create_semi-synthetic-data_multiple-assays.py --config_file [CONFIG-FILE]
```

To create `mmb0-1b_smb1-1b_1p` from `mmb0-1b_smb1-1b_2p`, use `config/multiple-assays/multiple-assays_mmb0-1b_smb1-1b_2p_to_mmb0-1b_smb1-1b_1p.yaml`
- `mmb0-1b_smb1-1b_2p` -- Merfish Mouse Brain | Batch 82 | Starmap Plus Mouse CNS | Batch 15 | 2 gene panels
- `mmb0-1b_smb1-1b_1p` -- Merfish Mouse Brain | Batch 82 | Starmap Plus Mouse CNS | Batch 15 | 1 gene panels (semi-real, shared genes only)
Use `config/multiple-assays/mmb70-1b_smb71-1b_smb13-1b_3p_to_mmb70-1b_smb71-1b_smb13-1b_1p.yaml` for creating a shared gene panel from the following three datasets (CAST paper):
- `mmb70-1b` -- Merfish Mouse Brain | co1_slice37 in co1_sample13
- `smb71-1b` -- STARmap plus Mouse Brain | S1–S8, S64_1 and S64_2 from SCP1375
- `smb13-1b` -- Slide-seq Mouse Brain | Puck/Slice 42

## Tokenization

### CellNeighborhoodTokenizer:

Execute the following to create a Hugging Face dataset created using the Cell Neighborhood Tokenization from a preprocessed `anndata` object:
```
python analysis/tokenization/create_cell_tokenized_dataset.py --config_file [CONFIG-FILE] --override [OPTIONS]
```
Sample config file is available at `config/cell-neighborhood-tokenizer/cell-neighborhood-tokenizer_sss2-1b_1p`. The override flag allows you to override `overwrite` parameter which is set to `True` by default in the config files. The `overwrite` parameter controls whether a previously created token dictionary should be reused or if it should be recreated from scratch.

If you are on `farm22`, then the easier alternative is to simply use the wrapper script as follows:
```
./scripts/wrapper_create_cell_neighborhood_tokenized_dataset.sh [EXPERIMENT-NAME]
```
This will create an LSF job with the appropriate requirements and fetch the corresponding config file. Currently, the following experiment names are supported:
- `mmb0-100k-1b_1p` -- Merfish Mouse Brain | Batch 224 | 1 gene panel
- `mmb0-300k-2b_1p` -- Merfish Mouse Brain | Batches 217, 218 | 1 gene panel
- `mmb0-300k-2b_2p` -- Merfish Mouse Brain | Batches 217, 218 | 2 gene panel (semi-real)
- `mmb0-239b_1p` -- Merfish Mouse Brain | All Batches 1-239 | 1 gene panel
- `mmb0-1b_smb1-1b_1p` -- Merfish Mouse Brain | Batch 82 | Starmap Plus Mouse CNS | Batch 15 | 1 gene panels (semi-real, shared genes only)
- `mmb0-1b_smb1-1b_2p` -- Merfish Mouse Brain | Batch 82 | Starmap Plus Mouse CNS | Batch 15 | 2 gene panels
- `smb1-20b_1p` -- Starmap Plus Mouse CNS | Batches 1-20 | 1 gene panel
- `sss2-1b_1p` -- Simulated 10k | Batch 1 | 1 gene panel
- `sss3-1b_1p` -- Simulated 100k | Batch 1 | 1 gene panel
- `xhs1000-39b_1p` -- Xenium Human Skin | Batch 39 | 1 gene panel


### Adding A New Experiment:
To tokenize a new experiment, follow the steps below:
1. Choose an `[EXPERIMENT-NAME]` (e.g.`mmb0-8b_1p`)
2. Create a folder at the following location: `/lustre/scratch126/cellgen/team361/DATASETS/silver/[EXPERIMENT-NAME]`. Add the appropriate (harmonized) AnnData batch files.
3. Create a config file at the following location with this naming convention: `config/cell-neighborhood-tokenizer/cell-neighborhood-tokenizer_[EXPERIMENT-NAME].yaml`
4. Update the `experiment_name`, `experiment_description`, and potentially `num_shards`. Ideally, you shouldn't need to update any of the other parameters here if you just want to repeat the same tokenization pipeline on a new experiment.
5. Update `scripts/wrapper_create_cell_neighborhood_tokenized_dataset.sh` by adding the `RAM`, `TIME`, `CORES`, and `QUEUE` as LSF job parameters as a new case titled `[EXPERIMENT-NAME]`.


### CellGraphTokenizer:

Executing Cell Graph Tokenization from a preprocessed `anndata` object occurs in exactly the same way as the Cell Neighborhood Tokenization described above:
```
python analysis/tokenization/create_cell_tokenized_dataset.py --config_file [CONFIG-FILE] --override [OPTIONS]
```
The only difference is that the config files are stored in `config/cell-graph-tokenizer`.
The corresponding wrapper script is available at `scripts/wrapper_create_cell_graph_tokenized_dataset.sh`.


## Analysis

### Compute Cohort Statistics:
Execute the following to compute batchwise statistics of a collection of datasets comprising of one or more `anndata` objects:
```
python analysis/statistics/collect_cohort_statistics.py --cohort_name [COHORT_NAME]
```

`COHORT_NAME` can be any folder in the `silver` directory (e.g. `human_cohort1_50m`, `sss2-1b_1p`, etc.). The output will be stored in `analysis/statistics/results/[COHORT_NAME]_statistics.csv`. 
This can also be achieved by an LSF job using `./scripts/collect_cohort_statistics.sh [COHORT_NAME]`.

## 是什么

这是一个用于**零样本（zero-shot）预测 CRISPRi 基因敲低（knockdown）在未扰动细胞系中的转录响应**的代码库。它基于简单的迁移学习基线（transfer baseline），而非深度模型，旨在为 2026 年虚拟细胞挑战赛（Virtual Cell Challenge）提供一个可复现的基线方案。其核心思路是：对于目标细胞系中未测量的敲低，直接平均该敲低在其他细胞系中的已测量响应，并恢复因平均而丢失的响应幅度。

## 亮点

- **极简且可复现的基线**：不依赖复杂的深度学习模型，仅用简单的统计操作（平均、幅度恢复）即可达到与深度模型相当的性能，为后续复杂模型提供了清晰的对比基准。
- **严谨的评估框架**：构建了留一线（leave-one-line-out）的本地基准测试，并使用 `cell-eval2` 评分，同时提供了**噪声上限（noise ceiling）**和**迁移上限（transfer ceiling）**的计算代码，用于量化预测误差中可修复与不可修复的部分。
- **数据工程完备**：提供了从原始公共数据（GEO/figshare）构建六个细胞系（K562, RPE1, HepG2, Jurkat, HCT116, HEK293T）的伪批量（pseudobulk）表达谱的完整流程，并保留“未测量”为 NaN，便于后续处理。
- **工程化良好**：使用 `uv` 管理依赖，提供 Dockerfile 和 Makefile，确保环境可复现，测试和代码风格检查（pytest, ruff）均已配置。

## 为何对本课题有用

本仓库直接针对**虚拟细胞**课题中的核心问题：**跨细胞系（context）的扰动响应预测**。它提供了：

1.  **可迁移的基线方法**：对于构建**生物基座模型**或**Bio Agent**，一个简单、可解释且性能不弱的基线是评估复杂模型价值的必要前提。此仓库的“迁移平均+幅度恢复”方法可直接作为基线。
2.  **性能上限的量化工具**：`ceiling.py` 中的噪声上限和迁移上限计算，对于任何虚拟细胞模型都至关重要。它帮助研究者理解，在给定数据噪声和跨细胞系差异下，模型性能的理论极限在哪里，从而避免过度追求不可实现的精度。
3.  **数据预处理流程**：其构建伪批量表达谱的脚本（`scripts/01_build_contexts.py`）和数据处理模块（`src/zsp/data.py`）可直接用于处理**单细胞/空间组学**数据，为训练或评估基座模型提供标准化的输入格式。
4.  **不确定性分析的尝试**：虽然其不确定性信号未提升性能，但提供了评估预测置信度的方法论，这对于构建可靠的 **Bio Agent**（需要知道何时该信任模型输出）具有参考价值。

## 怎么用

- **主入口/运行命令**：项目通过 Makefile 驱动，核心命令为 `make data`（下载数据）、`make contexts`（构建伪批量）、`make benchmark`（运行本地基准测试）、`make submission`（生成提交文件）。
- **安装与依赖**：使用 `uv sync` 安装依赖，依赖列表见 `pyproject.toml`，核心包括 `anndata`, `cell-eval2`, `scanpy`, `scikit-learn` 等。提供 Dockerfile 可构建完全可复现的环境。
- **输入/输出数据格式**：输入为公共 CRISPRi Perturb-seq 筛选的原始数据（从 GEO/figshare 下载），输出为每个敲低的伪批量表达谱（`.h5ad` 格式）和提交文件（`submission.h5ad`）。
- **GPU 算力**：不需要 GPU。所有计算基于 numpy/pandas 和简单的线性代数，CPU 即可快速完成。
- **调试入口**：单元测试位于 `tests/` 目录，特别是 `tests/test_emit_exact.py` 和 `tests/test_data_models.py`，可用于验证核心逻辑。`scripts/10_noise_ceiling.py` 和 `scripts/04_uncertainty_analysis.py` 有 `--plot-only` 模式，便于快速查看结果。

## 核心 idea

其核心方法学洞察是：**在跨细胞系迁移预测中，简单的“平均”操作会系统性低估响应幅度，而通过一个基于源数据幅度的归一化因子进行恢复，可以显著提升预测性能，且其效果已接近理论上的迁移上限。** 这提示我们，在构建复杂模型前，应首先分析任务的理论性能边界，并利用简单的统计校正来逼近该边界。

## 可搬移点

- **`src/zsp/ceiling.py`**：这是最值得搬移的模块。它实现了噪声上限和迁移上限的计算，逻辑独立且测试完善。可以将其解耦，用于任何虚拟细胞预测任务的性能评估，以判断模型误差中可修复的比例。
- **`src/zsp/models.py`**：其中的 `mean_transfer` 和 `norm_restored` 模型是简单且有效的基线。可以将其作为自定义 Pipeline 的初始模型，或作为更复杂模型的初始化/对照。
- **`src/zsp/profile.py`**：伪批量构建逻辑，可复用于处理单细胞数据，生成细胞系级别的表达谱。
- **License**：MIT 许可证，允许自由使用、修改和分发，包括商业用途。可以放心搬移代码。

# zero-shot-perturbation

[![CI](https://github.com/MMatinGerami/zero-shot-perturbation/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/MMatinGerami/zero-shot-perturbation/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
<!-- cut a v0.1.0 release (none exists yet) and add the release and Zenodo badges -->

Predicting the transcriptional response to CRISPRi knockdowns in cell lines that have never been
perturbed, using only their unperturbed cells. My entry to the
[2026 Virtual Cell Challenge](https://arcinstitute.org/news/virtual-cell-challenge-2026)
(Arc Institute), with the code to reproduce it on public data.

**In one line:** a transfer baseline (average the same knockdown's measured response in other
cell lines, then restore the magnitude that averaging removes) reached rank 433 and overall score
0.137 on the validation leaderboard (October 2026); a noise ceiling and a transfer ceiling
measured from the data show that transfer models are already near what copying another line can
give (HepG2: 0.35 of 0.40), so the remaining gain has to be line-specific.

Since deep models do not yet beat simple linear baselines on this task
([Ahlmann-Eltze et al., 2025](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41592-025-02772-6)), I started from
transfer baselines rather than a foundation model.

![ceilings](results/figures/ceilings.png)

*The best model against two ceilings, per held-out line. Light grey: the noise ceiling, the
highest gene-wise correlation any prediction could reach against a response measured from 50 to
100 cells. Dark grey: the transfer ceiling, what a perfect copy of another line's response would
reach. Bar: norm-restored transfer. Medians over 200 perturbations.*

## Results at a glance

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| How far does the same knockdown transfer between lines? | After noise correction, about 0.47 correlation between HepG2 and Jurkat |
| How close is the model to that limit? | HepG2 0.35 against a transfer ceiling of 0.40; Jurkat reaches 0.24 against a centred noise ceiling of 0.72 (34%) |
| What helped on the leaderboard? | Restoring the magnitude after averaging sources: rank 559 to 524 (6 sources) to 433 (8 sources, equal weights), overall 0.079 to 0.137 |
| Does weighting sources by basal similarity help? | Not on the challenge-like line: equal weights beat similarity weights (ablation on the leaderboard, 0.137 against 0.107) |
| Can the model say which predictions to trust? | Not yet: none of five uncertainty signals changes any metric by more than 0.06 when keeping the 50% most-certain targets; kept as a negative result |
| Does transfer survive a change of study? | Partly: on HCT116 (X-Atlas, shallow knockdowns) direction transfers (fid 0.49) but gene-wise correlation falls to 0.09 |

Final test entry submitted 23 October 2026; scores are hidden until the organisers announce
results. Per-round results, the local benchmark and all tables are in
[docs/results.md](docs/results.md); every leaderboard entry is in
`results/tables/leaderboard.csv`.

## Quickstart

```bash
uv sync
make data        # about 16 GB from figshare and GEO
make contexts    # pseudobulk per screen
make benchmark   # leave-one-line-out, scored with cell-eval2
make figures
make test
```

## When to use this

- You enter the Virtual Cell Challenge and want a reproducible transfer baseline, a local
  leave-one-line-out benchmark scored with `cell-eval2`, and a fast pseudobulk evaluator that
  matches the scorer's `pds` and `mse` within a few percent.
- You want the noise-ceiling and transfer-ceiling code (`src/zsp/ceiling.py`, tested on
  simulated counts) to know how much of your error is fixable.
- You want pseudobulk contexts of six public CRISPRi screens (K562, RPE1, HepG2, Jurkat,
  HCT116, HEK293T) built from the raw releases, with "not measured" kept as NaN.

Not a trained deep model and not a winning entry: it is the baseline the deep models have to
beat, with the measurement of why.

## Data

Public CRISPRi Perturb-seq screens, reduced to one pseudobulk profile per knockdown:

- K562 and RPE1, [Replogle et al., 2022](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2022.05.013)
- HepG2 and Jurkat, [Nadig et al., 2025](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41588-025-02169-3)
- HCT116 and HEK293T (X-Atlas/Orion), [Huang et al., 2025](https://doi.org/10.1101/2025.06.11.659105)

## Limitations

- Few source lines: a target measured only in K562 is effectively a K562 prediction.
- The direction of the response is inherited from the sources, not adapted to the new line.
- Knockdown depth differs between screens, so sources are not equally informative.
- Local scores are raw `cell-eval2` metrics on public lines, not leaderboard scores.
- No validated uncertainty yet.

## Citation

```bibtex
@software{gerami2026zsp,
  author = {Gerami, Matin},
  title  = {Zero-shot perturbation-response prediction across cell contexts},
  year   = {2026},
  url    = {https://github.com/MMatinGerami/zero-shot-perturbation}
}
```

## License

MIT

## 是什么

这是一个精选列表仓库，收录了将 **Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA)** 及其变体应用于单细胞和空间组学数据的研究论文与模型。JEPA 是一种自监督学习范式，通过在潜在空间中直接预测表示来学习，该列表也涵盖将 JEPA 作为额外目标项的 JEPA-inspired 模型。仓库按单细胞组学和空间组学分类，提供论文、代码和检查点的可用性信息。

## 亮点

- **聚焦前沿方向**：专门针对 JEPA 在单细胞/空间组学中的应用，是该领域首个系统化整理的资源列表，便于快速了解最新进展。
- **信息结构化**：以表格形式清晰列出每个模型的首次发布时间、论文、潜在目标与上下文、代码和检查点状态，方便对比和筛选。
- **严格的范围界定**：明确要求论文必须应用 JEPA 或 JEPA-inspired 潜在预测目标，并区分单细胞和空间组学，保证了列表的针对性。
- **资源可用性标注**：对每个模型明确标注代码是否开源、检查点是否可获取，节省了研究者寻找资源的时间。

## 为何对本课题有用

本仓库直接服务于「虚拟细胞/虚拟器官 × 单细胞/空间组学 × 生物基座模型」课题，因为 JEPA 是构建生物基座模型的重要范式之一。它提供了：

- **方法学参考**：列出了多种 JEPA 变体在单细胞和空间组学中的具体实现，例如 PerturbJEPA 预测扰动响应、TERRA 预测空间掩码基因 token、CellWorld 预测掩码细胞等，为设计虚拟细胞模型提供直接思路。
- **模型与代码资源**：部分模型（如 PerturbJEPA、GeneJEPA、TERRA）提供了开源代码和检查点，可直接用于复现或作为基线，加速课题研究。
- **趋势洞察**：通过列表可看出 JEPA 在单细胞和空间组学中的最新应用趋势，有助于确定课题的创新点。

## 怎么用

- **主入口**：仓库本身是资源列表，无运行代码。主要入口是 `README.md`，其中包含所有模型的信息。
- **安装与依赖**：无安装要求。若要使用列表中的模型，需访问各自代码仓库（如 [PerturbJEPA](https://github.com/BGI-Hangzhou-OmicsAI/PerturbJEPA)、[GeneJEPA](https://github.com/BiostateAI/GeneJEPA)、[TERRA](https://github.com/Lotfollahi-lab/terra)）并按其说明安装。
- **输入输出数据格式**：各模型不同，例如 PerturbJEPA 使用 Parse10M 数据，GeneJEPA 使用 scRNA-seq 数据，TERRA 使用空间转录组数据。具体格式需参考各模型仓库。
- **GPU 算力**：训练和推理通常需要 GPU，具体取决于模型规模。
- **调试与示例**：部分模型提供示例代码（如 PerturbJEPA 的 examples），可参考其 README 或代码仓库中的测试。

## 核心 idea

JEPA 的核心思想是**在潜在空间中预测表示，而非重建输入**。对于单细胞和空间组学，这意味着模型学习预测掩码部分（如基因、细胞）的潜在表示，从而捕捉数据中的高阶结构和关系，这比传统的重建目标更高效且更具泛化性。该列表展示了如何将这一思想应用于生物数据，例如通过掩码基因预测细胞状态、通过空间邻居预测目标细胞等。

## 可搬移点

- **JEPA 训练目标**：可借鉴列表中各模型的 JEPA 目标设计，例如 PerturbJEPA 的潜在能量匹配、TERRA 的掩码 token 预测，将其作为自定义 Pipeline 中的训练目标。
- **模型架构**：如 GeneJEPA 的 Perceiver-style 编码器、TERRA 的多尺度编码器（基因、细胞、邻域），可解耦后移植到自己的模型中。
- **数据增强策略**：如掩码策略（块掩码、空间掩码）可迁移到其他单细胞/空间组学任务。
- **License**：列表本身采用 CC-BY-4.0，但各模型的代码和检查点 License 不同（如 PerturbJEPA 为 MIT，TERRA 为 CC-BY-NC-4.0），使用前需确认。

# Awesome Single-Cell JEPA Models

A curated list of research papers and models on **Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs)** for single-cell and spatial omics. JEPA is a self-supervised learning paradigm by directly predicting representations in latent space. JEPA also could be an extra objective term in other learning paradigm, which we called the model to be JEPA-inspired. 

For general JEPA model, could check [Awesome JEPA](https://github.com/AI-in-Transportation-Lab/awesome-jepa). Also, [I-JEPA](https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.08243) for images, and [V-JEPA 2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.09985) for video, could also be a classic start to learn about JEPA.

## AI assistant disclosure

We will use AI assistant to manage and expand this list, but all updates would be reviewed carefully by repo owner. Any [contribution](#Contributing) is welcomed, but make sure you have reviewed the content and have your own judgement. 

## Contents

- [Single-cell omics](#single-cell-omics)
- [Spatial omics](#spatial-omics)
- [Contributing](#contributing)
- [Citation](#citation)
- [License](#license)

Papers are listed newest to oldest within each section. Dates use the arXiv v1 submission record or the first bioRxiv posting. A workshop date is labeled when the first online posting date could not be verified.

**Scope.** Papers must apply a JEPA or a JEPA-inspired latent prediction objective to single-cell or spatial omics data. Hybrid methods qualify when latent prediction is part of the training objective. Papers are grouped by the omics data they model.

**Resources.** Code and checkpoints are checked separately. **Not open-sourced** indicates that no official public implementation was found. **No public checkpoint found** indicates that model weights could not be located in an official release. Resource links were checked on 16 November 2026.

Combines latent population energy matching with effect alignment, state/effect regularization, and intervention ranking; no expression reconstruction. | [Training and evaluation code](https://github.com/BGI-Hangzhou-OmicsAI/PerturbJEPA) · MIT · Released examples use Parse10M | No public checkpoint found |

Training also uses masked-base reconstruction and SIGReg. | [Training and evaluation code](https://github.com/altoslabs/scRM) · MIT | Checkpoint availability not verified |

## 是什么

`hacettepe-stem-cell` 是一个面向计算干细胞生物学、表观遗传动力学与再生医学的端到端计算平台。它整合了从 Waddington 表观遗传景观与 Langevin 随机动力学、单细胞 RNA-seq 分析、Horvath 表观遗传时钟、仿生纳米药物药代动力学到 AI 驱动的多组学生物标志物发现等模块，并提供了 CLI、Python API 和 Streamlit 交互界面，旨在作为可复现的科研测试平台。

## 亮点

- **多模块集成**：将多个计算生物学核心方法（随机微分方程、单细胞分析、表观遗传时钟、药代动力学、富集分析）整合在一个统一框架中，便于端到端使用。
- **交互式可视化**：基于 Streamlit 提供 8 个交互模块，包括 3D Waddington 景观、单细胞 UMAP、药代动力学曲线等，降低使用门槛。
- **工程化完善**：提供 CLI（`hsc`）、Python API、Docker 容器化部署、30 个单元测试，并遵循 Black 代码风格，具备良好的可维护性和可复现性。
- **学术导向**：与 Hacettepe 大学干细胞研讨会深度结合，包含真实会议内容、调查数据和 8 张学术海报，具有教育价值。

## 为何对本课题有用

该仓库与「虚拟细胞/虚拟器官 × 单细胞/空间组学 × 生物基座模型、生物大语言模型、Bio Agent」课题高度相关，直接提供了以下可迁移价值：

- **虚拟细胞建模**：Module 1 的 Waddington 景观与 Langevin 动力学为细胞状态转换的随机建模提供了数学框架，可扩展为虚拟细胞动态模拟的基础。
- **单细胞组学分析**：Module 2 的 scRNA-seq 流程（QC、归一化、HVG、PCA、扩散伪时间）可直接用于单细胞数据预处理，为基座模型提供标准化的输入。
- **表观遗传时钟**：Module 3 的 Horvath 时钟可评估细胞年龄，为虚拟器官的衰老模拟提供量化指标。
- **多组学整合**：Module 6 的数字孪生扰动引擎（CRISPR KO、药物抑制）展示了如何将基因调控扰动与表型变化关联，可启发 Bio Agent 的因果推理设计。
- **Bio Agent 交互**：Streamlit 界面和 CLI 可作为 Bio Agent 的交互接口，便于自动化实验流程。

## 怎么用

- **安装**：Python 3.10-3.12，克隆仓库后 `pip install -r requirements.txt` 和 `pip install -e .`。
- **主入口**：CLI 入口为 `src/cli.py`（命令 `hsc`），Web 应用入口为 `app/app.py`（`streamlit run app/app.py`）。
- **依赖**：核心依赖为 numpy、pandas、scipy、scikit-learn、plotly、streamlit、matplotlib、seaborn（见 `requirements.txt` 和 `pyproject.toml`）。
- **输入/输出**：
  - scRNA-seq 模块：输入为基因表达矩阵（如 CSV），输出为 PCA/UMAP 嵌入、伪时间轨迹、标志物表达图。
  - 数字孪生模块：输入为基因名和扰动类型（如 `SETD2`、`CRISPR_KO`），输出为效率倍数和表型转变。
  - 表观遗传时钟：输入为 DNA 甲基化数据，输出为生物年龄和年轻化模拟结果。
- **GPU 需求**：README 未说明，但基于 scikit-learn 和 numpy 的实现，CPU 即可运行，大规模数据可能需要 GPU 加速（需自行评估）。
- **调试**：运行 `pytest -v --cov=src --cov-report=term-missing` 执行 30 个单元测试，可断点调试各模块。

## 核心 idea

核心方法学在于将细胞命运决定建模为随机动力学过程，通过 Waddington 势能景观和 Langevin 方程捕捉细胞状态转换的随机性，并利用 Kramers 逃逸理论量化重编程效率，从而将抽象的发育生物学概念转化为可计算的数学框架。

## 可搬移点

- **Waddington 景观模拟器**（`src/waddington.py`）：包含势能函数和 Langevin 积分器，可解耦后用于自定义的细胞状态转换模拟，License 为 MIT，允许自由使用。
- **scRNA-seq 流程**（`src/scrna_pipeline.py`）：包含 QC、归一化、HVG 选择、PCA 和伪时间推断，可逐步替换为自定义 Pipeline 中的预处理步骤，License 为 MIT。
- **数字孪生扰动引擎**（`src/digital_twin.py`）：提供基因扰动到表型变化的映射逻辑，可移植到 Bio Agent 的推理模块，License 为 MIT。
- **表观遗传时钟**（`src/epigenetic_clock.py`）：Horvath 时钟实现，可独立用于年龄预测，License 为 MIT。
- **CLI 框架**（`src/cli.py`）：可参考其命令注册和参数解析方式，快速构建自定义 CLI 工具，License 为 MIT。

Figure 2: 3D Waddington potential energy surface and stochastic Langevin reprogramming trajectory driven by OSKM induction.

--- ### Module 2: Single-Cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq) & Lineage Trajectory Full end-to-end single-cell quality control, $\log_1(p)$ library-size normalization, highly variable gene (HVG) selection, PCA, and diffusion pseudotime reconstruction.


Figure 3: Single-cell transcriptomic atlas across 7 phenotypic clusters with lineage gradient markers (POU5F1, NANOG, THY1, NPHS1).

--- ### Module 3: In Vivo Rejuvenation & Horvath Epigenetic Clock Calculates biological age based on DNA methylation dynamics. Simulates cyclic pulsatile expression of OSKM factors to reverse epigenetic age without causing somatic dedifferentiation or teratoma formation.


Figure 4: Pulsed OSKM intervention reversing the Horvath epigenetic clock from 75 to 38 biological years.

--- ### Module 4: Paracrine Secretome & Podocyte FSGS Rescue Quantifies the restorative kinetics of MSC secretome (VEGF-A, HGF, IGF-1, IL-10) and extracellular vesicles on damaged renal glomeruli, modeling Nephrin (`NPHS1`) restoration and proteinuria alleviation.


Figure 5: 28-day glomerular filtration barrier recovery curve following MSC exosome administration.

--- ### Module 5: Cancer Stem Cells (CSCs) & Biomimetic Nanomedicine Simulates 2-compartment pharmacokinetics, reticuloendothelial system (RES) immune evasion, and cell membrane-coated PLGA nanoparticles targeting chemoresistant CSC niches.


Figure 6: Correlation between THY1/CD90 and 5-FU chemoresistance, paired with biomimetic nanoparticle tumor penetration.

--- ### Module 6: In Silico Whole-Cell Digital Twin & Perturbation Engine Dynamically simulates the cascading impacts of CRISPR knockouts (`SETD2`, `MEFV`, `THY1`) and small molecule inhibitors (`Niclosamide`, `Temsirolimus`, `Etoposide`, `GYY4137`) across gene regulatory circuits. --- ## 🚀 Quick Start & Installation ### Requirements * Python 3.10, 3.11, or 3.12 * Git ```bash # Clone the repository git clone https://github.com/bahattinyunus/hacettepe-stem-cell.git cd hacettepe-stem-cell # Create and activate virtual environment python -m venv .venv source .venv/bin/activate # Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate # Install dependencies and package in editable mode pip install --upgrade pip pip install -r requirements.txt pip install -e . ``` --- ## ⌨️ Command Line Interface (CLI - `hsc`) The suite provides a high-performance command line tool (`hsc`): ```bash # 1. Simulate Waddington reprogramming hsc simulate-reprogramming --yamanaka 0.90 --steps 200 # 2. Compute mRNAsI stemness index from raw single-cell matrix hsc calc-stemness --counts data/scrna_counts.csv --output stemness_scores.csv # 3. Simulate pulsed Horvath epigenetic clock rejuvenation hsc epigenetic-clock --age 70 --cycles 5 --strength 0.85 # 4. Perform Gene Set Overrepresentation Analysis (ORA) hsc pathway-enrichment --genes POU5F1,SOX2,NANOG,SETD2 # 5. Run In Silico Whole-Cell Digital Twin Perturbation hsc digital-twin --target SETD2 --type CRISPR_KO --intensity 0.95 # 6. Simulate Biomimetic Nanomedicine Pharmacokinetics hsc nanomedicine --membrane STEM_CELL --drug 5-FU # 7. Launch Interactive Web Application hsc launch-app ``` --- ## 🖥️ Interactive Streamlit Web Platform Launch the dashboard locally: ```bash streamlit run app/app.py ``` The application provides **8 interactive modules**: 1. **🏠 Overview & Ecosystem:** Symposium summary, metrics, and multi-omics pipeline. 2. **🏔️ Waddington & Epigenetic Landscape:** 3D interactive surface & Langevin trajectory. 3. **🔬 scRNA-seq & Lineage Dynamics:** PCA/UMAP embeddings, marker violin plots, pseudotime. 4. **🦠 Cancer Stem Cells & THY1/CD90:** Chemoresistance simulator and nanocarrier kinetics. 5. **🧪 Regenerative Microenvironment & MSC Secretome:** Glomerular podocyte FSGS recovery. 6. **📊 Multi-Omics Biomarker Discovery:** Volcano plots, Benjamini-Hochberg FDR, Random Forest. 7. **🎓 Interactive Knowledge Quiz & Flashcards:** Self-assessment on workshop concepts. 8. **🏛️ Symposium Panel, AI Survey & Posters:** Interactive survey charts, career metrics, and digital twin simulator. --- ## 🐍 Python API Examples ```python import numpy as np from src.digital_twin import WholeCellDigitalTwin from src.epigenetic_clock import HorvathEpigeneticClock from src.waddington import simulate_reprogramming # 1. In Silico Whole-Cell Perturbation (SETD2 Epigenetic Barrier Knockout) twin = WholeCellDigitalTwin() result = twin.simulate_perturbation("SETD2", perturbation_type="CRISPR_KO", intensity=0.95) print(f"Reprogramming Efficiency Multiplier: {result.reprogramming_efficiency_multiplier}x") print(f"Phenotypic Shift: {result.phenotypic_transition}") # 2. Horvath Epigenetic Clock Rejuvenation clock = HorvathEpigeneticClock() rejuv = clock.simulate_pulsed_rejuvenation(chronological_age=65.0, cycles=5) print(f"Years Rejuvenated: {rejuv['years_rejuvenated']} years ({rejuv['safety_status']})") # 3. Langevin Stochastic Reprogramming traj = simulate_reprogramming(yamanaka_strength=0.88, steps=100) print(f"Final State: {traj['final_state']}, Pluripotency Achieved: {traj['success']}") ``` --- ## 🐳 Docker & Containerization Run the full platform instantly with zero configuration via Docker: ```bash # Using Docker Compose docker compose up -d # Or build and run directly docker build -t hacettepe-stem-cell . docker run -p 8501:8501 hacettepe-stem-cell ``` Open `http://localhost:8501` in your browser. --- ## 🧪 Unit Tests & Verification (30 Tests) The entire codebase is verified by 30 automated unit tests: ```bash pytest -v --cov=src --cov-report=term-missing ``` --- ## 📖 Academic References & Citation If you use this computational platform, datasets, or algorithms, please cite: ```bibtex @article{cetin2026hacettepe, author = {Çetin, Bahattin Yunus}, title = {An In Silico Whole-Cell Framework for Epigenetic Reprogramming, Stemness Dynamics, and Biomimetic Nanomedicine: Insights from the Hacettepe Stem Cell Technologies Symposium}, journal = {Computational and Structural Biotechnology Journal}, year = {2026}, doi = {10.5281/zenodo.10000000}, url = {https://github.com/bahattinyunus/hacettepe-stem-cell} } ``` --- ## 📜 License This project is licensed under the [MIT License](LICENSE).

## 是什么
SAFFRON 是一个用于评估空间转录组基础模型（SFM）嵌入是否捕捉已知空间变异来源的机制可解释性框架。它通过训练一个 Matryoshka 稀疏自编码器（SAE）将嵌入分解为稀疏、人类可解释的特征，并评估这些特征与已知空间变异度量（如 1D 空间轴、疾病特征评分）的相关性。

## 亮点
- **机制可解释性**：通过稀疏自编码器将高维嵌入分解为稀疏特征，便于人类理解模型捕捉的生物学信号。
- **灵活评估**：支持任意 SFM、单细胞 FM 或基因表达嵌入，可针对多种空间变异度量（全局梯度、局部微环境）进行评估。
- **高效稀疏性**：采用 Matryoshka SAE 和 BatchTopK 稀疏性，默认 M=4·D，K≈6% 的 M，平衡表示容量与稀疏性。
- **基准测试集成**：提供 8 个基准任务（6 个全局空间梯度、2 个阿尔茨海默病斑块微环境），并支持 Hugging Face 数据集加载，便于新模型评估。
- **易用 API**：简洁的 `SAFFRON` 类，`fit` 和 `evaluate` 分离，支持 OMP 特征选择。

## 为何对本课题有用
SAFFRON 直接针对虚拟细胞/虚拟器官 × 单细胞/空间组学 × 生物基座模型方向，提供了一种评估基础模型嵌入质量的方法。它帮助研究者验证 SFM 是否真正学习到空间变异信号，这对于构建可靠的虚拟细胞模型至关重要。其可解释性特征分解可迁移到生物大语言模型的可解释性分析，而基准测试框架可标准化模型评估。此外，其稀疏编码思想可借鉴用于压缩高维组学数据，提升计算效率。

## 怎么用
- **主入口**：`saffron/__init__.py` 导出 `SAFFRON` 类，核心逻辑在 `saffron/saffron.py`。
- **安装**：`git clone https://github.com/chitra-lab/SAFFRON && cd SAFFRON && pip install -e .`（依赖见 `pyproject.toml`，包括 numpy、scipy、scikit-learn、torch、anndata 等）。
- **输入/输出**：输入为 AnnData 对象，包含嵌入矩阵 `adata.obsm["X_embedding"]`（N×D）和空间变异向量 `adata.obs["isodepth"]`（N,）。输出为 `SAFFRON` 结果对象，包含特征相关性、最佳特征索引和 OMP 选择结果。
- **GPU 需求**：依赖 torch，但未明确要求 GPU；小规模数据 CPU 可运行，大规模建议 GPU。
- **调试示例**：`notebooks/global_spatial_variation_tutorial.ipynb` 和 `notebooks/local_spatial_variation_tutorial.ipynb` 提供完整分析流程，可断点调试。

## 核心 idea
核心方法学洞察：通过 Matryoshka 稀疏自编码器将嵌入分解为稀疏特征，并利用特征与空间变异的统计相关性（如 Spearman 相关）来评估模型是否捕捉到已知生物学信号，从而实现机制可解释性。其创新在于将可解释性分析从模型内部转向嵌入空间，提供了一种通用的评估框架。

## 可搬移点
- **稀疏自编码器模块**（`saffron/sae.py`）：可解耦并移植到自定义 Pipeline，用于任何嵌入的稀疏分解，需确认 License（README 未明确，需确认）。
- **相关性评估逻辑**（`saffron/correlate.py`）：可独立使用，用于计算特征与目标变量的相关性，适合快速评估。
- **OMP 特征选择**（`saffron/omp.py`）：可移植用于最小特征集重建，适用于特征选择任务。
- **基准测试框架**（`saffron/benchmark.py`）：可扩展用于新数据集和模型评估，需确认 License。
- **整体设计**：`SAFFRON` 类的 `fit`/`evaluate` 分离模式可借鉴，便于模块化替换。

# SAFFRON SAFFRON is a mechanistic interpretability framework for evaluating whether spatial transcriptomics foundation model (SFM) embeddings capture known sources of spatial variation in gene expression, using a Matryoshka sparse autoencoder (SAE) to decompose embeddings into sparse, human-interpretable features. Given: 1. a set of embeddings `Z` (from an SFM, a single-cell FM, or even gene expression), and 2. a known measure of spatial variation `τ` for the same cells (e.g. a 1-D spatial axis, a disease-signature score, distance to a pathological feature), SAFFRON trains a sparse autoencoder on `Z` and evaluates which of its learned features track `τ`. 📄 **Paper:** [Evaluating the ability of spatial transcriptomics foundation models to learn multi-scale spatial variation](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.08.01.742217) (*bioRxiv* preprint, 2026)

## 🚀 Quick Start ```bash git clone https://github.com/chitra-lab/SAFFRON && cd SAFFRON pip install -e . ``` ## ▶️ Running SAFFRON ```python import anndata as ad from saffron import SAFFRON adata = ad.read_h5ad("my_data.h5ad") Z = adata.obsm["X_embedding"] # (N, D) embeddings from an SFM, a single-cell FM, or gene expression tau = adata.obs["isodepth"].values # (N,) known spatial variation, e.g. a 1-D spatial axis model = SAFFRON() # Matryoshka SAE with BatchTopK sparsity (M = 4·D, K ≈ 6% of M by default) model.fit(Z) # train the SAE once ... result = model.evaluate(tau) # ... then evaluate its features against any spatial measure print(result.correlation.best_feature, result.correlation.best_rho) # SAE feature most correlated with tau if result.omp_selection is not None: # OMP runs when |rho| >= 0.3 print(result.omp_selection.selected_features, result.omp_selection.r2) # minimal reconstructing feature set ``` The tutorials below show the full analyses from the paper. ## Getting started Check out our [readthedocs](https://saffron-sae.readthedocs.io/en/latest/index.html), which includes tutorials for two analyses: - `notebooks/global_spatial_variation_tutorial.ipynb` — **Spatial gradients in the colorectal tumor-stroma boundary.** Novae embeddings on 10x Visium data, evaluated against a **global** 1-D tumor-to-stroma gradient, including a check of the SAE features against raw gene expression. - `notebooks/local_spatial_variation_tutorial.ipynb` — **Local microenvironment variation around Aβ plaques (MERFISH).** Compares a gene-expression SAE against a SFM's SAE on **local** microenvironment measures in an Alzheimer's disease brain dataset. ## 📊 Benchmark The paper's 8 benchmark tasks (6 global spatial gradients, 2 Alzheimer's disease plaque microenvironments), with their spatial measures `τ` and the baselines (PCA and an SAE on gene expression directly), are on Hugging Face at [ChitraLab/saffron-benchmark](https://huggingface.co/datasets/ChitraLab/saffron-benchmark). To evaluate a new model: ```python from saffron import SAFFRON, benchmark adata = benchmark.load("colorectal") # one of benchmark.TASKS Z = my_model.embed(adata) # your model's (cells x D) embeddings H = SAFFRON().fit(Z).sae_result_.Z # SAFFRON SAE features benchmark.score(adata, H) # same metric as the paper benchmark.score(adata, adata.obsm["X_pca"]) # PCA baseline (also obsm["gene_sae_features"]) ``` ## 📦 Dependencies `pip install -e .` installs everything needed for the core SAFFRON pipeline and both notebooks (numpy, scipy, scikit-learn, torch, anndata, matplotlib, jupyter, ipykernel).

## 是什么

这是一个精选的**生物基础模型（bio foundation models）**资源列表仓库，收集了针对生物数据（DNA、RNA、蛋白质、单细胞、病理图像、生物医学文本等）的大规模预训练模型，并附有简要说明和链接。它本身不是模型或框架，而是一个**知识索引和导航工具**，帮助研究者快速定位和了解当前生物基础模型领域的代表性工作。

## 亮点

- **覆盖面广**：按数据类型（DNA/基因组、调控基因组、单细胞转录组、单细胞表观/染色质、RNA、蛋白质、病理图像、生物医学文本）和用途（基准测试、框架/模型中心、综述）系统分类，便于按需检索。
- **持续维护**：包含自动化脚本（`scripts/check_list.py`、`scripts/publish-pr.sh`、`scripts/review-pr.sh`）和贡献指南（`automation/add-entries.md`、`automation/review-entries.md`），支持社区协作更新，保证列表的时效性。
- **链接丰富**：每个条目均提供官方仓库或模型页面链接，便于直接获取模型权重、代码和文档。

## 为何对本课题有用

本仓库直接服务于**虚拟细胞/虚拟器官 × 单细胞/空间组学 × 生物基座模型、生物大语言模型、Bio Agent** 课题，因为它集中收录了该方向的核心模型资源：

- **单细胞转录组模型**（如 Geneformer、scGPT、scFoundation、scPRINT、Nicheformer、CellPLM、GeneCompass 等）是构建虚拟细胞的基础组件，可用于细胞状态表示、细胞类型注释、基因调控推断等。
- **空间组学相关模型**（如 Nicheformer、sCellTransformer）支持将空间信息整合进细胞模型，对虚拟器官的空间结构建模至关重要。
- **DNA/基因组语言模型**（如 Evo、Evo 2、Nucleotide Transformer、DNABERT-2）提供基因组尺度的序列理解能力，可用于解析基因调控和变异效应。
- **蛋白质语言模型**（如 ESM、ESM3、ProGen）和**结构预测模型**（如 AlphaFold、RoseTTAFold）为虚拟细胞中的分子层面建模提供支持。
- **病理图像模型**（如 UNI、Prov-GigaPath）和**生物医学文本模型**（如 BioGPT、PubMedBERT）可整合多模态信息，助力构建多模态生物基座模型。
- **基准测试**（如 BEND、scEval、ProteinGym）和**框架**（如 helical、scvi-tools）为模型评估和集成提供基础设施。

因此，本仓库可作为课题选型、模型对比和快速上手的**导航地图**。

## 怎么用

- **主入口**：直接浏览 `README.md`，按分类查找感兴趣的模型，点击链接跳转到对应仓库或模型页面。
- **安装与依赖**：本仓库本身无代码依赖，仅需 Git 和 Markdown 阅读器。若需运行自动化脚本，需 Python 环境（`scripts/check_list.py` 用于检查列表格式）。
- **输入/输出数据格式**：不适用，因为本仓库不处理数据。
- **GPU 算力**：不适用，本仓库不涉及计算。
- **调试/示例**：无 Demo 或单元测试，但可通过 `automation/` 下的贡献指南了解如何添加新条目。

## 核心 idea

核心方法学 Insight：**通过社区驱动的分类索引，将分散的生物基础模型资源系统化，降低研究者检索和比较的成本，从而加速模型选型和集成**。其价值在于“导航”而非“实现”，为课题提供了快速定位和横向对比的入口。

## 可搬移点

- **分类体系**：可借鉴其按数据类型和任务分类的方式，构建自己的模型资源清单或知识库。
- **自动化检查脚本**：`scripts/check_list.py` 可被解耦，用于维护自定义的模型列表，确保格式规范。
- **贡献流程**：`automation/` 下的 PR 流程可参考，用于团队协作维护资源。
- **License**：README 未明确说明仓库本身的 License，需确认。但各条目对应的模型仓库各有其 License，使用时需分别查看。
