# Awesome bio foundation models

A collection of large-scale pretrained models built specifically for biological data.

## DNA and genome language models

- [AgroNT](https://huggingface.co/InstaDeepAI/agro-nucleotide-transformer-1b): nucleotide transformer trained on edible plant genomes
- [Caduceus](https://github.com/kuleshov-group/caduceus): bi-directional, reverse-complement-equivariant long-range DNA model
- [Carbon](https://github.com/huggingface/carbon): causal genomic language models trained on DNA and RNA sequences for sequence generation, zero-shot variant effect prediction, and fine-tuning
- [DNABERT](https://github.com/jerryji1993/DNABERT): first BERT-style pretrained model of the human genome
- [DNABERT-2](https://github.com/MAGICS-LAB/DNABERT_2): efficient multi-species genome model with byte-pair tokenization
- [DNABERT-S](https://github.com/MAGICS-LAB/DNABERT_S): species-aware embeddings for genome discrimination
- [Evo](https://github.com/evo-design/evo): genome-scale generative model spanning molecular to genome scale
- [Evo 2](https://github.com/ArcInstitute/evo2): genome modeling and design across all domains of life
- [GENA-LM](https://github.com/AIRI-Institute/GENA_LM): open-source foundation models trained on human genome sequences using byte-pair encoding
- [GENERator](https://github.com/GenerTeam/GENERator): long-context generative genomic foundation model trained on RefSeq DNA sequences for sequence generation and understanding
- [GenSLMs](https://github.com/ramanathanlab/genslm): genome-scale language models trained on microbial genomes
- [gLM2](https://github.com/TattaBio/gLM2): mixed-modality genomic language model over the OMG corpus
- [GPN](https://github.com/songlab-cal/gpn): genomic pretrained network, including the multiple-alignment GPN-MSA variant
- [GROVER](https://huggingface.co/PoetschLab/GROVER): DNA language model learning sequence context in the human genome
- [HyenaDNA](https://github.com/HazyResearch/hyena-dna): long-range genomic sequence modeling at single-nucleotide resolution
- [JEPA-DNA](https://github.com/NVIDIA-BioNeMo/JEPA-DNA): continual pretraining that adds a joint-embedding predictive objective to genomic language models (DNABERT-2, NTv3, HyenaDNA), with released checkpoints
- [megaDNA](https://github.com/lingxusb/megaDNA): long-context generative model of bacteriophage genomes
- [Nucleotide Transformer](https://github.com/instadeepai/nucleotide-transformer): multi-species foundation models for genomics

## Regulatory genome models

- [AlphaGenome](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphagenome): multi-modal regulatory prediction across megabase contexts
- [Borzoi](https://github.com/calico/borzoi): RNA-seq coverage prediction from sequence
- [Enformer](https://github.com/google-deepmind/deepmind-research/tree/master/enformer): long-range transformer for gene expression prediction
- [Sei](https://github.com/FunctionLab/sei-framework): genome-wide model of regulatory sequence activity classes

## Single-cell transcriptome models

- [BMFM-RNA](https://github.com/BiomedSciAI/biomed-multi-omic): IBM single-cell transcriptomic foundation models pretrained with whole-cell expression decoding, with an open training framework
- [Cell2Sentence](https://github.com/vandijklab/cell2sentence): converts single-cell transcriptomes into ranked gene-name sentences for analysis with large language models
- [CellPLM](https://github.com/OmicsML/CellPLM): pretrained cell language model that treats cells as tokens
- [GeneCompass](https://github.com/xCompass-AI/GeneCompass): knowledge-informed cross-species foundation model pretrained on over 100 million single-cell transcriptomes
- [Geneformer](https://huggingface.co/ctheodoris/Geneformer): transfer-learning model pretrained on ~30 million single-cell transcriptomes
- [Nicheformer](https://github.com/theislab/nicheformer): foundation model spanning dissociated and spatial single-cell data
- [scBERT](https://github.com/TencentAILabHealthcare/scBERT): pretrained model for cell type annotation
- [sCellTransformer](https://huggingface.co/InstaDeepAI/sCellTransformer): long-range model for zero-shot gene expression and cell type prediction in single-cell and spatial transcriptomics
- [scFoundation](https://github.com/biomap-research/scFoundation): large-scale model over the full transcriptome
- [scGPT](https://github.com/bowang-lab/scGPT): generative pretrained model for single-cell multi-omics
- [SCimilarity](https://github.com/Genentech/scimilarity): single-cell foundation model for cell annotation and similarity search
- [scLong](https://github.com/BaiDing1234/scLong): billion-parameter model pretrained on 48 million cells with self-attention across all ~28,000 human genes
- [scMulan](https://github.com/SuperBianC/scMulan): multitask generative model of cell language
- [scPRINT](https://github.com/cantinilab/scPRINT): pretrained model for gene network inference and denoising
- [Stack](https://github.com/ArcInstitute/stack): single-cell foundation model enabling in-context learning over cell-by-gene matrix chunks
- [STATE](https://github.com/ArcInstitute/state): model of cellular perturbation response
- [Tahoe-x1](https://github.com/tahoebio/tahoe-x1): single-cell foundation model up to 3B parameters pretrained on 266 million transcriptomes for perturbation prediction and cellular representation
- [UCE](https://github.com/snap-stanford/UCE): universal cell embeddings across species without cell-type labels

## Single-cell epigenome and chromatin models

- [Atacformer](https://doi.org/10.1101/2025.11.03.685753): transformer foundation model pretrained on 1.2 million scATAC-seq cells using genomic interval tokens
- [ChromFound](https://github.com/SAIS-LifeScience/ChromFound): genome-wide foundation model for single-cell chromatin accessibility
- [EpiAgent](https://github.com/xy-chen16/EpiAgent): foundation model for single-cell epigenomics
- [EpiFoundation](https://github.com/UCSC-VLAA/EpiFoundation): foundation model for single-cell ATAC-seq
- [geniml](https://github.com/databio/geniml): machine learning toolkit for genomic intervals, including region embeddings and tokenizers
- [HiCFoundation](https://github.com/Noble-Lab/HiCFoundation): foundation model pretrained on 118 million Hi-C contact submatrices for 3D chromatin architecture and single-cell analysis
- [scBasset](https://github.com/calico/scBasset): sequence-based model of single-cell accessibility

## RNA models

- [Orthrus](https://github.com/bowang-lab/Orthrus): contrastive mature RNA model for functional property prediction
- [RhoFold](https://github.com/ml4bio/RhoFold): language-model-based RNA 3D structure prediction
- [RiNALMo](https://github.com/lbcb-sci/RiNALMo): large RNA language model generalizing across structural tasks
- [RNAErnie](https://github.com/CatIIIIIIII/RNAErnie): motif-aware multi-purpose RNA language model
- [RNA-FM](https://github.com/ml4bio/RNA-FM): foundation model trained on non-coding RNA sequences
- [SpliceBERT](https://github.com/chenkenbio/SpliceBERT): language model pretrained on vertebrate primary RNA sequences for RNA splicing analysis
- [UTR-LM](https://github.com/a96123155/UTR-LM): language model of 5' UTRs for translation prediction

## Protein language models

- [AbLang](https://github.com/oxpig/AbLang): antibody language model pretrained on antibody sequences for sequence restoration and representation learning
- [AMPLIFY](https://github.com/chandar-lab/AMPLIFY): protein language models pretrained on diverse protein sequence databases for representation learning and property prediction
- [Ankh](https://github.com/agemagician/Ankh): optimized general-purpose protein language model
- [DPLM](https://github.com/bytedance/dplm): family of diffusion protein language models (DPLM, DPLM-2) for protein sequence and structure generation and representation learning
- [ESM](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm): ESM-1b, ESM-2, and ESMFold protein language models
- [ESM3 / ESM C](https://github.com/evolutionaryscale/esm): multimodal generative protein models over sequence, structure, and function
- [IgLM](https://github.com/Graylab/IgLM): generative language model pretrained on antibody sequences for conditionally generating and infilling antibody sequence libraries
- [ProGen](https://github.com/salesforce/progen): generative protein language models for controllable design
- [ProstT5](https://github.com/mheinzinger/ProstT5): bilingual language model translating between protein sequence and structure
- [ProtGPT2](https://huggingface.co/nferruz/ProtGPT2): autoregressive model generating de novo protein sequences
- [ProTrek](https://github.com/westlake-repl/ProTrek): tri-modal protein language model aligning protein sequence, structure, and text representations
- [ProtTrans](https://github.com/agemagician/ProtTrans): transformer models trained on large protein corpora
- [RITA](https://github.com/lightonai/RITA): family of autoregressive protein language models pretrained on UniRef100 for protein sequence generation and representation learning
- [SaProt](https://github.com/westlake-repl/SaProt): structure-aware protein language model
- [Tranception](https://github.com/OATML-Markslab/Tranception): autoregressive protein language model with inference-time retrieval for protein fitness prediction
- [xTrimoPGLM](https://github.com/biomap-research/xTrimoPGLM): unified 100B-scale protein language model family for protein understanding and design

## Protein structure and design models

- [AlphaFold](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold): highly accurate protein structure prediction
- [AlphaFold 3](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3): joint structure prediction for proteins, nucleic acids, and ligands
- [BioEmu](https://github.com/microsoft/bioemu): generative model that samples protein equilibrium structure ensembles from sequence
- [Boltz](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz): open biomolecular structure prediction model
- [Chai-1](https://github.com/chaidiscovery/chai-lab): multimodal model for molecular structure prediction
- [EvoDiff](https://github.com/microsoft/evodiff): generative protein diffusion model for sequence generation and design
- [OpenFold](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold): trainable open-source reimplementation of AlphaFold 2
- [ProteinMPNN](https://github.com/dauparas/ProteinMPNN): deep learning based protein sequence design
- [RFdiffusion](https://github.com/RosettaCommons/RFdiffusion): diffusion model for de novo protein design
- [RoseTTAFold All-Atom](https://github.com/baker-laboratory/RoseTTAFold-All-Atom): all-atom structure prediction for biomolecular assemblies

## Pathology and imaging models

- [BioCLIP](https://github.com/Imageomics/bioclip): vision-language foundation model for organismal biology pretrained on TreeOfLife-10M for fine-grained taxonomic classification
- [BiomedCLIP](https://huggingface.co/microsoft/BiomedCLIP-PubMedBERT_256-vit_base_patch16_224): vision-language foundation model pretrained on 15 million biomedical figure-caption pairs for cross-modal retrieval and classification
- [BiomedParse](https://github.com/microsoft/BiomedParse): biomedical foundation model for joint segmentation, detection, and recognition across nine imaging modalities
- [CHIEF](https://github.com/hms-dbmi/CHIEF): clinical histopathology foundation model for cancer evaluation and prognosis
- [CONCH](https://github.com/mahmoodlab/CONCH): vision-language foundation model for computational pathology
- [H-optimus-0](https://huggingface.co/bioptimus/H-optimus-0): open foundation model for pathology image representation
- [Hibou](https://github.com/histai/hibou): vision transformer foundation models pretrained on over 1 million histology whole-slide images for computational pathology
- [OpenPhenom](https://huggingface.co/recursionpharma/OpenPhenom): channel-agnostic masked autoencoder (ViT-S/16) that embeds multi-channel Cell Painting microscopy images
- [Phikon](https://huggingface.co/owkin/phikon): open foundation model for histology representation based on ViT-B/16 pretrained on 40 million human histopathology tiles
- [Phikon-v2](https://huggingface.co/owkin/phikon-v2): vision transformer foundation model pretrained on 450M pan-cancer histology images for biomarker prediction and computational pathology
- [PLIP](https://github.com/PathologyFoundation/plip): vision-language foundation model pretrained on pathology image-text pairs for zero-shot classification and image-text retrieval
- [Prov-GigaPath](https://github.com/prov-gigapath/prov-gigapath): whole-slide foundation model for digital pathology
- [TITAN](https://github.com/mahmoodlab/TITAN): multimodal whole-slide foundation model for pathology
- [UNI](https://github.com/mahmoodlab/UNI): general-purpose pathology image encoder
- [Virchow](https://huggingface.co/paige-ai/Virchow): large pathology foundation model

## Biomedical text and knowledge models

- [BioBERT](https://github.com/dmis-lab/biobert): domain-specific language model pretrained on PubMed biomedical literature
- [BioGPT](https://github.com/microsoft/BioGPT): generative pretrained transformer for biomedical text
- [BioLinkBERT](https://github.com/michiyasunaga/LinkBERT): biomedical language model pretrained on PubMed abstracts and their citation links for text mining and question answering
- [BioMedLM](https://huggingface.co/stanford-crfm/BioMedLM): 2.7B parameter GPT-style model pretrained on PubMed abstracts and full-text papers
- [PubMedBERT](https://huggingface.co/microsoft/BiomedNLP-PubMedBERT-base-uncased-abstract-fulltext): domain-specific language model pretrained from scratch on PubMed abstracts and full-text articles
- [TxGNN](https://github.com/mims-harvard/TxGNN): zero-shot drug repurposing over a medical knowledge graph

## Benchmarks and evaluation

- [BEND](https://github.com/frederikkemarin/BEND): benchmark of DNA language models on realistic genomic tasks
- [DART-Eval](https://github.com/kundajelab/DART-Eval): benchmark of DNA models on regulatory sequence tasks
- [Genomic Benchmarks](https://github.com/ML-Bioinfo-CEITEC/genomic_benchmarks): datasets and baselines for genomic sequence classification
- [Open Problems](https://github.com/openproblems-bio/openproblems): living benchmarks for single-cell analysis tasks
- [ProteinGym](https://github.com/OATML-Markslab/ProteinGym): large-scale benchmark of protein fitness prediction and design
- [scEval](https://github.com/HelloWorldLTY/scEval): evaluation framework for single-cell foundation models

## Frameworks and model hubs

- [AIDO](https://github.com/genbio-ai/AIDO): modular system of foundation models across biological modalities
- [gReLU](https://github.com/Genentech/gReLU): framework for training, interpreting, and designing with sequence models
- [helical](https://github.com/helicalAI/helical): unified API for running bio foundation models
- [Kipoi](https://github.com/kipoi/kipoi): model zoo and standardized API for genomics models
- [scvi-tools](https://github.com/scverse/scvi-tools): probabilistic models and infrastructure for single-cell omics

## Reviews

- [Foundation models in bioinformatics](https://doi.org/10.1093/nsr/nwaf028)
- [Progress and opportunities of foundation models in bioinformatics](https://doi.org/10.1093/bib/bbae548)
- [Genomic language models: opportunities and challenges](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tig.2024.11.013)
- [A comprehensive survey of genome language models in bioinformatics](https://doi.org/10.1093/bib/bbaf724)
- [The DNA dialect: a comprehensive guide to pretrained genomic language models](https://doi.org/10.1038/s44320-025-00184-4)
- [Benchmarking DNA foundation models for genomic and genetic tasks](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-65823-8)
- [Single-cell foundation models: bringing artificial intelligence into cell biology](https://doi.org/10.1038/s12276-025-01547-5)
- [A survey on foundation language models for single-cell biology](https://doi.org/10.18653/v1/2025.acl-long.26)

## 是什么

这是一个**单细胞转录组学基础模型的研究型代码仓库**，其核心定位并非提供一个全新的 Transformer 架构，而是构建一个**模块化、可扩展且“难以被愚弄”的评估与训练框架**。它基于 Stem–Backbone–Head 架构，专门用于构建和**诚实评估**单细胞 RNA-seq 数据的表示模型。该仓库强调，当前限制单细胞基础模型发展的瓶颈并非模型架构，而是**混杂因素、数据泄漏和评估方法**，因此它将评估层作为一等公民模块，并内置了强制基线、防泄漏分割和审计机制。

## 亮点

- **强制基线对比**：PCA、缩放 PCA、原始 HVG 和随机投影基线在每次评估中都会运行，且配置无法禁用，确保模型性能对比的公平性。
- **防泄漏的默认分割**：默认采用供体留出（Donor-held-out）分割，并在训练前运行泄漏审计，若发现供体重叠会直接**报错**。
- **训练集拟合强制**：HVG、基因词汇表、分词器统计和标签编码器均在分割后、仅基于训练集拟合，且 `RankTokenizer` 拒绝被重新拟合，从机制上杜绝了数据泄漏。
- **双指标族强制报告**：同时报告生物保守性（如 ARI, NMI）和批次校正（如 iLISI, PCR）指标，防止模型在单一指标上“刷分”。
- **明确的结论判定**：报告会以通俗语言说明模型是否击败了最佳基线，且当置信区间重叠时不会宣称胜利。
- **合成数据品牌化**：合成数据结果带有不可抑制的横幅，防止被误认为真实生物学结果。
- **高度模块化与可扩展性**：通过 Registry 和 Hydra 配置，可以轻松注册新组件（如新的 Backbone）并通过 YAML 文件引用，无需修改训练循环。

## 为何对本课题有用

该仓库直接服务于**生物基座模型**（特别是单细胞转录组学）的**评估与构建**，与课题方向高度对齐。

- **解决“评估危机”**：课题中构建虚拟细胞模型时，常面临“模型是否真的优于简单基线”的质疑。此仓库提供了一个**严谨、防泄漏的评估框架**，可作为我们模型评估的标准流程，确保科学结论的可靠性。
- **提供可复用的数据分割与预处理逻辑**：其供体留出分割、泄漏审计、训练集拟合等逻辑，可直接迁移到我们的 Pipeline 中，用于处理单细胞或空间组学数据，避免因数据划分不当导致的性能虚高。
- **提供模块化架构参考**：其 Stem–Backbone–Head 架构和 Registry 机制，为构建可扩展的**生物大语言模型**或**Bio Agent** 的底层数据表示模块提供了清晰的工程范式。
- **合成数据模拟器**：其可独立开关效应的合成数据生成器，可用于在开发阶段测试我们的模型和评估指标，尤其是在真实数据获取受限时。

## 怎么用

**安装与依赖**：
- 环境要求：Python ≥ 3.10。
- 安装命令：`python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate && pip install -r requirements.txt`。
- 依赖文件：`requirements.txt`（核心依赖）和 `pyproject.toml`（可选依赖，如 `cellxgene-census`）。

**主入口与运行**：
- 主入口文件为 `run.py`，使用 Hydra 进行配置管理。
- 快速端到端测试：`python run.py +experiment=smoke_test`（约 10 秒，CPU 即可）。
- 列出所有注册组件：`python run.py --list`。
- 运行单元测试：`pytest tests/ -q`（共 96 个测试）。

**关键实验命令**：
- 参考合成数据运行：`python run.py +experiment=pretrain_synthetic`。
- 泄漏消融实验：`python run.py +experiment=leakage_ablation`。
- 架构对照（无注意力）：`python run.py +experiment=pretrain_synthetic model=mlp_control`。
- 真实数据（需安装 `cellxgene-census` 并联网）：`python run.py +experiment=pretrain_census`。

**输入/输出数据格式**：
- 输入：支持 CELLxGENE Census（推荐）、本地 `.h5ad` 文件、10x 矩阵目录。
- 输出：训练日志、评估指标表（包含模型与基线对比）、包含明确结论的文本报告。

**调试与探索**：
- 提供 4 个 Jupyter Notebook（`Notebooks/`），可交互式探索数据预处理、分词、分割和泄漏审计的细节。
- 每个 Notebook 顶部有 `DATA_PATH` 开关，可切换使用合成数据或真实 `.h5ad` 数据。

## 核心 idea

**核心方法学 Insight**：该仓库的“新”不在于模型架构，而在于**将“评估的诚实性”作为系统设计的第一性原理**。它通过强制基线、防泄漏分割、训练集拟合和双指标族报告等机制，构建了一个**难以产生“虚假成功”的评估环境**，从而确保任何模型性能的提升都真实可信。这种“反脆弱”的评估设计，是其在基础模型研究中值得借鉴的核心方法学。

## 可搬移点

- **评估与报告模块**（`src/eval/`）：`metrics.py`、`probes.py`、`report.py` 和 `baselines.py` 构成了一个完整的评估框架。**可直接解耦**并集成到我们自己的模型训练 Pipeline 中，用于对虚拟细胞模型进行标准化评估。
- **数据分割与泄漏审计逻辑**（`src/data/splits.py`）：供体留出分割器和泄漏审计逻辑是防止数据泄漏的关键。**可复制**其实现，确保我们处理单细胞/空间组学数据时分割的严谨性。
- **合成数据生成器**（`src/data/synthetic/`）：可独立开关效应的模拟器，**可迁移**用于测试我们自己的模型和评估指标，尤其是在开发初期。
- **模块化注册机制**（`src/core/`）：Registry 模式允许我们**逐步替换**或**新增**自定义的 Backbone、Head 或 Tokenizer，而无需修改核心训练循环，这符合 REA 理念。
- **License**：README 未明确说明 License，需确认。

**注意**：真实数据加载器（`census_source.py` 等）虽已编写并通过单元测试，但未在真实服务上验证，使用时需根据实际数据列名调整 `obs_map`。

# Single-cell transcriptomics foundation model — research repository

A modular repository for building and, more importantly, **honestly
evaluating** representation models for single-cell RNA-seq.

Built on the Stem–Backbone–Head architecture from
`frontier_bio_repo_architecture.md`, specialized to single-cell
transcriptomics.

---

## What makes this different from a training script

The architecture here is conventional on purpose. Transformer design is not
what limits single-cell foundation models. Three independent benchmarks found
that these models often fail to beat PCA, logistic regression or linear
baselines on cell-type annotation, integration and perturbation prediction
(see `docs/BIBLIOGRAPHY.md`). What limits progress is **confounding,
leakage and evaluation**.

So the evaluation layer is a first-class module rather than an afterthought,
and it is built to be hard to fool:

| | |
|---|---|
| **Baselines are mandatory** | PCA, scaled PCA, raw HVG and a random projection run on every evaluation. The config cannot disable them. |
| **Honest splits are the default** | Donor-held-out splitting; a leakage audit runs before training and **raises** on donor overlap. |
| **Random splits are a control, not a result** | `RandomSplitter` warns, and the report labels the split regime so its numbers can't be mistaken for held-out ones. |
| **Fit-on-train is enforced** | HVGs, gene vocabulary, tokenizer statistics and label encoders are all fitted after splitting, on train only. `RankTokenizer` refuses to be re-fitted. |
| **Both metric families, always** | Biological conservation and batch correction are each trivially gameable alone — noise scores ~0.97 on batch mixing. |
| **The report states a verdict** | Plain language on whether the model beat its best control, and it won't call a win a win when the intervals overlap. |
| **Simulated data is branded** | An unsuppressable banner; synthetic numbers can never be quietly presented as biology. |

The rationale for each, with sources, is in **`docs/CONSTRAINTS.md`**.

---

## Install

```bash
python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

Python ≥ 3.10. CPU is fine for the smoke test and ablations.

## Run

```bash
python run.py +experiment=smoke_test        # ~10s, end-to-end
python run.py --list                        # every registered component
pytest tests/ -q                            # 96 tests
```

Then the real experiments:

```bash
# reference synthetic run
python run.py +experiment=pretrain_synthetic

# how much would a random split have inflated the result?
python run.py +experiment=leakage_ablation

# architectural control: no attention
python run.py +experiment=pretrain_synthetic model=mlp_control

# tokenization controls (pair the stem with the tokenizer)
python run.py +experiment=pretrain_synthetic model=continuous data/tokenizer=continuous
python run.py +experiment=pretrain_synthetic model=continuous data/tokenizer=rank

# real data (needs `pip install cellxgene-census` + network)
python run.py +experiment=pretrain_census
```

Any field is overridable from the CLI:

```bash
python run.py +experiment=pretrain_synthetic \
  data/splitter=study_held_out \
  model.d_model=512 \
  model.backbone.n_layers=8 \
  train.epochs=50
```

`model`, `data`, `data/tokenizer`, `data/splitter`, `execution` and `eval`
are Hydra config groups, so they are swapped with `group=name` rather than by
overriding individual keys. Model width is a single `model.d_model` that
propagates to the stem, backbone and every head — repeating it per component
is a reliable way to produce a silent dimension mismatch.

Enabling an off-by-default head:

```bash
python run.py +experiment=pretrain_synthetic model.heads.cell_type.enabled=true
```

## What a run prints

```
model                        probeF1      knnF1        ari        nmi      iLISI    PCRbatch        BIO      BATCH
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
foundation_model               0.474      0.094     -0.003      0.029     0.972*      0.008*      0.165     0.964*
baseline:pca                   0.858*     0.687*      0.214      0.317     0.535       0.243       0.350     0.591
baseline:hvg                   0.768      0.623      0.220*     0.349*     0.661       0.134       0.360*    0.672
baseline:random_projection     0.581      0.420       0.082      0.159     0.714       0.110       0.247     0.717

split regime   : donor_held_out (held-out 'donor_id')
                 *** SYNTHETIC DATA -- these numbers characterize the simulator, not biology ***
cells          : train=1506 test=502 over 2 held-out group(s)
                 WARNING: fewer than 3 held-out groups; the cell-level CIs understate real uncertainty badly.

VERDICT: model does NOT beat baseline:pca on probe_macro_f1: 0.474 vs 0.858 (-0.383).
         This is the common outcome in published benchmarks at this scale.
```

That is a real output from a deliberately under-trained model. A harness that
can only produce good news is not a research instrument — the point is that
this one tells you when you have not beaten PCA.

Note the second row of the model's own result: it wins every *batch* metric
and loses every *biology* metric. That is the noise regime, and it is exactly
why both families are always reported.

---

## Data

**Real data is the default intent**; `configs/data/census.yaml` points at
CELLxGENE Census, which supplies the harmonized `donor_id` / `assay` /
`tissue` / `cell_type` metadata the honest splitters need. Local `.h5ad` and
10x matrix directories are also supported.

```bash
pip install cellxgene-census
python run.py +experiment=pretrain_census
# or a file you downloaded from cellxgene.cziscience.com/datasets:
python run.py +experiment=pretrain_synthetic data=h5ad \
  data.source.path=/path/to/file.h5ad \
  'data.source.obs_map={donor: donor_id, sample: batch_id}'
```

> **The repo was built in a sandbox without access to the data hosts**
> (`cellxgene-census-public-us-west-2.s3...`, `cf.10xgenomics.com`,
> `ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov` were all policy-blocked). The real-data loaders are
> therefore written and unit-tested against their interfaces but have not
> been run against the live services. Expect to adjust `obs_map` for a given
> dataset's column names on first use.

**Synthetic data lives in a separate module** (`src/data/synthetic/`) and
reproduces the statistics that make real data hard, with every effect
individually switchable:

- negative-binomial counts with mean-dependent overdispersion (`phi ≈ a + b/mu`)
- ~90% sparsity and ~10% of genes detected per cell, matching 10x
- log-normal library sizes spanning an order of magnitude
- per-gene batch effects (not removable by a global scale factor)
- donors nested inside batches, so donor-held-out splitting tests something
- batch-dependent cell-type composition
- ambient RNA contamination and doublets
- hierarchical cell types, so metrics can distinguish coarse lineages from close subtypes

Switchability is what makes it useful: generate with `batch_effect=0` and a
batch metric must read ~0, or the metric is measuring something else. The
test suite asserts this.

---

## Layout

```
configs/            Hydra composition: experiment / model / data / execution / eval
src/core/           Registry + the Stem/Backbone/Head contract (CellBatch)
src/data/
  preprocessing.py  normalization, batch-aware HVG, frozen gene vocabulary
  splits.py         donor/study/tissue held-out splitters + leakage audit
  tokenizers/       rank (Geneformer-style) | binned (scGPT-style) | continuous (control)
  sources/          census | h5ad | 10x mtx | synthetic
  synthetic/        standalone simulator with known ground truth
src/models/
  stems/            expression (gene+bin) | continuous
  backbones/        set_transformer (no positional encoding) | mean_pool_mlp (control)
  heads/            masked_value | cell_type | zinb | batch_adversarial
src/eval/
  baselines.py      the mandatory controls
  metrics.py        ARI, NMI, ASW, iLISI, kBET, graph connectivity, PCR, library-size R²
  probes.py         linear + kNN probes with bootstrap CIs
  report.py         side-by-side comparison and verdict
src/runners/        pretrain | evaluate
docs/
  CONSTRAINTS.md    the ten recurring failure modes and how each is handled
  BIBLIOGRAPHY.md   verified sources for every idea implemented
tests/              96 tests
```

## Exploring the data methods

`Notebooks/` holds four executed notebooks that call the repo's own curation
and tokenization code and chart what each step does to the data:

| notebook | covers |
|---|---|
| `01_raw_count_characteristics` | depth, mean–variance, zeros vs the negative binomial, confounders, simulator knobs |
| `02_curation_qc_normalization_hvg` | QC thresholds, raw-count guard, CP10K and `log1p`, gene selection flavors, vocabulary alignment |
| `03_splitting_and_leakage` | splitters, leakage audit, what a random split buys, fit-on-train, donor-level uncertainty |
| `04_tokenization` | the three tokenizers, bin occupancy and chance level, truncation, depth robustness, sweeps, masking |

```bash
pip install jupyterlab matplotlib
jupyter lab Notebooks/
```

Each notebook has a `DATA_PATH` switch at the top: `None` uses the simulator,
a path to an `.h5ad` runs the same analysis on real data.

## Extending it

Write a class, decorate it, reference it by name in YAML. No training-loop
edits:

```python
from src.core import BaseBackbone, register_backbone

@register_backbone("mamba")
class MambaBackbone(BaseBackbone):
    def __init__(self, d_model=256, n_layers=8, d_state=16):
        super().__init__(d_model)
        ...
    def forward(self, x, pad_mask=None):
        return ...
```

```yaml
backbone: {name: mamba, d_model: 512, n_layers: 12}
```

`python run.py --list` enumerates everything registered. Unknown names fail
loudly with suggestions; a component registered against the wrong base class
is rejected at import.

## Known gaps

- `configs/execution/fsdp_cluster.yaml` is a placeholder. The training loop
  marks the two call sites a Fabric/FSDP wrapper replaces, but multi-node has
  not been run.
- The real-data sources are unvalidated against live services (see above).
- `graph_connectivity` saturates at 1.0 on small well-separated test sets;
  it discriminates only at realistic scale.
- No trajectory or cell-cycle conservation metrics yet; scIB has both.

## 是什么

CardiLearn 是一个面向心脏转录组学的 Python 研究代码库，用于表示学习和下游预测。它包含一个轻量级原型实现和一个更大规模的转录组级研究架构。该架构旨在从转录组规模的基因输入中学习分子程序，并通过 Transformer 处理这些程序，构建共享和私有的潜在表示，用于分子重建和生物学状态预测。它不是一个已验证的心脏基础模型，而是一个研究目标。

## 亮点

- **模块化架构**：代码库清晰分离了数据加载、特征化、模型、训练、评估和基准测试等模块，便于独立开发和测试。
- **泄漏感知的生物学划分**：实现了基于研究家族、研究、受试者、样本、细胞/核的层级划分，避免数据泄漏，确保评估的生物学有效性。
- **严格的来源审计与原始计数救援**：提供了脚本和流程，用于审计 GEO/SRA 等外部数据源，并支持对不符合严格整数计数契约的数据集进行原始读段重新处理，确保数据质量。
- **可复现的基准测试**：包含基准定义、协议和运行器，支持可配置的评估流程，并强调与简单基线（如 PCA、MLP、自编码器）的比较。
- **可解释性与扰动预测**：包含可解释性模块（如归因、反事实）和扰动预测模块，为生物学假设生成提供支持。
- **多模态支持**：包含多模态融合相关模块（`fusion.py`、`multimodal.py`），为整合不同数据模态（如转录组+空间）提供基础。

## 为何对本课题有用

CardiLearn 直接面向**虚拟心脏**（心脏转录组）的表示学习，与课题方向高度相关。其核心价值在于：

- **为虚拟细胞/器官模型提供可借鉴的架构**：其“基因输入 → 分子程序 → Transformer → 共享/私有表示”的流程，可作为构建单细胞/空间组学基础模型的参考。
- **提供严格的评估框架**：其泄漏感知的划分、跨研究/跨物种验证、与简单基线的比较等思想，对于验证生物基础模型至关重要，可迁移到虚拟细胞模型的评估中。
- **数据获取与处理流程**：其来源审计和原始计数救援脚本，对于构建大规模单细胞/空间组学训练数据集具有直接参考价值，确保数据质量和可追溯性。
- **可解释性与扰动预测**：其可解释性模块和扰动预测模块，为理解模型学到的生物学机制和模拟基因扰动提供了方法，是虚拟细胞模型的重要功能。

## 怎么用

- **安装**：`pip install -e '.[dev,torch]'`（开发+PyTorch 支持），或 `pip install -e '.[bio]'` 以支持 AnnData/Scanpy 数据格式。
- **命令行入口**：`cardilearn` 命令，支持 `models`、`validate`、`train`、`benchmark-info` 等子命令。
- **Python API**：代码库暴露了模型和训练 API，原型模型可用于轻量级测试。
- **示例与测试**：`tests/` 目录包含大量单元测试，可作为调试入口。`notebooks/` 目录提供了 Colab 笔记本，用于真实数据验证和 SRA 重处理。
- **输入输出**：输入为转录组基因/值矩阵、样本元数据、生物学分组标签、任务目标、配置和基准定义；输出为学习到的表示、预测、重建、训练/评估产物、模型检查点和溯源记录。
- **GPU 需求**：训练大型模型需要 GPU，但原型模型可在 CPU 上运行。

## 核心 idea

CardiLearn 的核心方法学在于**将转录组数据抽象为可学习的“分子程序”，并通过 Transformer 处理这些程序，同时强调严格的生物学划分和与简单基线的比较**，以确保模型学到的表示具有真正的生物学泛化能力，而非仅仅拟合训练数据。

## 可搬移点

- **泄漏感知的划分逻辑**（`cardilearn/splitting.py`、`study_families.py`）：可解耦并移植到任何单细胞/空间组学模型训练流程中，确保评估的生物学有效性。
- **来源审计与原始计数救援脚本**（`scripts/source_rescue_audit.py`、`step3_sra_reprocess.py`）：可复用其数据获取、校验和重处理流程，用于构建高质量训练数据集。
- **基准测试框架**（`cardilearn/benchmark*.py`、`configs/benchmark_v1.yaml`）：可借鉴其基准定义和运行方式，用于评估虚拟细胞模型的性能。
- **可解释性模块**（`cardilearn/interpretability/`）：其归因、反事实和富集分析逻辑可迁移到其他生物基础模型中。
- **许可证**：AGPL-3.0-or-later，允许复制和修改，但衍生作品需开源。

# Virelion-CardiLearn

CardiLearn is a Python research codebase for cardiac transcriptomic representation learning and downstream prediction. It contains a prototype implementation and a larger transcriptome-scale research architecture.


<!-- VALIDATION_PRODUCT_STATUS:BEGIN -->
## Validation and product completion status

**Reviewed 2026-10-14; implementation base `1b8ad6e5ca9f`.** **Status: Research architectures and locked metadata infrastructure; empirical staged gates incomplete.** This is an evidence-backed scope assessment, not a percentage-complete estimate or a declaration that the product is finished.

| Area | Current evidence / remaining gate |
|---|---|
| Software / operational checks | Automated test sources and CI definitions are present; this documentation audit does not report a new algorithm/data-validation run. |
| Scientific or domain evidence | The current manifest explicitly locks eligible tracks and exclusions rather than inventing biological IDs. Raw-count rescue and real-data benchmark runners exist; their presence does not establish a trained cross-study or paired-modality result. |
| Remaining for the declared product scope | Materialize/hash strict count sources and finish raw-read rescue for eligible cohorts; execute locked simple baselines before staged encoder evaluation; establish subject/study-family-safe independent results and real paired modalities before fusion; obtain independently labeled task/calibration evidence. Follow the existing AGENTS.md stage gates; this status update does not advance a scientific stage. |

Evidence and limits: [repository report](docs/VALIDATION_READINESS.md). The [organization status index](https://github.com/Virelion-Biotech/Virelion-HeartTwin/blob/main/docs/STACK_VALIDATION_STATUS.md) separates software, numerical, data-readiness and empirical qualification. Code/schema execution or a completed download is not a substitute for endpoint-specific validation.
<!-- VALIDATION_PRODUCT_STATUS:END -->

## What it contains

- Transcriptome-scale gene inputs.
- Learned molecular programs.
- Program-level Transformer processing.
- Shared and private latent representations.
- Molecular reconstruction and biological-state prediction.
- Interpretability and perturbation-prediction modules.
- Leakage-aware biological splitting.
- Benchmark and provenance contracts.

The larger architecture is a research target, not a validated cardiac foundation model.

## Installation

```bash
pip install -e '.[dev,torch]'
```

For development/testing, the command above installs the development and PyTorch extras required by the full test suite. The `torch` extra is optional for workflows that do not import the torch-backed model modules.

## Usage

```bash
cardilearn models --task classification
cardilearn validate --data data.csv --target label
cardilearn train --data data.csv --target label --output runs/example
cardilearn benchmark-info --definition configs/benchmark_v1.yaml
```

For representation-learning evaluation, use `configs/representation_benchmark_v1.yaml`. The research model is evaluated from frozen embeddings rather than by reconstruction loss alone, and repeated cells/nuclei can be aggregated to biological sample before the primary probe.

The repository also exposes Python model/training APIs. The prototype model should be used for lightweight software testing where supported by the training scripts.


### Colab real-data validation

Use the `notebooks/CardiLearn_v0_5_RealData_Validation_Colab.ipynb` notebook for the locked T4 workflow. It covers sparse single-cell/single-nucleus loading, hierarchy-safe study-family splitting, train-only gene selection, CardiLearnResearch training, frozen sample-level embeddings, PCA/autoencoder baselines, bootstrap/permutation statistics, and provenance export.

The notebook requires a user-supplied locked dataset bundle; it does not invent or silently resolve ambiguous biological metadata. Large raw datasets and model checkpoints remain local to the Colab run unless the optional lightweight results push is enabled.

### Source-rescue audit

Before spending cloud compute on SRA reprocessing, run `scripts/source_rescue_audit.py` or `notebooks/Step3_Source_Rescue_Audit_Colab.ipynb`. It checks the locked GSMs against GEO supplementary candidates, NCBI/ENA SRA mappings, EMBL-EBI ArrayExpress/BioStudies and Expression Atlas evidence, optional ARCHS4 H5 sample availability, and recount3 project/run availability. It is fail-closed: ARCHS4 Kallisto-derived rounded values are not treated as strict raw counts, and recount3-derived counts are reported as derived rather than original submitter counts. Candidate sources still require content-scale, exact sample-mapping, provenance, and SHA-256 validation before entering Step 3 external sources.

### SRA raw-count rescue

The four locked cohorts that fail the strict raw integer-count contract are now covered by a reproducible raw-read rescue workflow:

`GSE232259`, `GSE52313`, `GSE186875`, and `GSE308783`.

Run `scripts/step3_sra_reprocess.py` with `--step resolve` to create the exact GEO GSM → SRX → ENA SRR → FASTQ manifest, then `--step all` on a sufficiently provisioned Linux machine or Colab high-RAM runtime. The workflow uses pinned Mus musculus GRCm39 / Ensembl 112, fastp QC with read-preserving defaults, STAR, and featureCounts. It records source checksums, reference fingerprints, per-sample completion markers, and a validated `external_count_sources.json` that the existing Step 3 baseline runner can consume.

See `docs/SRA_REPROCESSING_V1.md`, `configs/sra_reprocessing_v1.json`, `envs/sra_reprocessing_v1.yml`, and `notebooks/Step3_SRA_Reprocess_Colab.ipynb`.

## Inputs and outputs

**Inputs:** transcriptomic gene/value matrices, sample metadata and biological grouping labels, task targets, model/training configuration, and benchmark definitions.

**Outputs:** learned representations, predictions, reconstructions, training/evaluation artifacts, model checkpoints, and provenance/benchmark records.

The intended biological hierarchy is study family → study → subject/donor/animal → sample/library → cell/nucleus. Cells are observations and are not automatically independent biological replicates.

## Validation

Software tests establish implementation behavior, not biological validity. Scientific evaluation requires locked datasets, biologically appropriate held-out splits, baseline comparisons, cross-study or cross-species testing where relevant, and independent biological validation for biological claims.

The proposed comparison includes PCA + linear probe, MLP, autoencoder, and the larger model; the larger model should be retained only if it improves held-out biological generalization.

## Limitations

The large architecture is not a validated cardiac foundation model. Model capacity, parameter count, reconstruction quality, or training loss do not establish biological significance or causal validity. Perturbation predictions are hypotheses until independently tested. Results can be affected by study-family leakage, batch effects, metadata errors, and distribution shift.

## 是什么

AnnoTuneAgent 是一个面向单细胞 RNA-seq 数据的**簇级细胞类型注释**工具，它结合了内置的 marker 基因打分、两个经过微调的语言模型（基于 Qwen3.5-4B 的 LoRA 适配器）以及规则判断，为每个细胞簇生成可审计的细胞类型标签。它旨在解决单细胞数据中细胞类型注释的自动化与可解释性问题。

## 亮点

- **本地推理与隐私保护**：语言模型权重托管在 Hugging Face，但推理完全在本地进行，确保单细胞数据不离开用户机器。
- **双 LoRA 适配器共享基础模型**：两个独立任务（名称选择与 ML 选择）共享同一个 Qwen3.5-4B 基础模型，通过两个 LoRA 适配器实现，无需合并权重，可独立替换，节省显存并提高灵活性。
- **可审计的决策流程**：每个簇的注释结果由 marker 打分、名称模型、ML 模型三部分构成，规则判断综合三者输出标题，并记录每个模型的答案、面板和原因，保证可追溯性。
- **模块化设计**：支持多种可选预处理方法（如 AmbiDose、scVI、SOLO、scFair、Harmony、Scanorama），用户可按需安装，缺失时仅提示而不中断流程。
- **内置 marker 数据库**：提供人类和小鼠的 marker 基因表，包含组织无关的核心和组织特异性页面，支持自定义假设列表。

## 为何对本课题有用

AnnoTuneAgent 直接属于**单细胞组学 × 生物基座模型**交叉方向，其核心价值在于：

- **将 LLM 引入单细胞注释**：展示了如何将通用大语言模型（Qwen3.5-4B）通过 LoRA 微调用于细胞类型命名，为构建**生物大语言模型**在单细胞领域的应用提供了可复用的范式。
- **可解释的 AI 决策**：通过规则判断整合模型输出，避免黑箱，这对于构建**虚拟细胞**模型中的可解释性模块具有借鉴意义。
- **本地化部署**：在生物医学场景中，数据隐私至关重要，其本地推理设计为**Bio Agent** 在敏感数据上的应用提供了参考。
- **模块化可扩展**：其 pipeline 设计（prepare → run → arbitrate）易于拆解，可被整合到更复杂的**虚拟器官**分析流程中，作为细胞类型注释的组件。

## 怎么用

- **安装**：`pip install annotuneagent`，如需本地模型则 `pip install 'annotuneagent[models]'`，可选方法需额外安装（如 `annotuneagent[scvi]`）。
- **主入口**：Python API 或 CLI。
  - Python：`import annotuneagent as ata; adata = ata.read_10x(...); adata = ata.prepare(...); report = ata.run(...)`。
  - CLI：`annotuneagent --input clustered.h5ad --cluster-key leiden --species human --output result.json`。
- **输入/输出**：输入为原始整数计数矩阵（10x 格式或 h5ad），输出为注释报告（JSON）、验证的 marker 面板、点图、注释后的 h5ad 文件。
- **模型加载**：需指定 `--name-adapter`、`--ml-adapter` 和 `--base` 参数，权重从 Hugging Face 下载。
- **测试**：仓库包含 `tests/` 目录，可运行 `pytest` 进行单元测试，便于调试。
- **GPU 需求**：本地 LLM 推理建议使用 GPU 加速，但未明确要求。

## 核心 idea

AnnoTuneAgent 的核心方法学是**“约束生成”**：两个语言模型被训练为从给定的候选列表（marker 命中或测量统计）中**复制**一个名称，而不是自由生成，从而保证输出可验证、可审计，同时利用 LLM 的语义理解能力提高注释准确性。

## 可搬移点

- **双 LoRA 适配器共享基础模型**：该设计可被搬移到其他生物 LLM 任务中，实现多任务微调而无需多个完整模型，节省资源。
- **规则判断与仲裁逻辑**（`arbitrate.py`、`decide.py`）：可解耦为独立的决策模块，用于整合多个模型输出，提高可解释性。
- **marker 打分与验证逻辑**（`evidence.py`、`markers.py`）：可独立用于任何单细胞注释 pipeline，作为特征提取层。
- **License**：Apache-2.0，允许自由使用和修改，但需注意模型权重的许可（需确认 Hugging Face 上的具体许可）。

# AnnoTuneAgent

[![PyPI version](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/annotuneagent.svg)](https://pypi.org/project/annotuneagent/)
[![PyPI downloads](https://img.shields.io/pepy/dt/annotuneagent.svg?label=PyPI%20downloads)](https://pepy.tech/project/annotuneagent)
[![Python versions](https://img.shields.io/pypi/pyversions/annotuneagent.svg)](https://pypi.org/project/annotuneagent/)
[![Documentation Status](https://readthedocs.org/projects/annotuneagent/badge/?version=latest)](https://annotuneagent.readthedocs.io/en/latest/?badge=latest)
[![CI](https://github.com/leelieber2025/AnnoTuneAgent/actions/workflows/tests.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/leelieber2025/AnnoTuneAgent/actions/workflows/tests.yml)
[![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache--2.0-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![DOI](https://zenodo.org/badge/DOI/10.5281/zenodo.24092828.svg)](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24092828)

Documentation: [Read the Docs](https://annotuneagent.readthedocs.io/en/latest/).

**Cluster-level cell-type annotation for single-cell RNA-seq, with two
fine-tuned language models that run locally.**

Each cluster gets a marker score, a name-model result, and an ML-model
result. A rule-based judgment reads all three and writes the title, so every
call stays auditable.

## What is fine-tuned

One Qwen3.5-4B base (Q6_K GGUF) is shared by two independent LoRA adapters.
The adapters are not merged into the base, so they load together on a single
local `llama-server` and can be replaced without touching the base. If that
server was started with `--api-key`, set `ANNOTUNE_API_KEY`. The same value
is sent as a bearer token.

| Model | Task it was fine-tuned for | Input | Output |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **name** | Choose a cell-type name from the marker dictionary | Cluster marker evidence and `dictionary_hits` | A name copied from `dictionary_hits` when that type's markers support the cluster |
| **ML** | Choose a name from measured cluster statistics | Differential expression, candidate marker panels, log fold change, fraction of cells expressing each gene inside and outside the cluster, panel summaries | A name copied from those candidates |

Both models are trained to **copy** a name from the candidates they are
shown, not to free-write one. A name outside the candidate list cannot become
a title, and a name with no marker that passes expression and specificity
validation is flagged (`no_marker_passed`) instead of being trusted silently.

The weights are on the Hugging Face Hub:
[lieberlee/annotune-qwen3.5-4b-gguf](https://huggingface.co/lieberlee/annotune-qwen3.5-4b-gguf)
(preview). Inference is local: no cluster data leaves the machine.

## Pipeline

```text
raw counts ─ prepare ─▶ QC, doublets, normalization, batch correction, Leiden
           ─ run ─────▶ per cluster:
                          1. marker score        (built-in human / mouse dictionary)
                          2. name model          (LoRA, copies from dictionary_hits)
                          3. ML model            (LoRA, copies from measured candidates)
                          ▼
                        judgment ─▶ title + status + reason + hint
                          ▼
                        validated marker panels, dotplot, report, annotated h5ad
```

- **Judgment, not voting.** Agreement among the three results gives a clear
  title. Disagreement, mixed programs, and unvalidated names are kept and
  flagged with a reason (`mixed_programs`, `near_clear_cluster`,
  `subcluster_labels`, `no_marker_passed`) so you can review them.
- **Marker evidence is checked, not quoted.** Panels are selected from cited
  dictionary markers and validated against measured expression and
  specificity in your data.
- **Every title is traceable.** The report records each model's answer, the
  panel, and the reason a cluster was or was not settled.

The models run when `models` is passed (or the CLI adapter flags are given).
Without them, `run` uses the marker score alone.

## Install

Python 3.10–3.13.

```bash
pip install annotuneagent
```

Local GGUF models need `pip install 'annotuneagent[models]'`, which installs
the tokenizer stack (`transformers` and `jinja2`). Optional methods:
AmbiDose (`denoise=True`, [install](https://github.com/leelieber2025/AmbiDose)),
scVI and SOLO (`annotuneagent[scvi]`), scFair (`annotuneagent[scfair]`),
Harmony, and Scanorama. If you select one that is missing, `prepare` prints
the install command and leaves the matrix unchanged. See
[Installation](docs/installation.md).

From a checkout:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/leelieber2025/AnnoTuneAgent.git
cd AnnoTuneAgent
pip install -e ".[dev]"
```

## First run

`prepare` expects raw integer counts. `run` expects finite, nonnegative,
library-size-normalized natural log1p expression with Scanpy's
`adata.uns["log1p"]`, which `prepare` writes.

```python
import annotuneagent as ata

adata = ata.read_10x("outs", ["sample_a", "sample_b"])
adata = ata.prepare(adata, species="human", batch_key="sample")
report = ata.run(adata, "leiden", species="human", subcluster=False)
```

`read_10x` takes one filtered matrix per sample folder (`*.h5`, or the mtx
directory when there is no h5). Scrublet and SOLO run per sample on those
filtered counts. `doublet_chip="10k"` (default) uses 0.8% multiplets per
1,000 recovered cells, and `"20k"` uses 0.4%.

`geo_info("GSE341410")` lists the samples in a GEO series. `read_geo` then
downloads the ones you name. `groups` sets `obs["group"]`. Characteristics
such as day and treatment are stored on `obs`, and `obs={...}` adds columns
the record does not name.
[docs/tutorials/gse266598_annotation.ipynb](docs/tutorials/gse266598_annotation.ipynb)
follows one series from the GEO page through annotation.

To score a caller-supplied list instead of the built-in dictionary:

```python
records = ata.annotate(
    adata,
    cluster_key="leiden",
    hypotheses=[
        ata.Hypothesis(
            "CD4-positive, alpha-beta T cell",
            positive=("CD3E", "CD4"),
            negative=("CD8A",),
        ),
        ata.Hypothesis(
            "CD8-positive, alpha-beta T cell",
            positive=("CD3E", "CD8A"),
            negative=("CD4",),
        ),
    ],
)
```

A label needs positive marker enrichment. A negative marker counts against a
hypothesis only when the cluster is enriched for it relative to the other
cells. Scores are operational, not probabilities.

The built-in table is `markers.tsv`: human and mouse, each with a
tissue-agnostic core and organ pages. Tissue rows stay hidden until `tissue`
matches. Symbols are not translated across species. `evaluate` compares
records with a per-cell author label: the reference for a cluster is the
majority label, a tied majority is left unmatched, and a parent name counts
as a coarse match.

```bash
annotuneagent \
  --input clustered.h5ad \
  --cluster-key leiden \
  --species human \
  --output result.json
```

`--name-adapter`, `--ml-adapter`, and `--base` run the name and ML models on
one local server and require `--output-h5ad`. The weights are on the Hugging
Face Hub: [lieberlee/annotune-qwen3.5-4b-gguf](https://huggingface.co/lieberlee/annotune-qwen3.5-4b-gguf).
The tokenizer is installed with the package. See
[docs/tutorials/load_model.ipynb](docs/tutorials/load_model.ipynb).

## Status

**0.1.5 (Alpha).** Import as `import annotuneagent as ata`.

## Citation

For the software record, cite the [Zenodo DOI](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24092828).
Pin the package version used in the analysis, for example `annotuneagent==0.1.5`.

## License

Software: [Apache License 2.0](LICENSE).

## Author

**Zhao Li (李钊)**
Email: [leelieber@gmail.com](mailto:leelieber@gmail.com)

## 是什么
SEMPER 是一个多模态蛋白质表示学习框架，用于生成人类大脑 442 种细胞类型中每个蛋白质的细胞类型特异性嵌入。它通过对比学习将蛋白质语言模型（ESM-C 600M）的序列表示与基于蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用（PPI）网络的图 Transformer 表示对齐，从而捕捉蛋白质在不同细胞类型中的上下文功能。

## 亮点
- **多模态对齐**：将序列信息（蛋白质语言模型）与网络上下文（细胞类型特异性 PPI）通过对称 InfoNCE 损失对齐，融合互补信息。
- **大规模细胞类型覆盖**：覆盖 442 种成人脑细胞类型，生成 1,256,780 个蛋白质-细胞类型表示。
- **零样本能力**：在药物靶点检索中，无需微调即可恢复临床追求的靶点，优于现有细胞类型特异性模型。
- **模块化设计**：代码分为三个独立阶段（ESM 嵌入、PPI 图 Transformer 预训练、对比对齐），便于逐步替换和扩展。
- **可复现性**：提供端到端教程和演示数据集，支持快速验证。

## 为何对本课题有用
- **虚拟细胞/虚拟器官**：SEMPER 提供了细胞类型特异性的蛋白质表示，可直接用于构建虚拟细胞模型，模拟不同细胞类型中蛋白质的功能状态。
- **单细胞/空间组学**：其方法可迁移到其他组织或物种，通过重新训练网络，将单细胞转录组或空间数据整合为蛋白质表示。
- **生物基座模型**：SEMPER 展示了如何将蛋白质语言模型与图神经网络结合，为构建多模态生物基座模型提供范式。
- **Bio Agent**：其零样本靶点检索和 LLM 辅助评估（结合 OpenAI 等）可直接用于药物靶点发现 Agent 的推理模块。

## 怎么用
- **安装**：需要 Linux、NVIDIA GPU（CUDA 11.8）、conda。克隆仓库后，创建两个环境：`semper`（主环境）和 `semper-esm`（ESM-C 嵌入）。
- **教程**：运行 `bash tutorial/run_tutorial.sh`，使用演示数据集（4 个模拟细胞类型网络）端到端训练 SEMPER，并生成论文风格的图。
- **主入口**：
  - 序列嵌入：`semper/esm/run_esm.sh`（输出 `protein_esmc_600m.pt`，形状 [N_proteins, 1152]）
  - PPI 图 Transformer：`semper/ppi_gt/run_ppi_gt.sh`（默认 4 GPU，可设 NUM_GPUS=1）
  - 对比对齐：`semper/contrastive/run_contrastive.sh`（输出 `semper_embed.pth`，形状 {cell type: [n_proteins, 512]}）
- **数据格式**：输入为 PPI 边列表（每细胞类型一个文件）、背景相互作用组 CSV、蛋白质序列 FASTA。输出为 PyTorch 张量。
- **评估**：`evaluate/` 目录包含各图表的复现脚本，需额外安装 `openai` 和 `tooluniverse` 用于 LLM 分析。

## 核心 idea
SEMPER 的核心在于通过对比学习将蛋白质序列的全局表示与细胞类型特异性 PPI 网络的局部上下文对齐，从而生成一个统一的、上下文感知的蛋白质嵌入空间，使得同一蛋白质在不同细胞类型中具有不同的表示，捕捉其功能异质性。

## 可搬移点
- **对比对齐模块**（`semper/contrastive/`）：包含 InfoNCE 损失和投影头设计，可解耦后用于其他多模态对齐任务（如基因表达与蛋白质序列）。
- **图 Transformer 预训练**（`semper/ppi_gt/`）：支持多 GPU DDP 和 GraphSAINT 采样，可迁移到其他图数据（如空间邻接图）。
- **数据预处理**（`data_prep/`）：构建细胞类型 PPI 网络的流程可复用于其他组织或物种。
- **评估脚本**（`evaluate/`）：零样本靶点检索和 LLM 评估逻辑可独立使用。
- **License**：MIT，允许自由使用和修改，但需确认是否包含第三方依赖（如 ESM、Open Targets）的许可限制。

# SEMPER: Multimodal protein representations across human brain cell types [![Project Page](https://img.shields.io/badge/Project_Page-mims--harvard-blue)](https://zitniklab.hms.harvard.edu/SEMPER/) [![Paper](https://img.shields.io/badge/Paper-bioRxiv-green)](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.11.10.765762) [![Code](https://img.shields.io/badge/Code-SEMPER-purple)](https://github.com/mims-harvard/SEMPER) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-lightgreen)](LICENSE) ## Overview The central nervous system (CNS) comprises diverse cell types whose molecular context shapes the roles of the proteins they express. Characterizing these context-specific protein functions is important for understanding cellular processes and identifying disease-relevant therapeutic targets. Protein language models and interactome- or single-cell-based models capture complementary information from protein sequences and cellular network contexts. **SEMPER** (**S**yst**E**m-scale **M**ultimodal **P**rot**E**in **R**epresentations) captures both in one model. It aligns protein language model representations with protein–protein interaction (PPI) networks from **442 cell types of the adult human brain**, giving each protein a sequence-informed representation in every cell type in which it is expressed. A frozen protein language model (ESM-C 600M) and a frozen graph transformer trained on these networks are aligned with a symmetric InfoNCE loss on two small projection heads, giving 1,256,780 protein–cell type representations of 15,487 proteins. SEMPER representations: - predict cell type-specific protein complexes, - predict genes essential to the survival of dopaminergic neurons, measured in a genome-wide CRISPR screen, - recover clinically pursued drug targets for five neurodegenerative diseases in zero-shot retrieval, at higher rates than existing cell type-specific models, and - recover more targets when combined with a large language model that reasons over protein functional annotations, with SEMPER providing experimentally derived cellular context that complements the literature-based reasoning of the large language model.

**Figure 1.** (a) SEMPER aligns a protein language model and a hybrid graph transformer over cell type-specific PPI networks through trainable adaptors (frozen encoders shown with a snowflake). (b–d) Downstream tasks: protein complex membership prediction, zero-shot target assessment, and LLM-assisted target assessment. (e) SEMPER improves target retrieval (Hits@10) over the protein language model alone across six backbones. --- ## Repository layout ``` SEMPER/ ├── semper/ # the model │ ├── esm/ # 1. ESM-C sequence embeddings │ ├── ppi_gt/ # 2. PPI graph transformer pretraining (multi-GPU DDP) │ └── contrastive/ # 3. contrastive alignment + final SEMPER representations ├── tutorial/ # end-to-end run on a small demo dataset (start here) ├── data/benchmarks/ # benchmark datasets used in the paper ├── data_prep/ # building cell type PPI networks and parsing Open Targets ├── evaluate/ # scripts behind each figure of the paper ├── img/ # figures for this README ├── environment.yml # main environment (training, evaluation) └── environment_esm.yml # ESM-C embedding environment ``` --- ## Installation **Requirements:** Linux, an NVIDIA GPU with CUDA 11.8, and conda. Tested on Rocky Linux 8.10 with NVIDIA H100 GPUs. ```bash git clone https://github.com/mims-harvard/SEMPER.git cd SEMPER conda env create -f environment.yml # about 30 minutes conda env create -f environment_esm.yml # about 15 minutes ``` SEMPER uses two environments, matching the ones used for the paper: | Environment | File | Used for | Key versions | |---|---|---|---| | `semper` | `environment.yml` | Network encoder pretraining, contrastive alignment, evaluation | Python 3.8, PyTorch 2.1.0 (CUDA 11.8), PyTorch Geometric 2.6.1 | | `semper-esm` | `environment_esm.yml` | ESM-C 600M sequence embeddings (`semper/esm/`) | Python 3.10, PyTorch 2.6.0, `esm` 3.2.1.post1 | The LLM analyses (Figs. 5–6) additionally need `openai` and `tooluniverse` and an Azure OpenAI or OpenAI API key. --- ## Tutorial For reproducibility, we provide a demo dataset and a [tutorial](tutorial) that runs the full SEMPER pipeline end to end. The demo dataset has four mock cell type networks. Each is a random 75% subset of a 500-protein neighbourhood of the Parkinson's disease targets in the public STRING interactome (v12.0, human physical interactions), so the interactions are real but the cell types are synthetic. The tutorial trains SEMPER on these networks, runs zero-shot target retrieval, and makes paper-style versions of Figs. 2a, 2b–d, 2e, 3b and 4. After installing both environments, run it from the repository root with ```bash bash tutorial/run_tutorial.sh ``` Outputs are written to `outputs/tutorial/`. The [tutorial README](tutorial/README.md) explains each step, shows the expected outputs and figures to compare against, and describes how to run SEMPER on your own networks. Because the cell types are synthetic, the demo results show that the code runs and are not comparable to the paper's results. --- ## Released benchmark datasets [`data/benchmarks/`](data/benchmarks) contains the benchmark datasets used to evaluate SEMPER in the paper. They contain no SEMPER outputs, so they can be used to benchmark any protein representation model. | Dataset | Contents | Paper | |---|---|---| | [Cell type-specific protein complexes](data/benchmarks/protein_complexes) | 547 CNS-relevant CORUM complexes and, for each of four complex definitions (transcriptional co-expression, structural connectivity, protein co-abundance, spatial colocalization), the complexes present in each brain cell type with the ten size-matched decoys per complex used for evaluation | Fig. 3, Supplementary Tables 4–5 | | [Clinically pursued targets](data/benchmarks/clinical_targets) | Targets of drugs and compounds in completed Phase 2 or in Phase 3–4 trials for Alzheimer's disease (130), Parkinson's disease (97), multiple sclerosis (166), Huntington's disease (86) and ALS (98) from the Open Targets Platform. Each target has its clinical phase, ChEMBL/DrugBank drugs, pharmacological action and curated therapeutic intent | Figs. 4–6, Supplementary Table 6 | | [Dopaminergic neuron essential genes](data/benchmarks/da_neuron_essential_genes) | 693 genes essential to the survival of human iPSC-derived midbrain dopaminergic neurons, from a genome-wide CRISPR/Cas9 screen (Nazeen et al., 2026) | Fig. 5 | See the [dataset README](data/benchmarks/README.md) for column descriptions and sources. --- ## Training SEMPER Steps 1 and 2 are independent. Step 3 needs the outputs of both. All scripts run from any directory and read and write paths relative to the repository root. Each path can be overridden with an environment variable, as shown in [`tutorial/run_tutorial.sh`](tutorial/run_tutorial.sh). **Inputs** (place under `data/`, or point the scripts at them): - `human_background.csv`, the cell type-agnostic interactome ([TransposeNet](https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.33717070)) - `networks/ppi_edgelists/_edgelist.txt`, one PPI network per cell type - `networks/mg_edgelist.txt`, the metagraph linking cell types, superclusters, brain structures and regions - `protein_sequences.fasta`, protein sequences, which can be fetched with [`semper/esm/fetch_sequences.py`](semper/esm/fetch_sequences.py) The 442 brain cell type networks are built with [`data_prep/construct_ppi_networks/`](data_prep/construct_ppi_networks). ### 1 · Sequence embeddings (ESM-C 600M, frozen) ```bash bash semper/esm/run_esm.sh ``` Writes `outputs/esm/protein_esmc_600m.pt` (`[N_proteins, 1152]`, mean-pooled over residues) and `protein_esmc_600m.pkl` (protein ID → row). ### 2 · PPI graph transformer ```bash bash semper/ppi_gt/run_ppi_gt.sh # 4 GPUs by default; NUM_GPUS=1 for one GPU ``` Trains the multi-scale graph transformer with link prediction and center loss for 300 epochs using GraphSAINT mini-batches and DistributedDataParallel. It writes `outputs/ppi_gt/_protein_embed.pth` (`{cell type → [n_proteins, 64]}`), `_labels_dict.txt` and the model checkpoint.
Arguments of semper/ppi_gt/train.py | Argument | Description | Default | |---|---|---| | `--G_f` | Background interactome CSV | — | | `--ppi_dir` | Directory of cell type edgelists | — | | `--mg_f` | Metagraph edgelist | — | | `--feat_mat` | Initial node feature dimension | `512` | | `--hidden` | Hidden dimension | `16` | | `--output` | Output dimension per head | `8` | | `--n_heads` | Attention heads | `8` | | `--batch_size` | GraphSAINT mini-batch size | `32` | | `--epochs` | Training epochs | `300` | | `--theta` | PPI vs. metagraph loss mixing coefficient | `0.1` | | `--lmbda` | Center loss weight λ | `0.01` | | `--lr` | Learning rate | `0.001` | | `--lr_cent` | Center loss learning rate | `0.01` | | `--dropout` | Dropout | `0.5` | | `--save_prefix` | Output prefix | — |
Training logs to [Weights & Biases](https://wandb.ai) when you are logged in. Set `WANDB_ENTITY` to choose the entity, or `WANDB_MODE=disabled` to turn logging off. ### 3 · Contrastive alignment and SEMPER representations ```bash bash semper/contrastive/run_contrastive.sh ``` This trains the two projection heads (sequence 1152 → 1024 → 512 → 512 and network 64 → 512 → 512 → 512) with a symmetric InfoNCE loss (τ = 0.07, batch 64, 200 epochs, Adam, learning rate 10⁻⁴). It then forms the final representation of protein *p* in cell type *c*: **z**p,c = normalize( (1 − t) · **u**p + t · **v**p,c ), t = 0.10 where **u**p is the sequence projection and **v**p,c is the cell type-specific network projection. Proteins without a sequence get the mean sequence projection. | Output (`outputs/`) | Contents | |---|---| | `semper/semper_embed.pth`, `semper_labels.txt` | **SEMPER representations** `{cell type → [n_proteins, 512]}`, used in all analyses | | `contrastive/clip_mlps.ckpt` | Projection head weights and configuration | | `contrastive/esm_projected.pth`, `ppi_projected.pth` | Aligned sequence and network projections per cell type | | `contrastive/joint_projected.pth` | Concatenation of the two (1024-d) |
Arguments of train_contrastive_MLP.py and build_semper_embeddings.py | Argument | Description | Default | |---|---|---| | `--embed_path`, `--label_path` | PPI graph transformer embeddings and labels | — | | `--esm_pickle`, `--esm_embeds` | ESM-C index and embeddings | — | | `--save_dir` | Output directory | — | | `--proj_dim` | Shared latent dimension | `512` | | `--hidden_esm` / `--hidden_ppi` | Hidden layer sizes | `1024 512` / `512 512` | | `--batch_size`, `--epochs`, `--lr` | Optimization | `64`, `200`, `1e-4` | | `--temperature` | InfoNCE temperature τ | `0.07` | | `--seed` | Random seed | `42` | | `--t` (`build_semper_embeddings.py`) | Weight on the network projection | `0.10` |
### Hardware The paper's model was trained on the [Kempner Institute](https://kempner.harvard.edu) cluster. The graph transformer used 4× NVIDIA H100 (80 GB) with DDP. ESM-C inference and contrastive alignment used one H100. The tutorial needs one GPU. --- ## Reproducing the paper's analyses [`evaluate/`](evaluate) holds the scripts behind each figure, with a README per folder: | Folder | Figure | Analysis | |---|---|---| | [`fig1e_plm_backbones/`](evaluate/fig1e_plm_backbones) | 1e | SEMPER vs. its protein language model backbone, for six backbones | | [`fig2_embedding_space/`](evaluate/fig2_embedding_space) | 2 | Cell type coherence, GO compactness, dopaminergic neuron clusters, tissue co-abundance | | [`fig3_protein_complexes/`](evaluate/fig3_protein_complexes) | 3 | Cell type-specific protein complex prediction under four complex definitions | | [`fig4_target_prioritization/`](evaluate/fig4_target_prioritization) | 4 | Zero-shot drug target retrieval for five neurodegenerative diseases | | [`fig56_llm_evaluator/`](evaluate/fig56_llm_evaluator) | 5–6 | LLM-only baseline, LLM reranking and Gene Ontology tournament | Target retrieval can be run directly on the released targets. Use [`make_seedplan.py`](evaluate/fig4_target_prioritization/make_seedplan.py) to generate seed sets, then the scripts in `run_evaluations/`; the tutorial does exactly this. The other analyses need SEMPER representations of the 442 brain cell types. These are not released (see below), so they can be run on representations trained with the code above. --- ## Code and data availability - **Code:** this repository, MIT License. - **Benchmark datasets:** [`data/benchmarks/`](data/benchmarks), see [above](#released-benchmark-datasets). - **Interactome:** TransposeNet 2 will be available at Figshare (doi:[10.6084/m9.figshare.33717070](https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.33717070)). - **Cell type networks, representations and model weights:** the 442 cell type PPI networks, the metagraph, and the SEMPER representations and model weights derived from them are not released. The weights are specific to these networks, so to apply SEMPER to another atlas, tissue or organism, retrain on your own networks with the code above. - **Project website:** https://zitniklab.hms.harvard.edu/SEMPER/ - **Preprint:** https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.11.10.765762 --- ## Citation If you use SEMPER, please cite: ```bibtex @article{dong2026semper, title = {Multimodal protein representations across human brain cell types}, author = {Dong, Amy and Li, Michelle M. and Ding, Kerr and Nazeen, Sumaiya and Noori, Ayush and Huang, Yepeng and Gao, Shanghua and Ritter, Dylan and Afroz, Jalwa and Henderson, Alexander B. H. and Studer, Lorenz and Luo, Yunan and Khurana, Vikram and Parmigiani, Giovanni and Zitnik, Marinka}, journal = {bioRxiv}, year = {2026}, doi = {10.64898/2026.11.10.765762}, url = {https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.11.10.765762} } ``` Please also cite Nazeen et al. (2025) when using the dopaminergic neuron essential genes, and the Open Targets Platform when using the target lists. --- ## License [MIT License](LICENSE) ## Acknowledgements SEMPER builds on [PINNACLE](https://github.com/mims-harvard/PINNACLE) and the [ESM](https://github.com/evolutionaryscale/esm) protein language models. We thank the Kempner Institute for computational resources.

Agentic and Transferable Panel Design
Imaging-based spatial molecular profiling with compact panels that preserve the biological signals your assay needs.

Documentation · Tutorials · Issues

--- SMITH learns a compact set of genes or molecular targets from single-cell, spatial or aligned reference data. Its multi-task objective can preserve cell identity, expression profiles, spatial organization and developmental signals; SMITH-Agent adds reference-aware workflow tools for panel design and evaluation. ## Why SMITH? Imaging-based spatial assays measure a limited number of molecular targets. Designing a useful panel therefore requires choosing which biological signals to preserve, which reference data to learn from, and how to evaluate the selected targets. | Panel-design challenge | How SMITH helps | |---|---| | A limited panel must preserve the biological differences of interest | Selects targets using objectives such as cell identity, expression reconstruction and developmental timing | | Spatial patterns matter alongside molecular profiles | Incorporates spatial coordinates and cell annotations into panel selection | | Reference data and the intended assay may come from different studies or modalities | Learns panels from related references and evaluates their performance in the target dataset | | Panel design involves multiple data sources and analysis steps | SMITH-Agent connects data inspection, reference integration, panel selection and evaluation |

## Install SMITH requires Python 3.10 or newer. ```bash git clone https://github.com/fym0503/SMITH.git cd SMITH python -m pip install --upgrade pip python -m pip install -e . ``` For notebooks and plotting, install the notebook dependencies too: ```bash python -m pip install -e '.[notebooks]' ``` ## Quick start Prepare an AnnData `.h5ad` file with targets in `adata.var_names`. For a cell-type task, include cell labels in `adata.obs['celltype']` (or `cell_type` or `subclass`). Then run: ```bash python scripts/main.py \ --adata_file data/your_reference.h5ad \ --saving_dir outputs/my_panel \ --log_dir outputs/my_panel/logs \ --tasks recon,cls \ --task_name celltype \ --panel_size 64 \ --epoch 100 \ --device cpu ``` Set `--device cuda` to train on a CUDA-enabled GPU. The run writes ranked targets and training logs under the output directories. ### Add spatial information If the AnnData object stores coordinates in `adata.obsm['spatial']`, add the spatial objective: ```bash --tasks recon,cls,coordination ``` Use `--layer counts` to train from a named AnnData layer rather than `adata.X`. ## SMITH-Agent Start an interactive session with `smith-agent`, or inspect the packaged registries: ```bash smith-agent tools smith-agent datasets smith-agent models smith-agent ``` To use configuration files from a source checkout, pass the registry explicitly: ```bash smith-cli --config configs/agent/agent.yaml tools smith-cli --config configs/agent/agent.yaml shell ``` For natural-language planning, set your OpenAI model and API key before starting the shell: ```bash export OPENAI_MODEL="your-model-id" read -r -s -p "API key: " OPENAI_API_KEY export OPENAI_API_KEY smith-agent ``` Replace `your-model-id` with the OpenAI model you want to use. Use `/help`, `/models`, `/tools` and `/status` to inspect the session. Enter `@/absolute/path/to/input.h5ad` to mount your data. Dataset registry entries need their corresponding H5AD files; probe-design tools also need their external backends and reference indexes. See [`configs/agent/`](configs/agent/) for registry entries. The shell and explicit `smith-agent run-tool` commands work without a language model. `smith-cli` is an alias for the same entry point. ## Tutorials `TF_profile`, `ribomap_profile` and `Agent_profile` configure the same SMITH implementation for their respective tasks. The CLI, Agent and notebooks share the trainer in `src/smith/train.py`. The tutorial notebooks walk through three biological settings: | Notebook | Example | |---|---| | `02_SMITH_Regulatory_Activity` | TF activity in *C. elegans* | | `03_SMITH_RIBOMap_Transfer` | Transfer from Deep-RIBOmap and STARmap into RIBOMap | | `05_SMITH_Agent_Evaluation` | Liver panel design with spatial references and MERFISH evaluation | Read the [rendered tutorials](https://smith-panel-design.readthedocs.io/en/latest/tutorials/index.html), or run the `_source.ipynb` files locally. Download the complete data bundle from [Zenodo](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24137308) (7.10 GB download; about 11.2 GB of input data). One download supplies all three tutorials, including the five TF lineage splits and five liver spatial references. From the SMITH repository root, run: ```bash python scripts/download_tutorial_data.py --data-root data/tutorials export SMITH_TUTORIAL_DATA="$PWD/data/tutorials" jupyter lab docs/source/tutorials/notebooks ``` The script verifies the archive SHA-256, extracts the inputs into `data/tutorials/`, and checks each input file. Allow about 20 GB of free disk space for the archive and extracted data, plus space for training outputs. If you already downloaded the archive, add `--archive /path/to/SMITH_tutorial_complete_20261110.tar.gz` to the download command. If you extracted it manually, set `SMITH_TUTORIAL_DATA` to the extracted `SMITH_tutorial_complete/` directory. Keep its `regulatory_activity/`, `ribomap_transfer/` and `agent/` subdirectories together. ### Tutorial execution environment The reference results use CUDA training. For the same execution mode, use Python 3.12, install `requirements-reproducibility.txt` alongside `.[notebooks]`, and set `SMITH_TUTORIAL_DEVICE=cuda:0`. Notebooks select CUDA when available and otherwise use CPU. CPU and CUDA training can produce different rankings even with the same seed. ## Reproduce paper analyses List the packaged workflows and check whether their input data are available locally: ```bash smith-repro list smith-repro check ``` Run a workflow after its required data are in place: ```bash smith-repro run 03_ribomap_transfer --data-root data/tutorials ``` Each workflow writes panels, metrics and a run manifest to its output directory. See [`reproducibility/`](reproducibility/) for workflow definitions and data requirements. ## AnnData fields | Objective | Required data | |---|---| | `recon` | Expression matrix in `adata.X`, or the layer selected with `--layer` | | `cls` | Cell labels in `adata.obs['celltype']`, `cell_type` or `subclass` | | `region` | Region labels in `adata.obs['region']` | | `pathology` | Labels in `adata.obs['pathology']` | | `coordination` | Coordinates in `adata.obsm['spatial']` | | Developmental time | Numeric time labels in the column specified by `--time_label` | Optional prior targets can be supplied with `--prior_file`, a CSV containing a `names` column that matches `adata.var_names`. ## Repository map ```text src/smith/ Core panel-selection model src/smith_agent/ Agent workflow and command-line interface configs/ Dataset, model, tool and workflow registries scripts/ Training, evaluation and data utilities docs/ Tutorials and API documentation reproducibility/ Paper workflows, manifests and reference metrics tests/ Package and workflow tests ``` ## Development Install the test dependencies and run the suite: ```bash python -m pip install -e '.[dev]' python -m pytest ``` Build the source and wheel distributions with: ```bash python -m pip install build python -m build ```

one_liner: scSet 是一个基于单细胞基础模型嵌入的集合编码器与基准测试仓库，聚焦跨队列样本表征的可迁移性，虽涉及细胞表征建模但非基座模型或Agent，且偏向基准评估而非虚拟细胞/器官建模。
card:
## 是什么

scSet 是一个**单细胞样本级表示学习**的基准测试与最小化实现仓库。它提供了一个置换不变的集合编码器（`Linear → GAT×2 → LayerNorm → 双池化 → MLP`），用于将单细胞嵌入（如 STATE 或 scGPT 的细胞嵌入）聚合为样本级（如肿瘤样本）的表示，并附带一个**预注册的 cohort-held-out 基准协议**，用于严格评估此类编码器相对于简单池化方法的真实泛化能力。其核心科学问题是：**集合编码器何时能真正超越简单的均值池化？**

## 亮点

- **极简且可复现的模型**：仅约 350 万参数，单次前向传播即可完成推理，设计非常精简（`Linear → GAT×2 → LayerNorm → 双池化 → MLP`），便于理解和复现。
- **严格的基准协议**：采用预注册的 cohort-held-out 旋转折（rotation folds），共享细胞子采样、共享探针和 cohort 级评估指标，避免了传统 in-atlas 评估带来的信息泄漏和排名虚高问题。
- **内置纯 PyTorch 的 GAT 实现**：`torch_geometric` 为可选依赖，若未安装则自动回退到语义等价的纯 PyTorch 实现，降低了环境配置门槛。
- **开箱即用的 CPU Demo**：捆绑了 36 个真实肿瘤样本（3 种癌症 × 3 个队列）的预计算嵌入，可在笔记本电脑 CPU 上约 1 分钟跑完端到端演示。
- **跨骨干网络验证**：提供了针对 scGPT 的骨干网络正交性检查脚本，验证结论在不同基础模型上的可迁移性。

## 为何对本课题有用

本仓库直接服务于**虚拟细胞/虚拟器官 × 单细胞/空间组学 × 生物基座模型**课题中的核心计算瓶颈：**如何将海量单细胞嵌入（来自基座模型如 STATE、scGPT）高效且有意义地聚合为样本级（或器官级）表示**，用于下游的分类、预后或虚拟器官建模。

- **对基座模型下游任务**：scSet 提供了一种轻量级、置换不变的集合编码器，可作为基座模型（如 scGPT、Geneformer）输出的标准聚合层，替代简单的均值池化，以捕捉细胞间相互作用和异质性。
- **对虚拟器官建模**：其 cohort-held-out 评估协议强调了跨队列泛化能力，这正是构建可迁移的虚拟器官模型所必需的——模型必须在未见过的患者/队列上表现稳定。
- **对 Bio Agent 与可解释性**：其“身份-语义二象性”发现（池化擅长身份识别，编码器擅长语义识别）为设计多任务 Bio Agent 提供了重要警示：单一目标函数可能无法同时满足身份与语义需求，需要多目标权衡。
- **方法学借鉴**：其预注册基准协议和“对比损失有毒”的结论，为任何单细胞/空间组学表示学习研究提供了严谨的评估范式和负面结果参考。

## 怎么用

- **主入口与运行命令**：
  - 快速演示：`python run_demo.py` 或 `bash run_demo.sh`（自动检查依赖并运行，约 1 分钟，CPU 即可）。
  - 完整基准：`python scripts/run_benchmark.py --cache /path/to/cell_inputs.npz --samples /path/to/samples.csv --rounds 0,1,2,3,4,5 --seeds 42,43,44 --cells 256`。
  - scGPT 骨干检查：`python scripts/embed_scgpt.py ...` 生成嵌入后，再运行 `run_benchmark.py` 和 `id_eval_backbone.py`。
- **安装与依赖**：`pip install -r requirements.txt`（核心依赖：`torch>=2.0`, `numpy`, `pandas`, `scikit-learn`, `scipy`）。`torch_geometric` 可选，未安装时自动使用内置纯 PyTorch GAT。
- **输入/输出数据格式**：
  - 输入：`cell_inputs.npz`（键为 `samples.csv` 的行索引，值为 `(n_cells × dim)` 的 float 数组，论文中使用 STATE 的 2058 维嵌入 + 12 维谱系协变量）和 `samples.csv`（需包含 `uid, cancer, cohort, sample_id` 列）。
  - 输出：`results/` 目录下的 cohort 级指标（如平衡准确率）和样本级预测，以及 `registry/folds.json`（预注册的折分配）。
- **GPU 需求**：Demo 和基准测试均可在 CPU 上运行（Demo 约 1 分钟），但完整基准（42 个队列 × 6 轮 × 3 种子）建议使用 GPU 加速以节省时间。
- **调试入口**：`run_demo.py` 是理想的断点调试入口，它捆绑了真实数据缓存，并会回退到合成缓存以保证流程可运行。`scset/model.py` 中的 `SetEncoder` 类可直接实例化并传入随机张量进行单元测试。

## 核心 idea

**核心方法学洞察**：scSet 的贡献不在于模型架构本身（GAT+池化是成熟技术），而在于**通过严格的 cohort-held-out 预注册基准协议，揭示了评估协议对模型排名的主导性影响**——即“协议决定排名”。它证明了在正确的评估协议下，一个极简的、带监督的集合编码器（仅用交叉熵损失）就能显著超越参数匹配的池化基线，而流行的对比学习目标反而有害。其可复用的方法学是：**如何设计一个公平、无泄漏、跨队列的基准，以科学地验证表示学习方法的真实泛化能力**。

## 可搬移点

- **`scset/model.py` 中的 `SetEncoder` 类**：这是最核心的可搬移模块。它实现了完整的置换不变集合编码器（含 GAT 层和双池化机制），且不依赖 `torch_geometric`（有纯 PyTorch 回退）。可直接复制或通过 `import scset.model` 引入，替换到任何需要将单细胞嵌入聚合为样本/器官级表示的自定义 Pipeline 中。
- **`benchmark/evaluate.py` 中的评估协议**：其 cohort-held-out 折生成、共享子采样和 cohort 级指标计算逻辑，可直接复用于任何跨队列泛化评估任务，确保结果的可比性和严谨性。
- **`scripts/embed_scgpt.py` 的嵌入生成流程**：展示了如何从 scGPT 模型提取细胞嵌入并缓存为 `.npz` 格式，可迁移到其他基座模型（如 Geneformer）的嵌入生成。
- **License**：MIT 许可证，允许自由使用、修改和分发，包括商业用途。可放心搬移代码，但引用论文（`@article{scset2026}`）是学术礼仪。
- **注意**：搬移时需注意模型输入维度（论文中为 2058 维 STATE 嵌入）需与你的基座模型输出维度匹配，或修改模型第一层的输入维度。
